note: S1_NAMES_EXPLANATIONS_V1: SiraatOne's explanation of the 99 Names in English, summarising named Ahl as-Sunnah scholars and authentic hadith; every quote checked against its source and independently audited. arabic_check holds the source's own Arabic words for audit.

names.summary: Allah is ar-Rahman: His mercy is vast and reaches every part of His creation, believer and disbeliever, human and animal alike.

quran.note: In al-Fatihah, recited in every prayer.
quran.arabic: الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ
quran.translation: The Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful,

quran.note: Call upon Allah or call upon ar-Rahman; to Him belong the best Names.
quran.arabic: قُلِ ادْعُوا اللَّهَ أَوِ ادْعُوا الرَّحْمَٰنَ ۖ أَيًّا مَّا تَدْعُوا فَلَهُ الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَىٰ ۚ وَلَا تَجْهَرْ بِصَلَاتِكَ وَلَا تُخَافِتْ بِهَا وَابْتَغِ بَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ سَبِيلًا
quran.translation: Say, "Call upon Allāh or call upon the Most Merciful [ar-Raḥmān]. Whichever [name] you call - to Him belong the best names." And do not recite [too] loudly in your prayer or [too] quietly but seek between that an [intermediate] way.

quran.note: Allah says His mercy encompasses all things.
quran.arabic: وَاكْتُبْ لَنَا فِي هَٰذِهِ الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ إِنَّا هُدْنَا إِلَيْكَ ۚ قَالَ عَذَابِي أُصِيبُ بِهِ مَنْ أَشَاءُ ۖ وَرَحْمَتِي وَسِعَتْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ ۚ فَسَأَكْتُبُهَا لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكَاةَ وَالَّذِينَ هُم بِآيَاتِنَا يُؤْمِنُونَ
quran.translation: And decree for us in this world [that which is] good and [also] in the Hereafter; indeed, we have turned back to You." [Allāh] said, "My punishment - I afflict with it whom I will, but My mercy encompasses all things." So I will decree it [especially] for those who fear Me and give zakāh and those who believe in Our verses-

hadith.text: When Allah created creation, He wrote in His Book, which is with Him above the Throne: "My mercy prevails over My anger."
Allah divided mercy into one hundred parts. He kept ninety-nine of them with Him and sent down one part to the earth, and it is through that one part that His creatures show mercy to one another.
The Prophet ﷺ saw a captive mother hold her baby to her chest and said: "Allah is more merciful to His servants than this woman is to her child."

scholars.text: Ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim tell us that Allah has a vast, immense mercy that covers everything and reaches every living being, and that He has written it in full for the God-fearing who follow His prophets.

Ar-Rahman points to mercy as an attribute that belongs to Allah Himself, while ar-Rahim points to that mercy reaching the ones He shows mercy to. The first describes Him; the second describes what He does.
In short, some of Allah's Names may also be used for others, while some may be used for no one but Him, such as Allah, ar-Rahman, al-Khaliq (the Creator), ar-Raziq (the Provider) and the like.
scholars.book: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, on the Basmalah (text quoted in ar-Rajihi's Sharh Tafsir Ibn Kathir, lesson 10)

scholars.text: All of creation lives by Allah's general mercy. Were it not for His mercy, no one would even eat or drink.
The special mercy that the prophets and their followers ask for is Allah guiding a person to faith, beneficial knowledge and good deeds.

notes: Allah's mercy is of two kinds: a general mercy for all creation in this life, and a special mercy for the believers that leads them to guidance and to Paradise.

Ahl as-Sunnah affirm mercy as a real attribute of Allah, befitting His majesty and unlike the mercy of His creation. Ibn al-Qayyim refuted those who called it only a figure of speech (al-Sawa'iq al-Mursalah).

lessons.text: Be merciful to others: "The merciful are shown mercy by ar-Rahman. Be merciful to those on earth, and the One above the heavens will be merciful to you."
"Whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy."

Keep hope and fear together: if the believer knew the punishment that is with Allah, no one would hope for His Paradise, and if the disbeliever knew the mercy that is with Allah, no one would lose hope of His Paradise.
Rely on Allah's mercy, not on your deeds alone: the Prophet ﷺ said that no one's deeds alone will admit him to Paradise, not even his own, unless Allah covers him with His mercy.

dua.text: O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me, give me well-being and provide for me.

names.summary: Allah is ar-Rahim: the One who actually bestows His mercy on His creatures. His mercy reaches people in this life, and He has a special, complete mercy for the believers: guidance in this world and safety and Paradise in the next.

quran.note: Ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim together in al-Fatihah.
quran.arabic: الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ
quran.translation: The Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful,

quran.note: Allah describes Himself as Rahim towards the believers.
quran.arabic: هُوَ الَّذِي يُصَلِّي عَلَيْكُمْ وَمَلَائِكَتُهُ لِيُخْرِجَكُم مِّنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى النُّورِ ۚ وَكَانَ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ رَحِيمًا
quran.translation: It is He who confers blessing upon you, and His angels [ask Him to do so] that He may bring you out from darknesses into the light. And ever is He, to the believers, Merciful.

quran.note: Ar-Rahim mentioned after a reminder of the blessings Allah gives all people.
quran.arabic: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ سَخَّرَ لَكُم مَّا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَالْفُلْكَ تَجْرِي فِي الْبَحْرِ بِأَمْرِهِ وَيُمْسِكُ السَّمَاءَ أَن تَقَعَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِالنَّاسِ لَرَءُوفٌ رَّحِيمٌ
quran.translation: Do you not see that Allāh has subjected to you whatever is on the earth and the ships which run through the sea by His command? And He restrains the sky from falling upon the earth, unless by His permission. Indeed Allāh, to the people, is Kind and Merciful.

hadith.text: In a hadith qudsi, Allah says that He has divided the prayer between Himself and His servant. When the servant says "ar-Rahman ar-Rahim", Allah says: "My servant has extolled Me."

Abu Bakr asked the Prophet ﷺ to teach him a supplication to say in his prayer. He said: "Say: O Allah, I have wronged myself greatly, and no one forgives sins except You. So forgive me with forgiveness from You and have mercy on me. You are al-Ghafur, ar-Rahim."

scholars.text: The Quran says that Allah is Rahim towards the believers, and it never says that He is Rahman towards them. So ar-Rahman is the One described by mercy, and ar-Rahim is the One who shows mercy to others by it.
His mercy to the believers in this world is that He guided them to the truth that others did not know, and showed them the way that others lost.
In the Hereafter, His mercy is that He keeps them safe from the Greatest Terror and commands His angels to meet them with the good news of winning Paradise and being saved from the Fire.
Part of His mercy and gentleness towards the believers is His salah and praise upon them, and the prayers and supplications of His angels for them.

notes: Ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim often come together. Ar-Rahman tells us that mercy is Allah's own vast attribute; ar-Rahim tells us that He actually shows that mercy to His creatures (see ar-Rahman).

Ar-Rahim has a special link with the believers (33:43), yet the Quran also says that Allah is Rahim towards people in general (22:65). The believers receive the complete mercy: guidance in this life and Paradise in the next.

lessons.text: Never despair of Allah's mercy, however many your sins. He forgives all sins for the one who turns back to Him, for He is al-Ghafur, ar-Rahim.
Do good and call on Allah with fear and hope, for His mercy is near to those who do good.
Recite al-Fatihah with a present heart: each time you say "ar-Rahman ar-Rahim", Allah answers that His servant has extolled Him.

dua.text: O Allah, I have wronged myself greatly, and no one forgives sins except You. So forgive me with forgiveness from You and have mercy on me. You are al-Ghafur, ar-Rahim.

names.summary: Allah is al-Malik: the true King who owns everything and governs it as He wills, with no one able to stop Him. Every other kingdom is given by Him and comes to an end; His kingdom never ends.

quran.note: Among the Names at the end of Surah al-Hashr.
quran.arabic: هُوَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْمَلِكُ الْقُدُّوسُ السَّلَامُ الْمُؤْمِنُ الْمُهَيْمِنُ الْعَزِيزُ الْجَبَّارُ الْمُتَكَبِّرُ ۚ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ
quran.translation: He is Allāh, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection, the Grantor of Security, the Overseer, the Exalted in Might, the Compeller, the Superior. Exalted is Allāh above whatever they associate with Him.

quran.note: Allah's kingship is described as the true kingship.
quran.arabic: فَتَعَالَى اللَّهُ الْمَلِكُ الْحَقُّ ۗ وَلَا تَعْجَلْ بِالْقُرْآنِ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُقْضَىٰ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُ ۖ وَقُل رَّبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْمًا
quran.translation: So high [above all] is Allāh, the Sovereign, the Truth. And, [O Muḥammad], do not hasten with [recitation of] the Qur’ān before its revelation is completed to you, and say, "My Lord, increase me in knowledge."

quran.note: Surah an-Nas: Allah is the King of all people.
quran.arabic: مَلِكِ النَّاسِ
quran.translation: The Sovereign of mankind,

quran.note: On the Day of Judgment, all kingship is shown to belong to Allah alone.
quran.arabic: يَوْمَ هُم بَارِزُونَ ۖ لَا يَخْفَىٰ عَلَى اللَّهِ مِنْهُمْ شَيْءٌ ۚ لِّمَنِ الْمُلْكُ الْيَوْمَ ۖ لِلَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ
quran.translation: The Day they come forth nothing concerning them will be concealed from Allāh. To whom belongs [all] sovereignty this Day? To Allāh, the One, the Prevailing.

hadith.text: On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will grip the earth and fold up the heavens in His Right Hand, then He will say: "I am the King. Where are the kings of the earth?"

Every night, when the first third of the night has passed, Allah descends to the lowest heaven and says: "I am the King, I am the King. Who is calling on Me, so that I may answer him? Who is asking Me, so that I may give him? Who is seeking My forgiveness, so that I may forgive him?" He continues like this until dawn breaks.
The Prophet ﷺ said that the most despised name in Allah's sight is that of a man who calls himself "King of kings". One narration adds: "There is no owner except Allah."

scholars.text: Al-Malik is the Owner of all things, who disposes of them as He wills, with no one to stop Him and no one to push Him back.
He owns every dominion. The upper world and the lower world, and everyone in them, are all owned by Allah, in need of Him and under His control.
He is the One worshipped, for whom alone worship is fitting; the King above whom there is no king, and everything is beneath Him.

notes: People own a little, for a short time, by what Allah gives them. Allah's kingship is real, complete and everlasting, and on the Day of Judgment it will be plain to all (40:16).

lessons.text: Call on the King in the last part of the night, when He asks who is calling on Him so that He may answer.
Be humble, and never take titles of grandeur such as "King of kings".
Ask the true King for every good, for He alone gives power and takes it away, and all good is in His Hand.

dua.text: O Allah, You are the King, there is no god but You. You are my Lord and I am Your servant. I have wronged myself and I admit my sin, so forgive me all my sins, for no one forgives sins except You.

names.summary: Allah is al-Quddus: the Most Pure and Holy, far above every fault, defect and shortcoming, perfect in His Names and Attributes, and worthy of all honour and glorification.

quran.note: Al-Quddus comes right after al-Malik.
quran.arabic: هُوَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْمَلِكُ الْقُدُّوسُ السَّلَامُ الْمُؤْمِنُ الْمُهَيْمِنُ الْعَزِيزُ الْجَبَّارُ الْمُتَكَبِّرُ ۚ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ
quran.translation: He is Allāh, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection, the Grantor of Security, the Overseer, the Exalted in Might, the Compeller, the Superior. Exalted is Allāh above whatever they associate with Him.

quran.note: Al-Quddus at the opening of Surah al-Jumu'ah.
quran.arabic: يُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ الْمَلِكِ الْقُدُّوسِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ
quran.translation: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is exalting Allāh, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

quran.note: The angels declare Allah's holiness (a verb form from the same root).
quran.arabic: وَإِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةً ۖ قَالُوا أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفْسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسْفِكُ الدِّمَاءَ وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ ۖ قَالَ إِنِّي أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
quran.translation: And [mention, O Muḥammad], when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority." They said, "Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we exalt You with praise and declare Your perfection?" He [Allāh] said, "Indeed, I know that which you do not know."

hadith.text: Aishah reported that in his bowing and prostration the Prophet ﷺ used to say: "Subbuhun Quddus, Lord of the angels and of the Spirit."
Ubayy ibn Ka'b reported that after the closing salam of the witr prayer, the Prophet ﷺ used to say: "Subhan al-Malik al-Quddus" (Glory be to the King, the Most Holy).

scholars.text: Wahb ibn Munabbih said al-Quddus means the Pure. Mujahid and Qatadah said it means the Blessed. Ibn Jurayj said: the noble angels declare His holiness.
Al-Quddus is the One free of all shortcomings and described with the attributes of perfection.

He is the Holy One, free from every fault, defect and shortcoming, magnified and glorified. The Name al-Quddus shows that He is free of every shortcoming and that He is honoured in His attributes and His majesty.

notes: Al-Quddus has two sides: Allah is free of every flaw, and He is honoured for His perfect Attributes. Declaring Him free of faults goes together with affirming His Attributes; it never means denying an Attribute that Allah affirmed for Himself.
Al-Quddus and as-Salam are close in meaning (see as-Salam).

lessons.text: Glorify Allah in your bowing and prostration with the words the Prophet ﷺ used.
After witr, say "Subhan al-Malik al-Quddus", as the Prophet ﷺ did.
Join all of creation in glorifying Allah, for everything in the heavens and the earth glorifies al-Malik al-Quddus.

dua.text: Subbuhun Quddus, Rabbul-mala'ikati war-Ruh: Glorified and Most Holy, Lord of the angels and of the Spirit.

names.meaning: The Source of Peace, Free from All Defects
names.summary: Allah is as-Salam: perfect and free from every defect and shortcoming in His essence, His Attributes and His actions. His creation is safe from any injustice from Him, all peace comes from Him, and He invites His servants to the Home of Peace.

quran.note: As-Salam comes right after al-Quddus.
quran.arabic: هُوَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْمَلِكُ الْقُدُّوسُ السَّلَامُ الْمُؤْمِنُ الْمُهَيْمِنُ الْعَزِيزُ الْجَبَّارُ الْمُتَكَبِّرُ ۚ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ
quran.translation: He is Allāh, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection, the Grantor of Security, the Overseer, the Exalted in Might, the Compeller, the Superior. Exalted is Allāh above whatever they associate with Him.

quran.note: Allah invites people to Dar as-Salam, the Home of Peace.
quran.arabic: وَاللَّهُ يَدْعُو إِلَىٰ دَارِ السَّلَامِ وَيَهْدِي مَن يَشَاءُ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ
quran.translation: And Allāh invites to the Home of Peace [i.e., Paradise] and guides whom He wills to a straight path.

quran.note: A greeting of peace from the Lord to the people of Paradise.
quran.arabic: سَلَامٌ قَوْلًا مِّن رَّبٍّ رَّحِيمٍ
quran.translation: [And] "Peace," a word from a Merciful Lord.

hadith.text: The Companions used to say in the prayer: "Peace be upon Allah from His servants." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Do not say 'Peace be upon Allah', for Allah is as-Salam." Then he taught them the tashahhud.
When the Prophet ﷺ finished his prayer, he would ask Allah's forgiveness three times and say: "O Allah, You are as-Salam and from You comes peace. Blessed are You, Possessor of majesty and honour."

The Prophet ﷺ said: "You will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I tell you something that will make you love one another if you do it? Spread the greeting of salam among yourselves."

scholars.text: As-Salam means free from all faults and shortcomings, because He is perfect in His essence, His attributes and His actions.
He is the One whose creation is kept safe from any injustice from Him. It is one of His Names.
He is as-Salam in reality: free from any likeness to creation and from any shortcoming.
scholars.book: Al-Kafiyah ash-Shafiyah (an-Nuniyyah), p. 210 (Maktabat Ibn Taymiyyah ed.)

notes: The two explanations fit together: Allah is free of every defect, and so His creatures are safe from any injustice from Him.
This is why the Prophet ﷺ taught us not to say "Peace be upon Allah": He is as-Salam, and peace comes from Him.

lessons.text: Spread the greeting of salam: it brings love between the believers and is a path to Paradise.
Let people be safe from your tongue and your hand, for the Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.
Seek the Home of Peace by following the straight path to which Allah guides.

dua.text: O Allah, You are as-Salam and from You comes peace. Blessed are You, Possessor of majesty and honour.

names.meaning: The Giver of Security and Faith
names.summary: Allah is al-Mu'min: He confirms the truth of His messengers with clear signs, confirms the faith of His believing servants, and gives security, so that His creation is safe from any injustice from Him.

quran.note: The Name al-Mu'min among the Names at the end of Surah al-Hashr.
quran.arabic: هُوَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْمَلِكُ الْقُدُّوسُ السَّلَامُ الْمُؤْمِنُ الْمُهَيْمِنُ الْعَزِيزُ الْجَبَّارُ الْمُتَكَبِّرُ ۚ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ
quran.translation: He is Allāh, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection, the Grantor of Security, the Overseer, the Exalted in Might, the Compeller, the Superior. Exalted is Allāh above whatever they associate with Him.

quran.note: Allah gave Quraysh safety from fear (a verb form from the same root).
quran.arabic: الَّذِي أَطْعَمَهُم مِّن جُوعٍ وَآمَنَهُم مِّنْ خَوْفٍ
quran.translation: Who has fed them, [saving them] from hunger and made them safe, [saving them] from fear.

quran.note: Security is promised to those whose faith is not mixed with wrongdoing.
quran.arabic: الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَلَمْ يَلْبِسُوا إِيمَانَهُم بِظُلْمٍ أُولَٰئِكَ لَهُمُ الْأَمْنُ وَهُم مُّهْتَدُونَ
quran.translation: They who believe and do not mix their belief with injustice - those will have security, and they are [rightly] guided.

hadith.text: In a hadith qudsi, Allah says: "O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and I have made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another."

Every morning and evening the Prophet ﷺ would ask Allah for well-being and pardon in his religion, his worldly life, his family and his wealth, and say: "O Allah, cover my faults and give me safety from what I fear."

scholars.text: Al-Mu'min is the One who has made His creation safe from His wronging them.
Qatadah said: He affirms that His own word is the truth. Ibn Zayd said: He confirms His believing servants in their faith in Him.
He confirms His messengers and prophets in what they brought, through clear signs, decisive proofs and plain evidence.
Al-Mu'min is the One who keeps His creation safe from any injustice from Him.

notes: The scholars mention two meanings, and both are true of Allah: confirming the truth (of His word, His messengers and the faith of the believers), and giving security (His creation is safe from any injustice from Him).

lessons.text: Do not wrong anyone. Allah has forbidden injustice for Himself and has forbidden it between His servants.
Keep your faith pure, not mixed with wrongdoing, and Allah promises you security and guidance.
Thank Allah for the safety you live in by worshipping Him, as Quraysh were told to worship the Lord who gave them safety from fear.

dua.text: O Allah, I ask You for pardon and well-being in my religion, my worldly life, my family and my wealth. O Allah, cover my faults and give me safety from what I fear.

names.summary: Allah is al-Muhaymin: the Witness over His creation who watches over everything they do, sees what is hidden in the hearts, and encompasses all things with His knowledge.

quran.note: The Name al-Muhaymin among the Names at the end of Surah al-Hashr.
quran.arabic: هُوَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْمَلِكُ الْقُدُّوسُ السَّلَامُ الْمُؤْمِنُ الْمُهَيْمِنُ الْعَزِيزُ الْجَبَّارُ الْمُتَكَبِّرُ ۚ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ
quran.translation: He is Allāh, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection, the Grantor of Security, the Overseer, the Exalted in Might, the Compeller, the Superior. Exalted is Allāh above whatever they associate with Him.

quran.note: The same word describes the Quran in relation to the scriptures before it.
quran.arabic: وَأَنزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ بِالْحَقِّ مُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ وَمُهَيْمِنًا عَلَيْهِ ۖ فَاحْكُم بَيْنَهُم بِمَا أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ ۖ وَلَا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْوَاءَهُمْ عَمَّا جَاءَكَ مِنَ الْحَقِّ ۚ لِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنَا مِنكُمْ شِرْعَةً وَمِنْهَاجًا ۚ وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَجَعَلَكُمْ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً وَلَٰكِن لِّيَبْلُوَكُمْ فِي مَا آتَاكُمْ ۖ فَاسْتَبِقُوا الْخَيْرَاتِ ۚ إِلَى اللَّهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ جَمِيعًا فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ
quran.translation: And We have revealed to you, [O Muḥammad], the Book [i.e., the Qur’ān] in truth, confirming that which preceded it of the Scripture and as a criterion over it. So judge between them by what Allāh has revealed and do not follow their inclinations away from what has come to you of the truth. To each of you We prescribed a law and a method. Had Allāh willed, He would have made you one nation [united in religion], but [He intended] to test you in what He has given you; so race to [all that is] good. To Allāh is your return all together, and He will [then] inform you concerning that over which you used to differ.

quran.note: Allah witnesses every deed people do; nothing in the heavens or the earth escapes Him.
quran.arabic: وَمَا تَكُونُ فِي شَأْنٍ وَمَا تَتْلُو مِنْهُ مِن قُرْآنٍ وَلَا تَعْمَلُونَ مِنْ عَمَلٍ إِلَّا كُنَّا عَلَيْكُمْ شُهُودًا إِذْ تُفِيضُونَ فِيهِ ۚ وَمَا يَعْزُبُ عَن رَّبِّكَ مِن مِّثْقَالِ ذَرَّةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ وَلَا أَصْغَرَ مِن ذَٰلِكَ وَلَا أَكْبَرَ إِلَّا فِي كِتَابٍ مُّبِينٍ
quran.translation: And, [O Muḥammad], you are not [engaged] in any matter and do not recite any of the Qur’ān and you [people] do not do any deed except that We are witness over you when you are involved in it. And not absent from your Lord is any [part] of an atom's weight within the earth or within the heaven or [anything] smaller than that or greater but that it is in a clear register.

hadith.text: Jibril asked the Prophet ﷺ about ihsan. He said: "It is to worship Allah as if you see Him; and if you do not see Him, He surely sees you."
The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah does not look at your appearance or your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds."

scholars.text: Ibn Abbas and others said: al-Muhaymin is the Witness over His creation and their deeds, meaning that He watches over them.
Ibn Abbas said: al-Muhaymin is the Witness; and on another occasion he said: the Trustworthy.
He is the One who sees the hidden matters and the secrets of the hearts, who encompasses everything in His knowledge.
scholars.book: Tafsir Asma' Allah al-Husna li-s-Sa'di (his explanations collected from his works), p. 239, from his Tafsir 5/624

notes: The explanations of the scholars meet together: Allah witnesses everything, watches over it, knows what is hidden of it, and is the Trustworthy over it.

lessons.text: Worship Allah as if you see Him, knowing that He always sees you.
Take care of your heart and your deeds, for that is what Allah looks at, not your appearance or your wealth.
Remember that every deed, however small, is witnessed by Allah and recorded.

dua.text: O Allah, forgive me my mistakes, my ignorance, my going too far in my affairs, and what You know about me better than I do.

names.summary: Allah is al-'Aziz: the Almighty who is never overcome. All might belongs to Him: the might of strength, the might of overpowering all things, and the might of being beyond the reach of any creature.

quran.note: Al-'Aziz among the Names at the end of Surah al-Hashr.
quran.arabic: هُوَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْمَلِكُ الْقُدُّوسُ السَّلَامُ الْمُؤْمِنُ الْمُهَيْمِنُ الْعَزِيزُ الْجَبَّارُ الْمُتَكَبِّرُ ۚ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ
quran.translation: He is Allāh, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection, the Grantor of Security, the Overseer, the Exalted in Might, the Compeller, the Superior. Exalted is Allāh above whatever they associate with Him.

quran.note: Whoever wants honour and might should seek it from Allah, to whom it all belongs.
quran.arabic: مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ الْعِزَّةَ فَلِلَّهِ الْعِزَّةُ جَمِيعًا ۚ إِلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ الْكَلِمُ الطَّيِّبُ وَالْعَمَلُ الصَّالِحُ يَرْفَعُهُ ۚ وَالَّذِينَ يَمْكُرُونَ السَّيِّئَاتِ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ ۖ وَمَكْرُ أُولَٰئِكَ هُوَ يَبُورُ
quran.translation: Whoever desires honor [through power] - then to Allāh belongs all honor. To Him ascends good speech, and righteous work raises it. But they who plot evil deeds will have a severe punishment, and the plotting of those - it will perish.

quran.note: Might belongs to Allah, His Messenger ﷺ and the believers, not to the hypocrites.
quran.arabic: يَقُولُونَ لَئِن رَّجَعْنَا إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ لَيُخْرِجَنَّ الْأَعَزُّ مِنْهَا الْأَذَلَّ ۚ وَلِلَّهِ الْعِزَّةُ وَلِرَسُولِهِ وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَلَٰكِنَّ الْمُنَافِقِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
quran.translation: They say, "If we return to al-Madīnah, the more honored [for power] will surely expel therefrom the more humble." And to Allāh belongs [all] honor, and to His Messenger, and to the believers, but the hypocrites do not know.

quran.note: Al-'Aziz paired with ar-Rahim, repeated through Surah ash-Shu'ara'.
quran.arabic: وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ
quran.translation: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.

hadith.text: A bedouin asked the Prophet ﷺ to teach him words to say. He said: "Say: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. Allah is the Greatest, most great. Much praise be to Allah. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. There is no power and no strength except by Allah, al-'Aziz, al-Hakim."
The Prophet ﷺ said: "Charity does not decrease wealth. When a servant forgives, Allah only increases him in honour. And no one humbles himself for Allah except that Allah raises him."

scholars.text: He is the One who has overpowered everything and prevailed over all things, so no one can reach Him, because of His might.
He cannot be overcome or resisted; rather He has overpowered everything, and everything submits to Him.
All might belongs to Him: the might of strength, the might of overpowering, and the might of being beyond reach, so that no created being can ever reach Him.
scholars.book: Tafsir Asma' Allah al-Husna li-s-Sa'di (his explanations collected from his works), p. 214, from his Tafsir 5/624

scholars.text: He is al-'Aziz, whose majesty is beyond anyone's reach, and al-Hakim, wise in His law and in His decree.

notes: In the Quran al-'Aziz often comes with al-Hakim (59:24) and with ar-Rahim (26:9): Allah's might goes together with His wisdom and His mercy.

lessons.text: Seek honour by obeying Allah, not by pleasing people, for all honour belongs to Him.
Forgive others and be humble: Allah increases the one who forgives in honour and raises the one who humbles himself for Him.
Seek refuge in Allah's might from being led astray.

dua.text: O Allah, to You I have submitted, in You I believe, on You I rely, to You I turn, and for You I argue. O Allah, I seek refuge in Your might, there is no god but You, from being led astray. You are the Ever-Living who does not die, while jinn and humans die.

names.summary: Allah is al-Jabbar: the Compeller whose will prevails over all creation, the Most High above His creation, and the One who mends what is broken, makes up for loss and sets right the affairs of His servants.

quran.note: The only place al-Jabbar occurs as a Name of Allah in the Quran.
quran.arabic: هُوَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْمَلِكُ الْقُدُّوسُ السَّلَامُ الْمُؤْمِنُ الْمُهَيْمِنُ الْعَزِيزُ الْجَبَّارُ الْمُتَكَبِّرُ ۚ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ
quran.translation: He is Allāh, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection, the Grantor of Security, the Overseer, the Exalted in Might, the Compeller, the Superior. Exalted is Allāh above whatever they associate with Him.

quran.note: The same word used for an arrogant tyrant among people, a quality that is blameworthy in creation.
quran.arabic: الَّذِينَ يُجَادِلُونَ فِي آيَاتِ اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ سُلْطَانٍ أَتَاهُمْ ۖ كَبُرَ مَقْتًا عِندَ اللَّهِ وَعِندَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يَطْبَعُ اللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ قَلْبِ مُتَكَبِّرٍ جَبَّارٍ
quran.translation: Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allāh without an authority having come to them - great is hatred [of them] in the sight of Allāh and in the sight of those who have believed. Thus does Allāh seal over every heart [belonging to] an arrogant tyrant.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: "On the Day of Resurrection the earth will be a single loaf of bread, which al-Jabbar will turn over with His Hand, as one of you turns over his bread on a journey, as a welcome meal for the people of Paradise."
Awf ibn Malik prayed with the Prophet ﷺ at night. In his bowing he said: "Glory be to the Possessor of might (jabarut), dominion, pride and greatness."

scholars.text: Al-Jabbar is the One who compels His creation to whatever He wills.
Al-Jabbar is the One who sets right the affairs of His creation and directs them in what is good for them.
He has overpowered all servants, and all creation has submitted to Him. He mends what is broken and makes the poor rich.

Al-Jabbar means the Most High; it means the One who subdues all; and it means the Most Kind, who mends broken hearts and sets right the weak and helpless and whoever seeks His protection and turns to Him.
scholars.book: Tafsir Asma' Allah al-Husna li-s-Sa'di (his explanations collected from his works), pp. 176-177

notes: Al-Jabbar has three meanings, all true of Allah: He mends and sets right what is broken and weak; He compels and overpowers; and He is High above His creation.
When jabbar describes a human being it means a blameworthy tyrant (40:35). Ibn Kathir explains that such might and pride befit Allah alone (see al-Mutakabbir).

lessons.text: When you are broken or in distress, call on Allah, for He answers the one in need and removes harm.
Never be a tyrant or arrogant towards people: Allah seals the heart of every arrogant tyrant.
Glorify Allah in your bowing with the words the Prophet ﷺ used, declaring His might and greatness.

dua.text: Subhana dhil-jabaruti wal-malakuti wal-kibriya'i wal-'azamah: Glory be to the Possessor of might, dominion, pride and greatness.

names.summary: Allah is al-Mutakabbir: the Supremely Great, to whom alone pride and greatness truly belong, far above every evil, fault and injustice. In Allah this greatness is perfection; in His creatures, pride is a blameworthy sin.

quran.note: The Name al-Mutakabbir among the Names at the end of Surah al-Hashr.
quran.arabic: هُوَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْمَلِكُ الْقُدُّوسُ السَّلَامُ الْمُؤْمِنُ الْمُهَيْمِنُ الْعَزِيزُ الْجَبَّارُ الْمُتَكَبِّرُ ۚ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ
quran.translation: He is Allāh, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection, the Grantor of Security, the Overseer, the Exalted in Might, the Compeller, the Superior. Exalted is Allāh above whatever they associate with Him.

quran.note: All greatness (al-kibriya') in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah.
quran.arabic: وَلَهُ الْكِبْرِيَاءُ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۖ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ
quran.translation: And to Him belongs [all] grandeur within the heavens and the earth, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

quran.note: Those who are arrogant on earth without right are turned away from Allah's signs.
quran.arabic: سَأَصْرِفُ عَنْ آيَاتِيَ الَّذِينَ يَتَكَبَّرُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ وَإِن يَرَوْا كُلَّ آيَةٍ لَّا يُؤْمِنُوا بِهَا وَإِن يَرَوْا سَبِيلَ الرُّشْدِ لَا يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلًا وَإِن يَرَوْا سَبِيلَ الْغَيِّ يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلًا ۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا وَكَانُوا عَنْهَا غَافِلِينَ
quran.translation: I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant upon the earth without right; and if they should see every sign, they will not believe in it. And if they see the way of consciousness, they will not adopt it as a way; but if they see the way of error, they will adopt it as a way. That is because they have denied Our signs and they were heedless of them.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Might is His lower garment and pride is His cloak. Allah says: Whoever contends with Me over them, I will punish him."

The Prophet ﷺ said: "No one who has an atom's weight of pride in his heart will enter Paradise." A man said that people like their clothes and shoes to be good. He said: "Allah is beautiful and loves beauty. Pride is rejecting the truth and looking down on people."

scholars.text: He is the One for whom alone compelling might is fitting, and for whom alone pride is fitting, because of His greatness.
Al-Mutakabbir: He is exalted above every evil.
He is the One to whom pride and greatness belong, far above every fault, injustice and wrongdoing.

He is the One exalted above the attributes of creation. It is also said: He is the One who shows His greatness over the rebellious among His creation when they contend with Him for greatness, and He breaks them.

notes: Pride is a perfection for Allah because it befits His greatness alone, as Ibn Kathir said. In a created being it is blameworthy, and the Quran warns the arrogant (7:146; 40:35).

lessons.text: Beware of pride: even an atom's weight of it keeps a person out of Paradise. Accept the truth and do not look down on anyone.
Humble yourself for Allah, and He will raise you.
Give greatness to Allah alone in your heart and on your tongue, for all greatness in the heavens and the earth is His.

dua.text: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. Allah is the Greatest, most great. Much praise be to Allah. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. There is no power and no strength except by Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise. O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me and provide for me.

names.summary: Allah is al-Khaliq: the Creator who determined all things by His knowledge and wisdom and brought them into being. He alone creates; everything other than Him is created.

quran.note: Al-Khaliq, al-Bari' and al-Musawwir together.
quran.arabic: هُوَ اللَّهُ الْخَالِقُ الْبَارِئُ الْمُصَوِّرُ ۖ لَهُ الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَىٰ ۚ يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۖ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ
quran.translation: He is Allāh, the Creator, the Producer, the Fashioner; to Him belong the best names. Whatever is in the heavens and earth is exalting Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

quran.note: Because He is the Creator of all things, He alone is to be worshipped.
quran.arabic: ذَٰلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ ۖ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۖ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ فَاعْبُدُوهُ ۚ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَكِيلٌ
quran.translation: That is Allāh, your Lord; there is no deity except Him, the Creator of all things, so worship Him. And He is Disposer of all things.

quran.note: There is no creator other than Allah who provides for people.
quran.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ ۚ هَلْ مِنْ خَالِقٍ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ يَرْزُقُكُم مِّنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۚ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۖ فَأَنَّىٰ تُؤْفَكُونَ
quran.translation: O mankind, remember the favor of Allāh upon you. Is there any creator other than Allāh who provides for you from the heaven and earth? There is no deity except Him, so how are you deluded?

quran.note: The intensive form al-Khallaq, joined with al-'Alim.
quran.arabic: أَوَلَيْسَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِقَادِرٍ عَلَىٰ أَن يَخْلُقَ مِثْلَهُم ۚ بَلَىٰ وَهُوَ الْخَلَّاقُ الْعَلِيمُ
quran.translation: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth Able to create the likes of them? Yes, [it is so]; and He is the Knowing Creator.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said that Allah says: "Who does greater wrong than one who sets out to create like My creating? Let them create an atom, or let them create a grain, or a grain of barley."
The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah wrote down the measures of all creatures fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth."

scholars.text: Creating (khalq) is determining (taqdir), and bar' is bringing what He determined into existence.
Al-Khaliq is the One who determines, and who turns a thing by His planning from one state into another, as in 39:6.

He is the Creator of all created things, the Originator of all that is originated, and the Fashioner of all that is shaped. These Names concern creating, planning and decreeing, and Allah alone does all of that, with no one sharing in it.

notes: The three Names of 59:24 belong together. As the scholars explain, khalq is determining a thing, bar' is bringing what was determined into existence, and taswir is giving it its particular form (see al-Bari' and al-Musawwir).

lessons.text: The One who created everything is the only One who deserves to be worshipped.
Reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth while remembering Allah, as the people of understanding do.
No one can create even an atom or a grain, so never set any created thing up as equal to the Creator.

dua.text: O Allah, You are my Lord, there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant. I hold to Your covenant and promise as much as I can. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favour upon me and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for no one forgives sins except You.

names.summary: Allah is al-Bari': the Originator who carries out what He has determined and brings it into existence from nothing. Anyone may plan, but only Allah can bring into being what He decrees.

quran.note: Al-Bari' comes between al-Khaliq and al-Musawwir.
quran.arabic: هُوَ اللَّهُ الْخَالِقُ الْبَارِئُ الْمُصَوِّرُ ۖ لَهُ الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَىٰ ۚ يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۖ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ
quran.translation: He is Allāh, the Creator, the Producer, the Fashioner; to Him belong the best names. Whatever is in the heavens and earth is exalting Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

quran.note: Musa tells his people to turn in repentance to their Bari' (the word occurs twice).
quran.arabic: وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِ يَا قَوْمِ إِنَّكُمْ ظَلَمْتُمْ أَنفُسَكُم بِاتِّخَاذِكُمُ الْعِجْلَ فَتُوبُوا إِلَىٰ بَارِئِكُمْ فَاقْتُلُوا أَنفُسَكُمْ ذَٰلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ عِندَ بَارِئِكُمْ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ ۚ إِنَّهُ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ
quran.translation: And [recall] when Moses said to his people, "O my people, indeed you have wronged yourselves by your taking of the calf [for worship]. So repent to your Creator and kill yourselves [i.e., the guilty among you]. That is best for [all of] you in the sight of your Creator." Then He accepted your repentance; indeed, He is the Accepting of Repentance, the Merciful.

quran.note: Every calamity is written in a Book before Allah brings it into being (a verb form from the same root).
quran.arabic: مَا أَصَابَ مِن مُّصِيبَةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي أَنفُسِكُمْ إِلَّا فِي كِتَابٍ مِّن قَبْلِ أَن نَّبْرَأَهَا ۚ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ
quran.translation: No disaster strikes upon the earth or among yourselves except that it is in a register before We bring it into being - indeed that, for Allāh, is easy -

hadith.text: Ali swore: "By the One who split the seed and brought the living soul into being, the unlettered Prophet ﷺ promised me that none but a believer would love me and none but a hypocrite would hate me."

scholars.text: Bar' is carrying out what He determined and decreed and bringing it into existence. Not everyone who determines and arranges a thing is able to carry it out and bring it into being; only Allah is.
Al-Bari' is the One who brings beings from non-existence into existence.
Bar' is creating a thing with a particular description. So everything that is originated (mabru') is created, but not everything created is called originated.
scholars.book: Tafsir Asma' Allah al-Husna, p. 27, quoted by alukah.net

scholars.text: This word is used especially for living beings, more than for other created things; it is rarely used for the creation of the heavens and the earth.
scholars.book: Sha'n ad-Du'a, p. 51, quoted by alukah.net

notes: The order of 59:24 follows the steps the scholars describe: Allah determines (al-Khaliq), brings what He determined into existence (al-Bari'), then gives each thing its form (al-Musawwir).
Khalq is wider than bar': az-Zajjaj noted that every originated thing is created but not the reverse, and al-Khattabi noted that the word is mostly used for living beings.

lessons.text: Whenever you sin, turn back to your Bari' in repentance, as Musa told his people.
Meet what befalls you with patience: it was written before Allah brought it into being, so do not grieve too much over what you miss or boast over what you are given.

dua.text: O Allah, You created my soul and You will take it back. Its death and its life belong to You. If You keep it alive, protect it; and if You cause it to die, forgive it.

names.summary: Allah is al-Musawwir: the Fashioner who gives every creature its own form and shape as He wills, shaping us in the wombs and giving each thing features that set it apart from all others.

quran.note: Al-Musawwir completes the three Names of creation.
quran.arabic: هُوَ اللَّهُ الْخَالِقُ الْبَارِئُ الْمُصَوِّرُ ۖ لَهُ الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَىٰ ۚ يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۖ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ
quran.translation: He is Allāh, the Creator, the Producer, the Fashioner; to Him belong the best names. Whatever is in the heavens and earth is exalting Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

quran.note: Allah shapes people in the wombs as He wills (a verb form from the same root).
quran.arabic: هُوَ الَّذِي يُصَوِّرُكُمْ فِي الْأَرْحَامِ كَيْفَ يَشَاءُ ۚ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ
quran.translation: It is He who forms you in the wombs however He wills. There is no deity except Him, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

quran.note: Allah shaped people and made their forms good (verb form).
quran.arabic: اللَّهُ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ قَرَارًا وَالسَّمَاءَ بِنَاءً وَصَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ وَرَزَقَكُم مِّنَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ ۚ ذَٰلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ ۖ فَتَبَارَكَ اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ
quran.translation: It is Allāh who made for you the earth a place of settlement and the sky a structure [i.e., ceiling] and formed you and perfected your forms and provided you with good things. That is Allāh, your Lord; then blessed is Allāh, Lord of the worlds.

quran.note: Man is reminded of how his Generous Lord created and shaped him.
quran.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الْإِنسَانُ مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ الْكَرِيمِ ۝ الَّذِي خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ ۝ فِي أَيِّ صُورَةٍ مَّا شَاءَ رَكَّبَكَ
quran.translation: O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous, Who created you, proportioned you, and balanced you? In whatever form He willed has He assembled you.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: "When forty-two nights have passed over the drop, Allah sends an angel to it, who shapes it and creates its hearing, its sight, its skin, its flesh and its bones."
The Prophet ﷺ said: "The people who will receive the severest punishment on the Day of Resurrection are those who try to imitate Allah's creation."

scholars.text: When He wills a thing, He says to it "Be", and it comes to be with the description He wants and in the form He chooses, as in 82:8.
Al-Musawwir is the One who gives created things their forms, with features by which each is distinguished from the others.

scholars.scholar: Dr. Hissah as-Saghir, quoted by IslamQA
scholars.text: Allah is al-Musawwir who shapes His creation as He wills; He gave every existing thing its own form. Al-Khaliq is general, al-Bari' is more specific, and al-Musawwir is more specific still.
scholars.book: Sharh Asma' Allah al-Husna, p. 240, quoted by IslamQA (answer 11317)

notes: Al-Khaliq, al-Bari' and al-Musawwir describe the stages of creation: determining, bringing into being, and giving form. Each Name is more specific than the one before it.

lessons.text: Thank Allah for the good form He gave you, and do not let anything deceive you about your Generous Lord.
Do not try to imitate Allah's creation, for those who do will face the severest punishment.
Remember in your prostration that Allah created and shaped your face, and gave it hearing and sight.

dua.text: O Allah, to You I have prostrated, in You I have believed, and to You I have submitted. My face has prostrated to the One who created it and shaped it, and opened its hearing and its sight. Blessed is Allah, the best of creators.

names.summary: Allah is al-Ghaffar: He forgives sins again and again, as often as His servant returns to Him in repentance, whatever the sin, and He forgives with full might and greatness.

quran.note: Allah's promise of forgiveness to whoever repents, believes, does good and stays guided.
quran.arabic: وَإِنِّي لَغَفَّارٌ لِّمَن تَابَ وَآمَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا ثُمَّ اهْتَدَىٰ
quran.translation: But indeed, I am the Perpetual Forgiver of whoever repents and believes and does righteousness and then continues in guidance.

quran.note: Nuh calls his people to seek their Lord's forgiveness.
quran.arabic: فَقُلْتُ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّهُ كَانَ غَفَّارًا
quran.translation: And said, 'Ask forgiveness of your Lord. Indeed, He is ever a Perpetual Forgiver.

quran.note: After signs of creation, the ayah ends with the Names al-'Aziz and al-Ghaffar.
quran.arabic: خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ ۖ يُكَوِّرُ اللَّيْلَ عَلَى النَّهَارِ وَيُكَوِّرُ النَّهَارَ عَلَى اللَّيْلِ ۖ وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ ۖ كُلٌّ يَجْرِي لِأَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى ۗ أَلَا هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْغَفَّارُ
quran.translation: He created the heavens and earth in truth. He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night and has subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term. Unquestionably, He is the Exalted in Might, the Perpetual Forgiver.

quran.note: The believer from Pharaoh's people calls them to al-'Aziz al-Ghaffar.
quran.arabic: تَدْعُونَنِي لِأَكْفُرَ بِاللَّهِ وَأُشْرِكَ بِهِ مَا لَيْسَ لِي بِهِ عِلْمٌ وَأَنَا أَدْعُوكُمْ إِلَى الْعَزِيزِ الْغَفَّارِ
quran.translation: You invite me to disbelieve in Allāh and associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge, and I invite you to the Exalted in Might, the Perpetual Forgiver.

quran.note: Al-Ghaffar paired with al-'Aziz and with Allah's lordship over the heavens and the earth.
quran.arabic: رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا الْعَزِيزُ الْغَفَّارُ
quran.translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Exalted in Might, the Perpetual Forgiver."

hadith.text: When the Prophet ﷺ turned over in his bed at night, he would say: "There is no god but Allah, the One, al-Qahhar, Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, al-'Aziz, al-Ghaffar."
hadith.ref: an-Nasa'i, al-Hakim and Ibn Hibban; al-Albani, Sahih al-Jami' 4693

hadith.text: A servant committed a sin and said: "My Lord, I have sinned, so forgive me." His Lord said: "Does My servant know that he has a Lord who forgives sins and holds to account for them? I have forgiven My servant." He sinned again and asked again, and it happened three times, and each time Allah forgave him.
The Prophet ﷺ said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, if you did not sin, Allah would remove you and bring a people who sin, then ask Allah for forgiveness, and He would forgive them."

scholars.text: Ghaffar means the One who forgives much and shows much mercy to the one who repents of disbelief, innovation and sin.
Allah says: whoever turns to Me in repentance, I accept his repentance, whatever sin it was.
With all His might, greatness and majesty, He forgives the one who disobeyed Him and then repented and turned back to Him.
He is al-Ghaffar even to the one who associated partners with Him after seeing His great signs, if he then repents and turns back to Him.

notes: In the Quran, al-Ghaffar comes three times with al-'Aziz (38:66, 39:5, 40:42): Allah forgives while He is the Almighty whom no one can overcome.
His forgiveness is for the one who turns back to Him. The servant in the hadith kept returning, and each time he was forgiven.

lessons.text: Ask Allah for forgiveness often: the Prophet ﷺ said that he asked Allah for forgiveness a hundred times every day.
Seeking forgiveness brings good in this life too: Nuh told his people it brings rain, wealth, children, gardens and rivers.
Never give up on Allah's forgiveness, however many times you fall. Keep turning back to Him, and He keeps forgiving.
Make your repentance real: leave the sin, believe, do good deeds and stay on guidance.

dua.text: O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I keep to Your covenant and promise as much as I can. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I admit Your favour upon me and I admit my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins except You.

names.summary: Allah is al-Qahhar: all of creation submits to His might and authority. Whatever He wills happens, nothing can resist Him, and He alone is al-Wahid al-Qahhar, with no partner in anything.

quran.note: Yusuf asks his prison companions: many scattered lords, or Allah, al-Wahid al-Qahhar?
quran.arabic: يَا صَاحِبَيِ السِّجْنِ أَأَرْبَابٌ مُّتَفَرِّقُونَ خَيْرٌ أَمِ اللَّهُ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ
quran.translation: O [my] two companions of prison, are separate lords better or Allāh, the One, the Prevailing?

quran.note: The closing words of an ayah about Allah as the only Creator.
quran.arabic: قُلْ مَن رَّبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ قُلِ اللَّهُ ۚ قُلْ أَفَاتَّخَذْتُم مِّن دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَاءَ لَا يَمْلِكُونَ لِأَنفُسِهِمْ نَفْعًا وَلَا ضَرًّا ۚ قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمَىٰ وَالْبَصِيرُ أَمْ هَلْ تَسْتَوِي الظُّلُمَاتُ وَالنُّورُ ۗ أَمْ جَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكَاءَ خَلَقُوا كَخَلْقِهِ فَتَشَابَهَ الْخَلْقُ عَلَيْهِمْ ۚ قُلِ اللَّهُ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُوَ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ
quran.translation: Say, "Who is Lord of the heavens and earth?" Say, "Allāh." Say, "Have you then taken besides Him allies not possessing [even] for themselves any benefit or any harm?" Say, "Is the blind equivalent to the seeing? Or is darkness equivalent to light? Or have they attributed to Allāh partners who created like His creation so that the creation [of each] seemed similar to them?" Say, "Allāh is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Prevailing."

quran.note: On the Day the earth is changed, all come out before al-Wahid al-Qahhar.
quran.arabic: يَوْمَ تُبَدَّلُ الْأَرْضُ غَيْرَ الْأَرْضِ وَالسَّمَاوَاتُ ۖ وَبَرَزُوا لِلَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ
quran.translation: [It will be] on the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth, and the heavens [as well], and they [i.e., all creatures] will come out before Allāh, the One, the Prevailing,

quran.note: A declaration of tawhid by the Prophet ﷺ, ending with al-Wahid al-Qahhar.
quran.arabic: قُلْ إِنَّمَا أَنَا مُنذِرٌ ۖ وَمَا مِنْ إِلَٰهٍ إِلَّا اللَّهُ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ
quran.translation: Say, [O Muḥammad], "I am only a warner, and there is not any deity except Allāh, the One, the Prevailing,

quran.note: Allah declares Himself free of taking a son: He is al-Wahid al-Qahhar.
quran.arabic: لَّوْ أَرَادَ اللَّهُ أَن يَتَّخِذَ وَلَدًا لَّاصْطَفَىٰ مِمَّا يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَاءُ ۚ سُبْحَانَهُ ۖ هُوَ اللَّهُ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ
quran.translation: If Allāh had intended to take a son, He could have chosen from what He creates whatever He willed. Exalted is He; He is Allāh, the One, the Prevailing.

quran.note: The question about dominion on the Day of Resurrection, and its answer.
quran.arabic: يَوْمَ هُم بَارِزُونَ ۖ لَا يَخْفَىٰ عَلَى اللَّهِ مِنْهُمْ شَيْءٌ ۚ لِّمَنِ الْمُلْكُ الْيَوْمَ ۖ لِلَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ
quran.translation: The Day they come forth nothing concerning them will be concealed from Allāh. To whom belongs [all] sovereignty this Day? To Allāh, the One, the Prevailing.

quran.note: Mentions the related Name al-Qahir.
quran.arabic: وَهُوَ الْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ ۚ وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ
quran.translation: And He is the subjugator over His servants. And He is the Wise, the Aware.

hadith.text: When the Prophet ﷺ turned over in his bed at night, he would say: "There is no god but Allah, the One, al-Qahhar, Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, al-'Aziz, al-Ghaffar."
hadith.ref: an-Nasa'i, al-Hakim and Ibn Hibban; al-Albani, Sahih al-Jami' 4693

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: "On the Day of Resurrection Allah will grasp the earth and fold up the heavens in His right Hand, then He will say: I am the King. Where are the kings of the earth?"

scholars.text: Al-Qahhar is the One to whose might and authority all things submit: whatever He wills happens, and whatever He does not will does not happen.
His oneness and His subduing go together: the One can only be al-Qahhar, and al-Qahhar can only be one.
He is al-Qahhar over the whole world, the upper world and the lower.
He is the One who alone has subdued everything and overpowered it.

notes: Al-Qahhar comes six times in the Quran, and every time together with al-Wahid (12:39, 13:16, 14:48, 38:65, 39:4, 40:16).
Allah also describes Himself as al-Qahir above His servants (6:18), joining His subduing with His being above His creation.

lessons.text: Worship al-Wahid al-Qahhar alone. The many gods people take are only names, with no power at all.
Do not be impressed by the power of tyrants. On the Day of Resurrection Allah will ask: Where are the kings of the earth?
Remember the Day when everyone stands before al-Wahid al-Qahhar and nothing about them is hidden from Him.

dua.text: There is no god but Allah, the One, al-Qahhar, Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, al-'Aziz, al-Ghaffar.

names.summary: Allah is al-Wahhab: the One whose gifts are vast and never stop, whose generosity reaches all of creation, and whose treasures never decrease however much He gives.

quran.note: The du'a of those firm in knowledge for steady hearts, ending with al-Wahhab.
quran.arabic: رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا وَهَبْ لَنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحْمَةً ۚ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ الْوَهَّابُ
quran.translation: [Who say], "Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower.

quran.note: The treasures of mercy belong to Allah, al-'Aziz al-Wahhab.
quran.arabic: أَمْ عِندَهُمْ خَزَائِنُ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّكَ الْعَزِيزِ الْوَهَّابِ
quran.translation: Or do they have the depositories of the mercy of your Lord, the Exalted in Might, the Bestower?

quran.note: Sulayman's du'a for forgiveness and a unique kingdom, ending with al-Wahhab.
quran.arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَهَبْ لِي مُلْكًا لَّا يَنبَغِي لِأَحَدٍ مِّن بَعْدِي ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ الْوَهَّابُ
quran.translation: He said, "My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower."

quran.note: Allah gives children as He wills: daughters, sons, both, or none.
quran.arabic: لِّلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۚ يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَاءُ ۚ يَهَبُ لِمَن يَشَاءُ إِنَاثًا وَيَهَبُ لِمَن يَشَاءُ الذُّكُورَ ۝ أَوْ يُزَوِّجُهُمْ ذُكْرَانًا وَإِنَاثًا ۖ وَيَجْعَلُ مَن يَشَاءُ عَقِيمًا ۚ إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ قَدِيرٌ
quran.translation: To Allāh belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He creates what He wills. He gives to whom He wills female [children], and He gives to whom He wills males. Or He makes them [both] males and females, and He renders whom He wills barren. Indeed, He is Knowing and Competent.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah's right Hand is full; spending does not decrease it, and it pours out gifts night and day. Do you see what He has spent since He created the heavens and the earth? It has not decreased what is in His right Hand."

In a hadith qudsi, Allah says: "O My servants, if the first and the last of you, humans and jinn, stood in one place and asked Me, and I gave each one what he asked, that would not decrease what I have, any more than a needle decreases the sea when it is dipped into it."
The Prophet ﷺ said: "When one of you makes du'a, let him not say: O Allah, forgive me if You wish. Let him ask firmly and hope for much, for nothing Allah gives is too great for Him."

scholars.text: Al-Wahhab means vast in gifts and grants, abundant in goodness, whose generosity covers all of creation.
The believers ask Him for a great mercy by which He guides them to good deeds and protects them from evil.
They ask for a mercy by which Allah makes their hearts firm, brings their affairs together, and increases their faith and certainty.
This is Allah's own bounty and mercy. It is not in people's hands, so they cannot hold it back from whom Allah wills.
Allah answered Sulayman's du'a: He forgave him, gave him back his kingdom, and added a kingdom that no one after him would have.

notes: The greatest gift of al-Wahhab is guidance and a firm heart, which is why the believers ask Him for mercy right after asking Him to keep their hearts from turning away (3:8).
Ahl as-Sunnah affirm Allah's Hands as real and befitting His majesty, unlike the hands of creation, as in the hadith of His full right Hand (Bukhari 7419) and in 5:64.

lessons.text: Ask Allah firmly and with big hopes. Nothing you ask for is too great for Him.
Ask Allah first for a steady heart and guidance, the best of all His gifts.
Remember that Allah's bounty is in His hand alone; no one can stop it from reaching whom He wills.

dua.text: O Allah, I ask You of Your bounty.

names.summary: Allah is ar-Razzaq: the One who provides abundantly and has taken on the provision of every living creature. He feeds bodies with food and drink, and nourishes the hearts of His believing servants with faith and knowledge.

quran.note: The ayah where the Name ar-Razzaq appears, joined with Allah's strength.
quran.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الرَّزَّاقُ ذُو الْقُوَّةِ الْمَتِينُ
quran.translation: Indeed, it is Allāh who is the [continual] Provider, the firm possessor of strength.

quran.note: Allah's care for the provision of every creature, and His knowledge of where it lives.
quran.arabic: وَمَا مِن دَابَّةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا عَلَى اللَّهِ رِزْقُهَا وَيَعْلَمُ مُسْتَقَرَّهَا وَمُسْتَوْدَعَهَا ۚ كُلٌّ فِي كِتَابٍ مُّبِينٍ
quran.translation: And there is no creature on earth but that upon Allāh is its provision, and He knows its place of dwelling and place of storage. All is in a clear register.

quran.note: A reminder of Allah's favour as the only Creator and Provider.
quran.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ ۚ هَلْ مِنْ خَالِقٍ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ يَرْزُقُكُم مِّنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۚ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۖ فَأَنَّىٰ تُؤْفَكُونَ
quran.translation: O mankind, remember the favor of Allāh upon you. Is there any creator other than Allāh who provides for you from the heaven and earth? There is no deity except Him, so how are you deluded?

quran.note: Ends with Allah as the best of providers, after people left the Friday sermon for trade.
quran.arabic: وَإِذَا رَأَوْا تِجَارَةً أَوْ لَهْوًا انفَضُّوا إِلَيْهَا وَتَرَكُوكَ قَائِمًا ۚ قُلْ مَا عِندَ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ مِّنَ اللَّهْوِ وَمِنَ التِّجَارَةِ ۚ وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الرَّازِقِينَ
quran.translation: But [on one occasion] when they saw a transaction or a diversion, [O Muḥammad], they rushed to it and left you standing. Say, "What is with Allāh is better than diversion and than a transaction, and Allāh is the best of providers."

hadith.text: Prices rose in Madinah, and the people asked the Prophet ﷺ to fix prices for them. He said: "Allah is the One who fixes prices, al-Qabid, al-Basit, ar-Razzaq. I hope to meet Allah with no one claiming that I wronged him in blood or wealth."

The Prophet ﷺ said that when a child is formed in the womb, Allah sends an angel who is commanded to write four things: his deeds, his provision, his lifespan, and whether he will be wretched or happy.

scholars.text: Ar-Razzaq means the One whose provision is abundant: there is no creature on earth or in the heavens except that its provision is upon Allah.
Part of His strength is that He brings His provision to the whole world.
Allah tells us that He has taken on the provision of all creatures.
Allah does not need His creation; they are the ones in need of Him in every state. He is their Creator and their Provider.

Allah's provision is of two kinds. The first is beneficial provision that carries no burden and brings the servant to the highest goals; it comes through the guidance and teaching of the Messenger ﷺ. This too is of two kinds: the provision of hearts with beneficial knowledge and sound faith, and Allah making His servant content with what is lawful instead of what is unlawful, and with His bounty instead of anyone else. The second kind is Allah bringing to all creatures, righteous and wicked, the food that nourishes them.
scholars.book: Tafsir Asma' Allah al-Husna li-s-Sa'di (his explanations collected from his works), p. 204

scholars.text: The provision by which the religion stands is knowledge and faith.
scholars.book: Sharh al-Arba'in an-Nawawiyyah, quoted by IslamQA 160556

notes: Ar-Razzaq is an intensive form: Allah's provision is abundant and never stops. The same hadith also comes with the form ar-Raziq (Abu Dawud 3451).
The best provision is the special one: faith, beneficial knowledge and lawful sustenance that helps a person in his religion.

lessons.text: Your provision was written while you were still in the womb, so put your trust in Allah for it.
Be mindful of Allah and rely on Him: He provides from where one does not expect.
Keep ties with your relatives: the Prophet ﷺ said this is a cause of wider provision and a longer life.
Do not let trade or amusement pull you away from Allah's remembrance; what is with Him is better, and He is the best of providers.

dua.text: O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me, give me well-being and provide for me.

names.summary: Allah is al-Fattah: the just Judge who decides between His servants with truth, and the One who opens the doors of His mercy. What He opens of mercy, no one can hold back.

quran.note: The Prophet ﷺ is told to speak of Allah gathering and judging between people; the only ayah with this Name.
quran.arabic: قُلْ يَجْمَعُ بَيْنَنَا رَبُّنَا ثُمَّ يَفْتَحُ بَيْنَنَا بِالْحَقِّ وَهُوَ الْفَتَّاحُ الْعَلِيمُ
quran.translation: Say, "Our Lord will bring us together; then He will judge between us in truth. And He is the Knowing Judge."

quran.note: Shu'ayb and the believers ask Allah to judge between them and their people.
quran.arabic: قَدِ افْتَرَيْنَا عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا إِنْ عُدْنَا فِي مِلَّتِكُم بَعْدَ إِذْ نَجَّانَا اللَّهُ مِنْهَا ۚ وَمَا يَكُونُ لَنَا أَن نَّعُودَ فِيهَا إِلَّا أَن يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ رَبُّنَا ۚ وَسِعَ رَبُّنَا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عِلْمًا ۚ عَلَى اللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْنَا ۚ رَبَّنَا افْتَحْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ قَوْمِنَا بِالْحَقِّ وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ الْفَاتِحِينَ
quran.translation: We would have invented against Allāh a lie if we returned to your religion after Allāh had saved us from it. And it is not for us to return to it except that Allāh, our Lord, should will. Our Lord has encompassed all things in knowledge. Upon Allāh we have relied. Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth, and You are the best of those who give decision."

quran.note: No one can hold back the mercy Allah opens for people.
quran.arabic: مَّا يَفْتَحِ اللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ مِن رَّحْمَةٍ فَلَا مُمْسِكَ لَهَا ۖ وَمَا يُمْسِكْ فَلَا مُرْسِلَ لَهُ مِن بَعْدِهِ ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ
quran.translation: Whatever Allāh grants to people of mercy - none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds - none can release it thereafter. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

quran.note: The keys of the unseen are with Allah alone.
quran.arabic: وَعِندَهُ مَفَاتِحُ الْغَيْبِ لَا يَعْلَمُهَا إِلَّا هُوَ ۚ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا فِي الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ ۚ وَمَا تَسْقُطُ مِن وَرَقَةٍ إِلَّا يَعْلَمُهَا وَلَا حَبَّةٍ فِي ظُلُمَاتِ الْأَرْضِ وَلَا رَطْبٍ وَلَا يَابِسٍ إِلَّا فِي كِتَابٍ مُّبِينٍ
quran.translation: And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. And He knows what is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls but that He knows it. And no grain is there within the darknesses of the earth and no moist or dry [thing] but that it is [written] in a clear record.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: "The keys of the unseen are five, and no one knows them except Allah: what tomorrow will bring, what happens in the wombs, when rain will come, in which land a soul will die, and when the Hour will come."
The Prophet ﷺ said: "When one of you enters the mosque, let him say: O Allah, open for me the gates of Your mercy. And when he leaves, let him say: O Allah, I ask You of Your bounty."

scholars.text: Al-Fattah al-'Alim means the just Judge who knows the true reality of all matters.
Allah's judgement between them makes clear who is truthful and who is lying, and who deserves reward and who deserves punishment, and He is the best of judges.
On Shu'ayb's du'a: judge between us and our people, and grant us victory over them.
He is the best of judges, for He is the Just One who never wrongs anyone.
Allah alone manages all affairs, giving and withholding, and this calls for the heart to depend on Allah alone in every way.

notes: Al-Fattah carries two meanings, both true of Allah: He judges between His servants with truth and justice (34:26, 7:89), and He opens the doors of His mercy for them (35:2).
The keys of the unseen are with Allah alone (6:59). No one opens them except Him.

lessons.text: When you enter the mosque, ask al-Fattah to open for you the gates of His mercy.
When you are wronged in a dispute, put your trust in Allah and ask Him to judge with truth, as Shu'ayb did.
Hope in Allah alone: no one can close what He opens, and no one can open what He holds back.

dua.text: O Allah, open for me the gates of Your mercy.

names.summary: Allah is al-'Alim: His knowledge is perfect and covers everything, the hidden and the open, what was, what is and what will be. Nothing, however small, is hidden from Him, and He knows what is in every heart.

quran.note: The angels admit they know only what Allah taught them, and praise Him as al-'Alim al-Hakim.
quran.arabic: قَالُوا سُبْحَانَكَ لَا عِلْمَ لَنَا إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمْتَنَا ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ الْعَلِيمُ الْحَكِيمُ
quran.translation: They said, "Exalted are You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, it is You who is the Knowing, the Wise."

quran.note: After the creation of the earth and the seven heavens, Allah describes His knowledge of all things.
quran.arabic: هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ لَكُم مَّا فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ اسْتَوَىٰ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ فَسَوَّاهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ ۚ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ
quran.translation: It is He who created for you all of that which is on the earth. Then He directed Himself to the heaven, [His being above all creation], and made them seven heavens, and He is Knowing of all things.

quran.note: One of the most detailed ayahs on Allah's knowledge of the unseen and the seen.
quran.arabic: وَعِندَهُ مَفَاتِحُ الْغَيْبِ لَا يَعْلَمُهَا إِلَّا هُوَ ۚ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا فِي الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ ۚ وَمَا تَسْقُطُ مِن وَرَقَةٍ إِلَّا يَعْلَمُهَا وَلَا حَبَّةٍ فِي ظُلُمَاتِ الْأَرْضِ وَلَا رَطْبٍ وَلَا يَابِسٍ إِلَّا فِي كِتَابٍ مُّبِينٍ
quran.translation: And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. And He knows what is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls but that He knows it. And no grain is there within the darknesses of the earth and no moist or dry [thing] but that it is [written] in a clear record.

quran.note: A question showing that the Creator must know what He created.
quran.arabic: أَلَا يَعْلَمُ مَنْ خَلَقَ وَهُوَ اللَّطِيفُ الْخَبِيرُ
quran.translation: Does He who created not know, while He is the Subtle, the Aware?

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever says three times in the evening: "In the name of Allah, with whose Name nothing on earth or in heaven can cause harm, and He is as-Sami', al-'Alim," no sudden affliction will strike him until morning, and whoever says it three times in the morning, none will strike him until evening.
The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah does not look at your appearance or your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds."
The Prophet ﷺ said: "The keys of the unseen are five, and no one knows them except Allah."

scholars.text: Al-'Alim is the One who knows everything, and al-Hakim is wise in His creation and His command, in teaching whom He wills and withholding from whom He wills.
The angels declared Allah far above anyone grasping anything of His knowledge except what He wills.
Allah knows every movement, even the movements of lifeless things.
This great ayah is among the clearest in detailing Allah's all-encompassing knowledge, and that it includes every unseen thing.
The ayah shows that His knowledge encompasses all things, and His Book records all events.

notes: Allah's knowledge goes together with His writing: He knows all things and has recorded them in a clear Book (6:59).
Our knowledge is only what Allah teaches us. Even the angels said they had no knowledge except what He taught them (2:32).

lessons.text: Allah knows what is in your heart, so be mindful of Him in private as you are in public.
Take care of your heart and your deeds, because that is what Allah looks at.
Be humble about your knowledge and return it to Allah, as the angels did.
Say the evening and morning remembrance that ends with as-Sami', al-'Alim.

dua.text: In the name of Allah, with whose Name nothing on earth or in heaven can cause harm, and He is as-Sami', al-'Alim. (Three times, morning and evening.)

names.summary: Allah is al-Qabid, always mentioned with al-Basit: He holds back and narrows provision for whom He wills, takes the souls when He wills, and will hold the whole earth in His grasp on the Day of Resurrection, always with perfect wisdom.
names.established_note: Al-Qabid and al-Basit come together as Names in a sahih hadith (at-Tirmidhi 1314; Abu Dawud 3451). Some scholars counted them among the Names because of it, while others held that they are not among the Beautiful Names but are only said about Allah (IslamQA 218084).

quran.note: Allah holds back and expands (the verbs of these two Names), and to Him all return.
quran.arabic: مَّن ذَا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا فَيُضَاعِفَهُ لَهُ أَضْعَافًا كَثِيرَةً ۚ وَاللَّهُ يَقْبِضُ وَيَبْسُطُ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ
quran.translation: Who is it that would loan Allāh a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over? And it is Allāh who withholds and grants abundance, and to Him you will be returned.

quran.note: Allah expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it (a related verb).
quran.arabic: اللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَن يَشَاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ ۚ وَفَرِحُوا بِالْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَمَا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا فِي الْآخِرَةِ إِلَّا مَتَاعٌ
quran.translation: Allāh extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]. And they rejoice in the worldly life, while the worldly life is not, compared to the Hereafter, except [brief] enjoyment.

quran.note: Allah takes the souls at death and in sleep, holding some and sending others back.
quran.arabic: اللَّهُ يَتَوَفَّى الْأَنفُسَ حِينَ مَوْتِهَا وَالَّتِي لَمْ تَمُتْ فِي مَنَامِهَا ۖ فَيُمْسِكُ الَّتِي قَضَىٰ عَلَيْهَا الْمَوْتَ وَيُرْسِلُ الْأُخْرَىٰ إِلَىٰ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى ۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
quran.translation: Allāh takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die [He takes] during their sleep. Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death and releases the others for a specified term. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.

quran.note: The whole earth will be in Allah's grasp on the Day of Resurrection.
quran.arabic: وَمَا قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ وَالْأَرْضُ جَمِيعًا قَبْضَتُهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَالسَّمَاوَاتُ مَطْوِيَّاتٌ بِيَمِينِهِ ۚ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَىٰ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ
quran.translation: They have not appraised Allāh with true appraisal, while the earth entirely will be [within] His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.

hadith.text: Prices rose in Madinah, and the people asked the Prophet ﷺ to fix prices for them. He said: "Allah is the One who fixes prices, al-Qabid, al-Basit, ar-Razzaq. I hope to meet Allah with no one claiming that I wronged him in blood or wealth."
On a journey the Companions slept and missed the Fajr time. When they woke after sunrise, the Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah took your souls when He willed and returned them to you when He willed."
The Prophet ﷺ said: "On the Day of Resurrection Allah will grasp the earth and fold up the heavens in His right Hand, then He will say: I am the King. Where are the kings of the earth?"

scholars.text: Al-Qabid al-Basit is the One who widens provision and narrows it.
It is good to join these two Names when mentioning Allah, one with the other, because together they speak more clearly of His power and point more clearly to His wisdom.
The proper manner with these two Names is to mention them together, because complete power is shown by mentioning both.
scholars.book: Tafsir Asma' Allah al-Husna, p. 40, quoted by IslamQA 218084

scholars.text: He narrows provision for whom He wills of His servants and widens it for others, and His is the perfect wisdom in that.
Holding back does not widen provision, and spending does not narrow it.

notes: Al-Qabid and al-Basit come together in a sahih hadith (Abu Dawud 3451; at-Tirmidhi 1314), and the Quran mentions both actions together (2:245). IslamQA notes that some scholars counted them as Names because of this hadith, while others held that they are only said about Allah; al-Khattabi and az-Zajjaj advised mentioning the two together (IslamQA 218084).
Allah's holding back is never a lack of generosity. It comes from His wisdom, and if He gave everyone wide provision, they would transgress on earth (42:27).

lessons.text: Do not let fear of poverty stop you from spending in Allah's way. Holding back does not increase provision.
Be content when your provision is narrow. Allah sends it down in measure, out of His knowledge of His servants.
Let each night's sleep remind you that Allah takes the souls, holds back some and sends back others until an appointed time.

dua.text: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things. O Allah, no one can withhold what You give, and no one can give what You withhold, and the wealth of a wealthy man cannot help him against You.

names.summary: Allah is al-Basit, mentioned together with al-Qabid: He expands provision for whom He wills and stretches out His Hand to accept the repentance of those who sin, with generosity and perfect wisdom.
names.established_note: Al-Qabid and al-Basit come together as Names in a sahih hadith (at-Tirmidhi 1314; Abu Dawud 3451). Some scholars counted them among the Names because of it, while others held that they are not among the Beautiful Names but are only said about Allah (IslamQA 218084).

quran.note: Allah holds back and expands (the verbs of these two Names), and to Him all return.
quran.arabic: مَّن ذَا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا فَيُضَاعِفَهُ لَهُ أَضْعَافًا كَثِيرَةً ۚ وَاللَّهُ يَقْبِضُ وَيَبْسُطُ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ
quran.translation: Who is it that would loan Allāh a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over? And it is Allāh who withholds and grants abundance, and to Him you will be returned.

quran.note: Allah expands and restricts provision (the verb of this Name), knowing His servants.
quran.arabic: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَن يَشَاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ ۚ إِنَّهُ كَانَ بِعِبَادِهِ خَبِيرًا بَصِيرًا
quran.translation: Indeed, your Lord extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]. Indeed He is ever, concerning His servants, Aware and Seeing.

quran.note: Allah sends provision down in measure, out of His knowledge of His servants.
quran.arabic: وَلَوْ بَسَطَ اللَّهُ الرِّزْقَ لِعِبَادِهِ لَبَغَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَٰكِن يُنَزِّلُ بِقَدَرٍ مَّا يَشَاءُ ۚ إِنَّهُ بِعِبَادِهِ خَبِيرٌ بَصِيرٌ
quran.translation: And if Allāh had extended [excessively] provision for His servants, they would have committed tyranny throughout the earth. But He sends [it] down in an amount which He wills. Indeed He is, of His servants, Aware and Seeing.

quran.note: A reply to those who claimed Allah's Hand was tied, affirming His two Hands and His giving.
quran.arabic: وَقَالَتِ الْيَهُودُ يَدُ اللَّهِ مَغْلُولَةٌ ۚ غُلَّتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَلُعِنُوا بِمَا قَالُوا ۘ بَلْ يَدَاهُ مَبْسُوطَتَانِ يُنفِقُ كَيْفَ يَشَاءُ ۚ وَلَيَزِيدَنَّ كَثِيرًا مِّنْهُم مَّا أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِن رَّبِّكَ طُغْيَانًا وَكُفْرًا ۚ وَأَلْقَيْنَا بَيْنَهُمُ الْعَدَاوَةَ وَالْبَغْضَاءَ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ ۚ كُلَّمَا أَوْقَدُوا نَارًا لِّلْحَرْبِ أَطْفَأَهَا اللَّهُ ۚ وَيَسْعَوْنَ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَسَادًا ۚ وَاللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُفْسِدِينَ
quran.translation: And the Jews say, "The hand of Allāh is chained." Chained are their hands, and cursed are they for what they say. Rather, both His hands are extended; He spends however He wills. And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. And We have cast among them animosity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. Every time they kindled the fire of war [against you], Allāh extinguished it. And they strive throughout the land [causing] corruption, and Allāh does not like corrupters.

hadith.text: Prices rose in Madinah, and the people asked the Prophet ﷺ to fix prices for them. He said: "Allah is the One who fixes prices, al-Qabid, al-Basit, ar-Razzaq. I hope to meet Allah with no one claiming that I wronged him in blood or wealth."
