The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah stretches out His Hand at night so that the one who sinned during the day may repent, and stretches out His Hand during the day so that the one who sinned at night may repent, until the sun rises from the west."
The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever would like his provision to be expanded and his life to be extended, let him keep ties with his relatives."

scholars.text: He widens provision for whom He wills and narrows it for whom He wills. All control is in His Hands, and every matter returns to Him.
Spend and do not worry, for Allah is ar-Razzaq; He narrows provision for some and widens it for others, with perfect wisdom.
Al-Qabid al-Basit is the One who widens provision and narrows it.
It is good to join these two Names when mentioning Allah, one with the other, because together they speak more clearly of His power and point more clearly to His wisdom.
The proper manner with these two Names is to mention them together, because complete power is shown by mentioning both.
scholars.book: Tafsir Asma' Allah al-Husna, p. 40, quoted by IslamQA 218084

notes: Al-Basit is mentioned together with al-Qabid, as in the sahih hadith (Abu Dawud 3451; at-Tirmidhi 1314), because the perfection is in the pair: Allah gives and holds back, both by His wisdom.

Ahl as-Sunnah affirm Allah's Hands as real and befitting His majesty, unlike the hands of creation: He stretches out His Hand to accept repentance (Muslim 2759), and the Quran affirms His two Hands outstretched (5:64). We affirm this without asking how and without likening it to anything.

lessons.text: Hurry to repent, by night or by day. Allah stretches out His Hand to accept your repentance.
Keep ties with your relatives, a cause of wider provision and a longer life.
Spend in Allah's way and trust Him; He is the One who expands and holds back, and to Him you will return.

dua.text: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things. O Allah, no one can withhold what You give, and no one can give what You withhold, and the wealth of a wealthy man cannot help him against You.

names.summary: Allah lowers whom He wills and raises whom He wills, by His justice and wisdom. He brings down the arrogant and the tyrants, and this lowering is only ever mentioned together with His raising.
names.established_note: Al-Khafid comes as a Name only in the enumeration narrations, which the hadith scholars say are not the words of the Prophet ﷺ (Ibn Taymiyyah, Majmu' al-Fatawa 6/380; IslamQA 20476). Ibn Uthaymeen did not include it among the Names, because it does not come in the Quran or the authentic Sunnah in the form of a Name, only as a verb (IslamQA 531246). The action itself is authentic (Sahih Muslim 179) and is only mentioned together with raising (IslamQA 531246).

quran.note: The Day of Resurrection lowers some people and raises others.
quran.arabic: خَافِضَةٌ رَّافِعَةٌ
quran.translation: It will bring down [some] and raise up [others].

quran.note: Allah raises the believers and the people of knowledge in rank.
quran.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا قِيلَ لَكُمْ تَفَسَّحُوا فِي الْمَجَالِسِ فَافْسَحُوا يَفْسَحِ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ ۖ وَإِذَا قِيلَ انشُزُوا فَانشُزُوا يَرْفَعِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ دَرَجَاتٍ ۚ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ
quran.translation: O you who have believed, when you are told, "Space yourselves" in assemblies, then make space; Allāh will make space for you. And when you are told, "Arise," then arise; Allāh will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge, by degrees. And Allāh is Aware of what you do.

quran.note: Allah gives honour and lowers whom He wills; all good is in His Hand.
quran.arabic: قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ مَالِكَ الْمُلْكِ تُؤْتِي الْمُلْكَ مَن تَشَاءُ وَتَنزِعُ الْمُلْكَ مِمَّن تَشَاءُ وَتُعِزُّ مَن تَشَاءُ وَتُذِلُّ مَن تَشَاءُ ۖ بِيَدِكَ الْخَيْرُ ۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
quran.translation: Say, "O Allāh, Owner of Sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty away from whom You will. You honor whom You will and You humble whom You will. In Your hand is [all] good. Indeed, You are over all things competent.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah does not sleep, and it is not fitting for Him to sleep. He lowers the scale and raises it. The deeds of the night are raised up to Him before the deeds of the day, and the deeds of the day before the deeds of the night."

The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah's Hand is full; spending does not decrease it, and it pours out gifts night and day. His Throne is over the water, and in His other Hand is the Balance: He lowers and raises."

Umar was surprised that his governor had put a freed slave in charge of Makkah. When told the man was a skilled reciter of the Quran who knew the laws of inheritance, Umar said that the Prophet ﷺ had said: "Allah raises some people by this Book and lowers others by it."

scholars.text: Al-Khafid is the One who brings down the tyrants and humbles the arrogant pharaohs.
scholars.book: Sha'n ad-Du'a, p. 58, quoted by IslamQA 20476

scholars.text: The Day of Resurrection lowers some people to the lowest of the low in Hell, though they were mighty in this world, and raises others to the highest place in lasting bliss, though they were lowly in this world. Al-Hasan, Qatadah and others said the same.
Shaykh Ibn Uthaymeen did not include al-Khafid in his list of the Beautiful Names, because it did not come in the Quran or the authentic Sunnah in the form of a Name used on its own.
scholars.book: IslamQA (answer 531246), referring to al-Qawa'id al-Muthla, p. 15

scholars.text: The scholars of hadith agree that the two narrations that list the Names (in at-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah) are not the words of the Prophet ﷺ.
Al-Mani', al-Qabid, al-Mudhill, al-Khafid and ad-Darr are not applied to Allah each on its own; each is said only together with its opposite (al-Mu'ti, al-Basit, al-Mu'izz, ar-Rafi' and an-Nafi').

notes: The meaning is true and affirmed: Allah lowers the scale and raises it (Muslim 179), and He lowers and raises with the Balance in His Hand (Bukhari 7411). It is said of Allah only together with raising, never alone.

Allah's lowering of anyone is never unjust: He lowers those who turn away from His Book and raises those who hold to it (Muslim 817). Some scholars, such as al-Khattabi, counted al-Khafid as a Name, but Ibn Uthaymeen did not (IslamQA 531246).

lessons.text: Do not be deceived by worldly rank. On the Day of Resurrection some who were mighty will be lowered, and some who were lowly will be raised.
Hold firmly to the Quran: by it Allah raises some people and lowers others.
Humble yourself for Allah, and He will raise you.

dua.text: O Allah, forgive [name] and raise his rank among those who are guided. (The Prophet ﷺ made this du'a for Abu Salamah when he died.)

names.summary: Allah raises whom He wills in rank, in this life and the next: the believers, the people of knowledge and the humble. He raised 'Isa to Himself, and good words and deeds rise up to Him. His raising often comes paired with His lowering, as in "He lowers the scale and raises it".
names.established_note: Ar-Rafi' comes as a Name only in the enumeration narrations, which the hadith scholars say are not the words of the Prophet ﷺ (Ibn Taymiyyah, Majmu' al-Fatawa 6/380, via IslamQA 163745). The Quran and authentic Sunnah affirm it as an action of Allah (3:55, 58:11; Sahih Muslim 179), and IslamQA notes that al-Khafid is only said together with ar-Rafi' (IslamQA 531246).

quran.note: Allah tells 'Isa that He will raise him up to Himself.
quran.arabic: إِذْ قَالَ اللَّهُ يَا عِيسَىٰ إِنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرَافِعُكَ إِلَيَّ وَمُطَهِّرُكَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَجَاعِلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوكَ فَوْقَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ ۖ ثُمَّ إِلَيَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَأَحْكُمُ بَيْنَكُمْ فِيمَا كُنتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ
quran.translation: [Mention] when Allāh said, "O Jesus, indeed I will take you and raise you to Myself and purify [i.e., free] you from those who disbelieve and make those who follow you [in submission to Allāh alone] superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that in which you used to differ.

quran.note: Allah raises the believers and the people of knowledge in rank.
quran.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا قِيلَ لَكُمْ تَفَسَّحُوا فِي الْمَجَالِسِ فَافْسَحُوا يَفْسَحِ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ ۖ وَإِذَا قِيلَ انشُزُوا فَانشُزُوا يَرْفَعِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ دَرَجَاتٍ ۚ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ
quran.translation: O you who have believed, when you are told, "Space yourselves" in assemblies, then make space; Allāh will make space for you. And when you are told, "Arise," then arise; Allāh will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge, by degrees. And Allāh is Aware of what you do.

quran.note: Allah raises in rank whom He wills, as He did with Ibrahim.
quran.arabic: وَتِلْكَ حُجَّتُنَا آتَيْنَاهَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَىٰ قَوْمِهِ ۚ نَرْفَعُ دَرَجَاتٍ مَّن نَّشَاءُ ۗ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ حَكِيمٌ عَلِيمٌ
quran.translation: And that was Our [conclusive] argument which We gave Abraham against his people. We raise by degrees whom We will. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing.

quran.note: Good words rise to Allah, and righteous deeds are raised.
quran.arabic: مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ الْعِزَّةَ فَلِلَّهِ الْعِزَّةُ جَمِيعًا ۚ إِلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ الْكَلِمُ الطَّيِّبُ وَالْعَمَلُ الصَّالِحُ يَرْفَعُهُ ۚ وَالَّذِينَ يَمْكُرُونَ السَّيِّئَاتِ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ ۖ وَمَكْرُ أُولَٰئِكَ هُوَ يَبُورُ
quran.translation: Whoever desires honor [through power] - then to Allāh belongs all honor. To Him ascends good speech, and righteous work raises it. But they who plot evil deeds will have a severe punishment, and the plotting of those - it will perish.

quran.note: The Day of Resurrection lowers some people and raises others.
quran.arabic: خَافِضَةٌ رَّافِعَةٌ
quran.translation: It will bring down [some] and raise up [others].

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah does not sleep, and it is not fitting for Him to sleep. He lowers the scale and raises it. The deeds of the night are raised up to Him before the deeds of the day, and the deeds of the day before the deeds of the night."

Umar was surprised that his governor had put a freed slave in charge of Makkah. When told the man was a skilled reciter of the Quran who knew the laws of inheritance, Umar said that the Prophet ﷺ had said: "Allah raises some people by this Book and lowers others by it."
The Prophet ﷺ said: "Charity does not decrease wealth. Allah only increases a servant in honour when he forgives. And no one humbles himself for Allah except that Allah raises him."

scholars.text: Allah raises the people of knowledge and faith in rank, according to the knowledge and faith He has given them.
When Allah raised al-Masih ('Isa) up to the heaven, his companions split into groups after him.
These good words and deeds are raised up to Allah, and Allah raises the one who does them and gives him honour.
The scholars of hadith agree that the two narrations that list the Names (in at-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah) are not the words of the Prophet ﷺ.

notes: Allah's raising includes raising people in rank (58:11), raising deeds up to Him (Muslim 179; 35:10) and raising 'Isa to Himself (3:55). These show that Allah is above His creation: deeds rise up to Him, and He raised 'Isa to Himself.
Lowering (al-Khafid) is only ever mentioned together with raising, because the perfection is in the pair: Allah raises by His grace and lowers by His justice.

lessons.text: Be humble for Allah's sake: no one humbles himself for Allah except that Allah raises him.
Seek knowledge together with faith, for Allah raises the believers and the people of knowledge in rank.
Let your words be good and your deeds righteous, for they rise up to Allah.

dua.text: O Allah, forgive [name] and raise his rank among those who are guided. (The Prophet ﷺ made this du'a for Abu Salamah when he died.)

names.summary: Allah gives honour to whom He wills, and all honour belongs to Him. He honours those who obey Him and lowers those who oppose Him, by His justice and wisdom. In the Quran His giving honour comes together with His lowering (3:26).
names.established_note: Al-Mu'izz comes as a Name only in the enumeration narrations, which the hadith scholars say are not the words of the Prophet ﷺ (Ibn Taymiyyah, Majmu' al-Fatawa 6/380), and Ibn Hajar and Ibn Uthaymeen did not include it in their lists (IslamQA 163745). The Quran affirms the action with a verb (3:26), where it comes together with lowering.

quran.note: Allah gives honour and lowers whom He wills (the verb form); all good is in His Hand.
quran.arabic: قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ مَالِكَ الْمُلْكِ تُؤْتِي الْمُلْكَ مَن تَشَاءُ وَتَنزِعُ الْمُلْكَ مِمَّن تَشَاءُ وَتُعِزُّ مَن تَشَاءُ وَتُذِلُّ مَن تَشَاءُ ۖ بِيَدِكَ الْخَيْرُ ۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
quran.translation: Say, "O Allāh, Owner of Sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty away from whom You will. You honor whom You will and You humble whom You will. In Your hand is [all] good. Indeed, You are over all things competent.

quran.note: Whoever wants honour should know that all honour belongs to Allah.
quran.arabic: مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ الْعِزَّةَ فَلِلَّهِ الْعِزَّةُ جَمِيعًا ۚ إِلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ الْكَلِمُ الطَّيِّبُ وَالْعَمَلُ الصَّالِحُ يَرْفَعُهُ ۚ وَالَّذِينَ يَمْكُرُونَ السَّيِّئَاتِ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ ۖ وَمَكْرُ أُولَٰئِكَ هُوَ يَبُورُ
quran.translation: Whoever desires honor [through power] - then to Allāh belongs all honor. To Him ascends good speech, and righteous work raises it. But they who plot evil deeds will have a severe punishment, and the plotting of those - it will perish.

quran.note: Honour belongs to Allah, His Messenger ﷺ and the believers.
quran.arabic: يَقُولُونَ لَئِن رَّجَعْنَا إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ لَيُخْرِجَنَّ الْأَعَزُّ مِنْهَا الْأَذَلَّ ۚ وَلِلَّهِ الْعِزَّةُ وَلِرَسُولِهِ وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَلَٰكِنَّ الْمُنَافِقِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
quran.translation: They say, "If we return to al-Madīnah, the more honored [for power] will surely expel therefrom the more humble." And to Allāh belongs [all] honor, and to His Messenger, and to the believers, but the hypocrites do not know.

quran.note: A warning to those who seek honour with the disbelievers.
quran.arabic: الَّذِينَ يَتَّخِذُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِن دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ۚ أَيَبْتَغُونَ عِندَهُمُ الْعِزَّةَ فَإِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا
quran.translation: Those who take disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do they seek with them honor [through power]? But indeed, honor belongs to Allāh entirely.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Charity does not decrease wealth. Allah only increases a servant in honour when he forgives. And no one humbles himself for Allah except that Allah raises him."
The Prophet ﷺ taught al-Hasan ibn Ali a du'a to say in the witr prayer, which includes: "The one You take as an ally is never humbled. Blessed are You, our Lord, and Exalted."

scholars.text: Allah gives honour to whom He wills through obedience to Him, and lowers whom He wills through disobedience.
You are the One who gives and the One who withholds. Whatever You will happens, and whatever You do not will does not happen.
Honour is in Allah's hand and is only gained by obeying Him.
These good words and deeds are raised up to Allah, and Allah raises the one who does them and gives him honour.
The scholars of hadith agree that the two narrations that list the Names (in at-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah) are not the words of the Prophet ﷺ.
Some of Allah's Names are only said together with another, because perfection is reached only with it, such as al-Mani' with al-Mu'ti.
scholars.book: Bada'i al-Fawa'id, as selected in al-Muntaqa min Fara'id al-Fawa'id

notes: Allah gives honour (3:26) by His grace, and the way to it is obedience to Him (35:10). In 3:26 it comes together with lowering: Allah gives honour by His grace and lowers by His justice.
Some scholars counted al-Mu'izz as a Name; IslamQA hesitates to state this firmly, while affirming the meaning (IslamQA 163745).

lessons.text: Seek honour only by obeying Allah. All honour belongs to Him.
Forgive those who wrong you: Allah only increases the one who forgives in honour.
Do not seek honour by taking the enemies of Allah as allies.

dua.text: O Allah, guide me among those You have guided, give me well-being among those You have given well-being, take me as an ally among those You have taken as allies, bless me in what You have given me, and protect me from the evil of what You have decreed. For You decree, and nothing is decreed over You, and the one You take as an ally is never humbled. Blessed are You, our Lord, and Exalted.

names.summary: Allah lowers and humbles whom He wills, and no one can honour the one He humbles. He lowers those who oppose Him and His Messenger ﷺ, by His justice, and this is always mentioned together with His giving honour.
names.established_note: Al-Mudhill comes as a Name only in the enumeration narrations, which the hadith scholars say are not the words of the Prophet ﷺ (Ibn Taymiyyah, Majmu' al-Fatawa 6/380, via IslamQA 163745). The Quran affirms the action with a verb (3:26), and the scholars say it is never said of Allah alone, only together with al-Mu'izz (IslamQA 20476).

quran.note: Allah gives honour and lowers whom He wills (the verb form); all good is in His Hand.
quran.arabic: قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ مَالِكَ الْمُلْكِ تُؤْتِي الْمُلْكَ مَن تَشَاءُ وَتَنزِعُ الْمُلْكَ مِمَّن تَشَاءُ وَتُعِزُّ مَن تَشَاءُ وَتُذِلُّ مَن تَشَاءُ ۖ بِيَدِكَ الْخَيْرُ ۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
quran.translation: Say, "O Allāh, Owner of Sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty away from whom You will. You honor whom You will and You humble whom You will. In Your hand is [all] good. Indeed, You are over all things competent.

quran.note: Allah's humbling of those who deserve punishment, which no one can undo.
quran.arabic: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُ مَن فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَن فِي الْأَرْضِ وَالشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ وَالنُّجُومُ وَالْجِبَالُ وَالشَّجَرُ وَالدَّوَابُّ وَكَثِيرٌ مِّنَ النَّاسِ ۖ وَكَثِيرٌ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ الْعَذَابُ ۗ وَمَن يُهِنِ اللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُ مِن مُّكْرِمٍ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَفْعَلُ مَا يَشَاءُ
quran.translation: Do you not see [i.e., know] that to Allāh prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth and the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, the moving creatures and many of the people? But upon many the punishment has been justified. And he whom Allāh humiliates - for him there is no bestower of honor. Indeed, Allāh does what He wills.

quran.note: The end of those who oppose Allah and His Messenger ﷺ is humiliation.
quran.arabic: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُحَادُّونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ أُولَٰئِكَ فِي الْأَذَلِّينَ
quran.translation: Indeed, the ones who oppose Allāh and His Messenger - those will be among the most humbled.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ taught al-Hasan ibn Ali a du'a to say in the witr prayer, which includes: "The one You take as an ally is never humbled. Blessed are You, our Lord, and Exalted."
The Prophet ﷺ said: "Charity does not decrease wealth. Allah only increases a servant in honour when he forgives. And no one humbles himself for Allah except that Allah raises him."
The Prophet ﷺ said: "On the Day of Resurrection Allah will grasp the earth and fold up the heavens in His right Hand, then He will say: I am the King. Where are the kings of the earth?"

scholars.text: Allah gives honour to whom He wills through obedience to Him, and lowers whom He wills through disobedience.
You are the One who gives and the One who withholds. Whatever You will happens, and whatever You do not will does not happen.
Nothing is beyond Allah; all things submit to His will and power.
The one who schemes evil only increases in disgrace and falls lower.
The scholars of hadith agree that the two narrations that list the Names (in at-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah) are not the words of the Prophet ﷺ.
Al-Mani', al-Qabid, al-Mudhill, al-Khafid and ad-Darr are not applied to Allah each on its own; each is said only together with its opposite (al-Mu'ti, al-Basit, al-Mu'izz, ar-Rafi' and an-Nafi').

notes: Allah's lowering of anyone is pure justice: He lowers those who disobey and oppose Him (58:20), and no one can raise the one He lowers (22:18).
It is never said of Allah alone, only paired with giving honour (Hafiz al-Hakami, via IslamQA 20476).

lessons.text: Fear disobedience, for opposing Allah and His Messenger ﷺ leads to humiliation.
Take Allah as your ally through obedience: the one He takes as an ally is never humbled.
Humble yourself for Allah's sake, and He will raise you.

dua.text: O Allah, guide me among those You have guided, give me well-being among those You have given well-being, take me as an ally among those You have taken as allies, bless me in what You have given me, and protect me from the evil of what You have decreed. For You decree, and nothing is decreed over You, and the one You take as an ally is never humbled. Blessed are You, our Lord, and Exalted.

names.summary: Allah is as-Sami': He hears every voice, in every language and with every need, the secret and the open alike. His hearing is a real Attribute, perfect and befitting Him, unlike the hearing of His creation.

quran.note: Allah denies that anything is like Him and affirms His hearing and sight in the same verse.
quran.arabic: فَاطِرُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۚ جَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا وَمِنَ الْأَنْعَامِ أَزْوَاجًا ۖ يَذْرَؤُكُمْ فِيهِ ۚ لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ ۖ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ
quran.translation: [He is] Creator of the heavens and the earth. He has made for you from yourselves, mates, and among the cattle, mates; He multiplies you thereby. There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing.

quran.note: Revealed about the woman who pleaded with the Prophet ﷺ about her husband; Allah heard her.
quran.arabic: قَدْ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ قَوْلَ الَّتِي تُجَادِلُكَ فِي زَوْجِهَا وَتَشْتَكِي إِلَى اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ يَسْمَعُ تَحَاوُرَكُمَا ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ
quran.translation: Certainly has Allāh heard the speech of the one who argues [i.e., pleads] with you, [O Muḥammad], concerning her husband and directs her complaint to Allāh. And Allāh hears your dialogue; indeed, Allāh is Hearing and Seeing.

quran.note: Ibrahim and Isma'il call on Allah as the All-Hearing while raising the foundations of the Ka'bah.
quran.arabic: وَإِذْ يَرْفَعُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ الْقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ وَإِسْمَاعِيلُ رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ
quran.translation: And [mention] when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House and [with him] Ishmael, [saying], "Our Lord, accept [this] from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.

hadith.text: On a journey, the Companions would call out the takbir loudly whenever they climbed high ground. The Prophet ﷺ said: "O people, be gentle with yourselves. You are not calling on One who is deaf or absent. You are calling on One who is All-Hearing, All-Seeing and near."

Abu Hurayrah recited the end of 4:58, which names Allah All-Hearing, All-Seeing, and placed his thumb on his ear and the next finger on his eye, saying he had seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite it and do this. The narrator al-Muqri explained: it means that Allah has hearing and sight. Abu Dawud said: this is a refutation of the Jahmiyyah.

scholars.text: Praise be to Allah, whose hearing takes in all voices. The woman who disputed came to the Prophet ﷺ and spoke to him while I was in a corner of the house, and I could not hear what she was saying.
scholars.book: Reported by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir 58:1 (from Ahmad, and al-Bukhari without a full chain)

scholars.text: He hears all voices, in all their different languages and with all their many different needs.
This verse and others like it are proof for the way of Ahl as-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah: affirming Allah's Attributes while denying that anything created is like Him.

notes: Ahl as-Sunnah affirm Hearing as a real Attribute of Allah, as He affirmed it for Himself. It is not explained away as mere knowledge: Allah knows all things, and He also truly hears every sound, without His hearing being like that of any creature.
Aisha, sitting in the same house, could not hear the woman, yet Allah heard every word and answered her complaint in the Quran (58:1).

lessons.text: Guard your words, even in private conversations: Allah hears secrets and whispered talk, and His angels write them down.
Call on Allah with a calm and humble voice; you are calling on One who hears and is near, not on one who is deaf or far away.
Take your hardship to Allah: He heard the woman who complained to Him about her husband and sent down an answer to her complaint.

dua.text: In the name of Allah, with whose Name nothing on earth or in the heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. (Say it three times in the morning and three times in the evening.)

names.summary: Allah is al-Basir: He sees all things, the smallest and the most hidden, in light and in darkness. Nothing escapes His sight, and His sight is a real Attribute, perfect and unlike the sight of His creation.

quran.note: Allah affirms His sight together with His hearing, right after denying any likeness to Him.
quran.arabic: فَاطِرُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۚ جَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا وَمِنَ الْأَنْعَامِ أَزْوَاجًا ۖ يَذْرَؤُكُمْ فِيهِ ۚ لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ ۖ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ
quran.translation: [He is] Creator of the heavens and the earth. He has made for you from yourselves, mates, and among the cattle, mates; He multiplies you thereby. There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing.

quran.note: Ends the command to return trusts and to judge with justice.
quran.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَن تُؤَدُّوا الْأَمَانَاتِ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهَا وَإِذَا حَكَمْتُم بَيْنَ النَّاسِ أَن تَحْكُمُوا بِالْعَدْلِ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ نِعِمَّا يَعِظُكُم بِهِ ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ سَمِيعًا بَصِيرًا
quran.translation: Indeed, Allāh commands you to render trusts to whom they are due and when you judge between people to judge with justice. Excellent is that which Allāh instructs you. Indeed, Allāh is ever Hearing and Seeing.

quran.note: The verse of the Night Journey ends with as-Sami' al-Basir.
quran.arabic: سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي أَسْرَىٰ بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلًا مِّنَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ الْأَقْصَى الَّذِي بَارَكْنَا حَوْلَهُ لِنُرِيَهُ مِنْ آيَاتِنَا ۚ إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ
quran.translation: Exalted is He who took His Servant [i.e., Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ)] by night from al-Masjid al-Ḥarām to al-Masjid al-Aqṣā, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him of Our signs. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing.

quran.note: Allah sees everything we do, wherever we are.
quran.arabic: هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ اسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا يَلِجُ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَا يَخْرُجُ مِنْهَا وَمَا يَنزِلُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ وَمَا يَعْرُجُ فِيهَا ۖ وَهُوَ مَعَكُمْ أَيْنَ مَا كُنتُمْ ۚ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ
quran.translation: It is He who created the heavens and earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne. He knows what penetrates into the earth and what emerges from it and what descends from the heaven and what ascends therein; and He is with you wherever you are. And Allāh, of what you do, is Seeing.

hadith.text: Abu Hurayrah recited the end of 4:58, which names Allah All-Hearing, All-Seeing, and placed his thumb on his ear and the next finger on his eye, saying he had seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite it and do this. The narrator al-Muqri explained: it means that Allah has hearing and sight. Abu Dawud said: this is a refutation of the Jahmiyyah.
The Prophet ﷺ said: "His veil is light. If He were to remove it, the splendour of His Face would burn all of His creation that His sight reaches."
Asked about ihsan, the Prophet ﷺ said: "It is to worship Allah as though you see Him, for even if you do not see Him, He sees you."

scholars.text: Allah is All-Hearing of everything you say and All-Seeing of everything you do.
Al-Basir sees a black ant creeping on a solid rock on a dark night, and He sees nourishment flowing through the limbs of the tiniest creatures.

In this verse there is a refutation of those who liken Allah to His creation, in its words denying any likeness to Him, and of those who deny His Attributes, in its words affirming that He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.

notes: Ahl as-Sunnah affirm Sight as a real Attribute of Allah. It is not explained away as mere knowledge: Allah sees all things with a sight that befits His majesty, and nothing is like Him (42:11).
The Prophet ﷺ pointing to his ear and eye was to confirm that Allah truly hears and sees, as the narrator al-Muqri explained, not to compare Allah's hearing and sight with ours.

lessons.text: Aim for ihsan: worship Allah as though you see Him, remembering that even if you do not see Him, He sees you.
Allah does not look at your appearance or your wealth; He looks at your hearts and your deeds, so take care of what He sees in you.
Let the knowledge that Allah sees you hold you back from wrongdoing, in public and in private.

dua.text: O Allah, let us enjoy our hearing, our sight and our strength for as long as You keep us alive.

names.summary: Allah is al-Hakam: the Judge whose judgment is final. He judges between His servants in this world and in the Hereafter with His justice and fairness, and He never wrongs anyone.
names.established_note: In the Quran it comes as "hakam" (a judge) in 6:114, and Allah is called the best and the wisest of judges; the exact Name al-Hakam is in the authentic hadith of Abu Dawud 4955.

quran.note: The Prophet ﷺ is told to declare that he seeks no judge other than Allah.
quran.arabic: أَفَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أَبْتَغِي حَكَمًا وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَنزَلَ إِلَيْكُمُ الْكِتَابَ مُفَصَّلًا ۚ وَالَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ الْكِتَابَ يَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ مُنَزَّلٌ مِّن رَّبِّكَ بِالْحَقِّ ۖ فَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُمْتَرِينَ
quran.translation: [Say], "Then is it other than Allāh I should seek as judge while it is He who has revealed to you the Book [i.e., the Qur’ān] explained in detail?" And those to whom We [previously] gave the Scripture know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth, so never be among the doubters.

quran.note: A question that affirms Allah is the wisest and most just of all judges.
quran.arabic: أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِأَحْكَمِ الْحَاكِمِينَ
quran.translation: Is not Allāh the most just of judges?

quran.note: Shu'ayb tells his people to wait patiently until Allah judges between them.
quran.arabic: وَإِن كَانَ طَائِفَةٌ مِّنكُمْ آمَنُوا بِالَّذِي أُرْسِلْتُ بِهِ وَطَائِفَةٌ لَّمْ يُؤْمِنُوا فَاصْبِرُوا حَتَّىٰ يَحْكُمَ اللَّهُ بَيْنَنَا ۚ وَهُوَ خَيْرُ الْحَاكِمِينَ
quran.translation: And if there should be a group among you who has believed in that with which I have been sent and a group that has not believed, then be patient until Allāh judges between us. And He is the best of judges."

quran.note: Yusuf tells his prison companions that all judgment belongs to Allah.
quran.arabic: مَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِهِ إِلَّا أَسْمَاءً سَمَّيْتُمُوهَا أَنتُمْ وَآبَاؤُكُم مَّا أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِن سُلْطَانٍ ۚ إِنِ الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ ۚ أَمَرَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
quran.translation: You worship not besides Him except [mere] names you have named them, you and your fathers, for which Allāh has sent down no evidence. Legislation is not but for Allāh. He has commanded that you worship not except Him. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.

hadith.text: Hani' ibn Yazid came to the Prophet ﷺ with his people, who called him Abu al-Hakam. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah is al-Hakam, and judgment belongs to Him. Why are you called Abu al-Hakam?" He said that when his people disagreed, they came to him and he judged between them, and both sides were pleased. The Prophet ﷺ said: "How good this is!" Then he asked about his eldest son, Shurayh, and said: "Then you are Abu Shurayh."

scholars.text: The Messenger ﷺ is told to declare that he will take no one but Allah as the judge he refers to, and that he binds himself to Allah's commands and prohibitions.
The only one who must be taken as judge is Allah alone, who has no partner, to whom belong the creation and the command.
Al-Hakam al-'Adl is the One who judges between His servants in this world and the Hereafter with His justice and fairness.
scholars.book: Al-Sa'di, at the end of his Tafsir, as quoted by IslamQA (answer 104488)

scholars.text: He is the wisest and most just of judges, who never acts unjustly and never wrongs anyone.

notes: The Prophet ﷺ changed the kunyah Abu al-Hakam, because al-Hakam, the Judge whose judgment is final, is Allah alone. Yet he praised the man for settling disputes fairly.

lessons.text: Refer every dispute to the judgment of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ, and accept it with a willing heart, without resentment.
Settling disputes fairly so that both sides are pleased is praised: the Prophet ﷺ said of it, "How good this is!"

dua.text: O Allah, Lord of Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, You judge between Your servants in what they used to differ over. Guide me, by Your permission, to the truth in what they have differed over, for You guide whom You will to a straight path.

names.summary: Allah is perfectly just. His words are true and just, His decree is just, and He never wrongs anyone, not even by the weight of an atom. Justice is His confirmed Attribute, though scholars differ about counting al-'Adl as a Name.
names.established_note: No verse of the Quran and no authentic hadith calls Allah "al-'Adl"; it appears only in the weak list of Names (at-Tirmidhi 3507), so Ibn Uthaymeen left it out of the 99 Names in al-Qawa'id al-Muthla, and 'Alawi as-Saqqaf says it is an Attribute, not a Name (Sifat Allah al-Waridah fi al-Kitab wa as-Sunnah). Some scholars, such as al-Sa'di, did count it, while justice itself is a confirmed Attribute of Allah.

quran.note: Allah describes His words as complete in truthfulness and justice.
quran.arabic: وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ صِدْقًا وَعَدْلًا ۚ لَّا مُبَدِّلَ لِكَلِمَاتِهِ ۚ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ
quran.translation: And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and in justice. None can alter His words, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing.

quran.note: Allah commands justice and good conduct.
quran.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُ بِالْعَدْلِ وَالْإِحْسَانِ وَإِيتَاءِ ذِي الْقُرْبَىٰ وَيَنْهَىٰ عَنِ الْفَحْشَاءِ وَالْمُنكَرِ وَالْبَغْيِ ۚ يَعِظُكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ
quran.translation: Indeed, Allāh orders justice and good conduct and giving [help] to relatives and forbids immorality and bad conduct and oppression. He admonishes you that perhaps you will be reminded.

quran.note: No one is wronged by Allah even slightly, and good deeds are multiplied.
quran.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَظْلِمُ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ ۖ وَإِن تَكُ حَسَنَةً يُضَاعِفْهَا وَيُؤْتِ مِن لَّدُنْهُ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا
quran.translation: Indeed, Allāh does not do injustice, [even] as much as an atom's weight; while if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.

quran.note: On the Day of Judgment every deed is found recorded, and no one is wronged.
quran.arabic: وَوُضِعَ الْكِتَابُ فَتَرَى الْمُجْرِمِينَ مُشْفِقِينَ مِمَّا فِيهِ وَيَقُولُونَ يَا وَيْلَتَنَا مَالِ هَٰذَا الْكِتَابِ لَا يُغَادِرُ صَغِيرَةً وَلَا كَبِيرَةً إِلَّا أَحْصَاهَا ۚ وَوَجَدُوا مَا عَمِلُوا حَاضِرًا ۗ وَلَا يَظْلِمُ رَبُّكَ أَحَدًا
quran.translation: And the record [of deeds] will be placed [open], and you will see the criminals fearful of that within it, and they will say, "Oh, woe to us! What is this book that leaves nothing small or great except that it has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present [before them]. And your Lord does injustice to no one.

hadith.text: In a hadith qudsi, Allah says: "O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself, and I have made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another."

After the Battle of Hunayn the Prophet ﷺ gave some leaders a larger share, and a man said the division was not fair. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Who will be just if Allah and His Messenger are not just? May Allah have mercy on Musa; he was hurt with more than this, and he was patient."

scholars.text: Al-'Adl has not come as a Name of Allah in the Quran, and no authentic hadith mentions it as a Name.
He gathered ninety-nine Names from the Quran and the Sunnah in his book al-Qawa'id al-Muthla, and he did not include al-'Adl among them.
scholars.book: Al-Qawa'id al-Muthla, as reported by IslamQA (answer 104488)

scholars.text: Some counted al-'Adl among the Names of Allah, but they have no evidence for it. The correct view is that it is not one of His Names; rather, it is an Attribute.
scholars.book: Sifat Allah al-Waridah fi al-Kitab wa as-Sunnah

scholars.text: He counted it with al-Hakam: Al-Hakam al-'Adl is the One who judges between His servants in this world and the Hereafter with His justice and fairness.
scholars.book: Al-Sa'di, at the end of his Tafsir, as quoted by IslamQA (answer 104488)

notes: Whether or not al-'Adl is counted as a Name, Allah's justice is certain: His commands are just, His decree is just and His recompense is just, and He has forbidden injustice for Himself.
Ibn al-Qayyim wrote in a line of verse that justice is among Allah's Attributes, in His actions, in His words and in His judgment with the Scale (quoted by IslamQA, answer 104488).

lessons.text: Never wrong anyone, for Allah has forbidden injustice for Himself and made it forbidden among His servants.
Be just even with people you dislike; justice is closer to taqwa.
Trust Allah's decree and His reckoning: every deed is recorded, and no one will be wronged in the least.

names.summary: Allah is al-Latif: His knowledge reaches the finest and most hidden things, and He is gentle with His servants, bringing goodness and kindness to them by ways they do not even notice.

quran.note: Ends the verse about Allah encompassing all vision while no vision encompasses Him.
quran.arabic: لَّا تُدْرِكُهُ الْأَبْصَارُ وَهُوَ يُدْرِكُ الْأَبْصَارَ ۖ وَهُوَ اللَّطِيفُ الْخَبِيرُ
quran.translation: Vision perceives Him not, but He perceives [all] vision; and He is the Subtle, the Aware.

quran.note: The Creator knows fully what He has created.
quran.arabic: أَلَا يَعْلَمُ مَنْ خَلَقَ وَهُوَ اللَّطِيفُ الْخَبِيرُ
quran.translation: Does He who created not know, while He is the Subtle, the Aware?

quran.note: Allah's gentle kindness to His servants and His provision for them.
quran.arabic: اللَّهُ لَطِيفٌ بِعِبَادِهِ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَاءُ ۖ وَهُوَ الْقَوِيُّ الْعَزِيزُ
quran.translation: Allāh is Subtle with His servants; He gives provision to whom He wills. And He is the Powerful, the Exalted in Might.

quran.note: Yusuf's words when Allah reunited him with his family after long trials.
quran.arabic: وَرَفَعَ أَبَوَيْهِ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ وَخَرُّوا لَهُ سُجَّدًا ۖ وَقَالَ يَا أَبَتِ هَٰذَا تَأْوِيلُ رُؤْيَايَ مِن قَبْلُ قَدْ جَعَلَهَا رَبِّي حَقًّا ۖ وَقَدْ أَحْسَنَ بِي إِذْ أَخْرَجَنِي مِنَ السِّجْنِ وَجَاءَ بِكُم مِّنَ الْبَدْوِ مِن بَعْدِ أَن نَّزَغَ الشَّيْطَانُ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ إِخْوَتِي ۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي لَطِيفٌ لِّمَا يَشَاءُ ۚ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْعَلِيمُ الْحَكِيمُ
quran.translation: And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they bowed to him in prostration. And he said, "O my father, this is the explanation of my vision of before. My Lord has made it reality. And He was certainly good to me when He took me out of prison and brought you [here] from bedouin life after Satan had induced [estrangement] between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills. Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise.

quran.note: Luqman tells his son that Allah brings out even a tiny seed hidden in a rock.
quran.arabic: يَا بُنَيَّ إِنَّهَا إِن تَكُ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِّنْ خَرْدَلٍ فَتَكُن فِي صَخْرَةٍ أَوْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ أَوْ فِي الْأَرْضِ يَأْتِ بِهَا اللَّهُ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَطِيفٌ خَبِيرٌ
quran.translation: [And Luqmān said], "O my son, indeed if it [i.e., a wrong] should be the weight of a mustard seed and should be within a rock or [anywhere] in the heavens or in the earth, Allāh will bring it forth. Indeed, Allāh is Subtle and Aware.

hadith.text: One night Aisha quietly followed the Prophet ﷺ to the graveyard of al-Baqi' and hurried home before him. When he found her out of breath and she would not say why, he said: "Tell me, or al-Latif al-Khabir will tell me."

scholars.text: Al-Latif al-Khabir is the One whose knowledge and awareness are so fine that they reach secrets, hidden thoughts, concealed matters and the unseen.
Among the meanings of al-Latif: He is gentle with His servant and friend, and drives goodness and kindness to him from where he does not perceive.
Al-Latif in bringing it out, al-Khabir in knowing where it is. (Ibn Kathir quotes this at 6:103 and follows it with Luqman's words about the tiny seed that Allah brings out, 31:16.)

notes: Al-Latif joins two meanings: Allah's knowledge reaches the finest and most hidden things, and He is gentle and kind with His servants in ways they do not perceive (al-Sa'di).

lessons.text: Trust Allah's gentle planning through hardship, as Yusuf did when Allah brought him out of prison and reunited him with his family.
Be sincere in private: even a tiny seed inside a rock is not hidden from Allah, and He brings it out.

names.summary: Allah is al-Khabir: fully aware of the inner reality of all things, of secrets, hidden thoughts and concealed matters. Nothing we do, say or intend escapes His awareness.

quran.note: Allah's supremacy over His servants, His wisdom and His full awareness.
quran.arabic: وَهُوَ الْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ ۚ وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ
quran.translation: And He is the subjugator over His servants. And He is the Wise, the Aware.

quran.note: The Creator knows fully what He has created.
quran.arabic: أَلَا يَعْلَمُ مَنْ خَلَقَ وَهُوَ اللَّطِيفُ الْخَبِيرُ
quran.translation: Does He who created not know, while He is the Subtle, the Aware?

quran.note: All praise belongs to Allah in this world and the next.
quran.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ ۚ وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ
quran.translation: [All] praise is [due] to Allāh, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and to Him belongs [all] praise in the Hereafter. And He is the Wise, the Aware.

quran.note: Believers are urged to look at what they are sending ahead for the Hereafter.
quran.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَلْتَنظُرْ نَفْسٌ مَّا قَدَّمَتْ لِغَدٍ ۖ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ
quran.translation: O you who have believed, fear Allāh. And let every soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow - and fear Allāh. Indeed, Allāh is Aware of what you do.

quran.note: Honour with Allah is by taqwa, not by lineage.
quran.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَاكُم مِّن ذَكَرٍ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلْنَاكُمْ شُعُوبًا وَقَبَائِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوا ۚ إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِندَ اللَّهِ أَتْقَاكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌ
quran.translation: O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allāh is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allāh is Knowing and Aware.

hadith.text: When Aisha came home out of breath after secretly following him at night and would not say why, the Prophet ﷺ said: "Tell me, or al-Latif al-Khabir will tell me."

scholars.text: Al-Hakim is wise in what He commands and forbids, in how He rewards and punishes, and in what He creates and decrees. Al-Khabir is the One who sees into secrets, hidden thoughts and concealed matters.
The verse means: does the Creator not know? Some said it means: does Allah not know His creation? The first is more fitting, because the verse ends with al-Latif, al-Khabir.
Al-Latif al-Khabir is the One whose knowledge and awareness are so fine that they reach secrets, hidden thoughts, concealed matters and the unseen.

notes: Al-Khabir is knowledge that reaches the inner reality of things, not only what is seen. It often comes together with al-Hakim (the Wise) and al-Latif (the Subtle).

lessons.text: Check your deeds today and prepare for the Hereafter, knowing that Allah is fully aware of everything you do.
Do not judge people by their looks or lineage: honour with Allah is by taqwa, and He looks at hearts and deeds.

dua.text: O Allah, I ask You to guide me to what is best by Your knowledge, and I ask You for ability by Your power, and I ask You from Your great bounty; for You are able and I am not, You know and I do not know, and You are the Knower of the unseen. (The opening of the istikharah supplication.)

names.summary: Allah is al-Halim, the Forbearing: He sees His servants disobey Him, yet He does not rush to punish them. He keeps giving them blessings and gives them time to repent, while being fully able to punish.

quran.note: On oaths sworn without intention; the verse ends with Allah's forgiveness and forbearance.
quran.arabic: لَّا يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ اللَّهُ بِاللَّغْوِ فِي أَيْمَانِكُمْ وَلَٰكِن يُؤَاخِذُكُم بِمَا كَسَبَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ ۗ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ
quran.translation: Allāh does not impose blame upon you for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He imposes blame upon you for what your hearts have earned. And Allāh is Forgiving and Forbearing.

quran.note: On marriage proposals during the waiting period; it ends with Allah's forgiveness and forbearance.
quran.arabic: وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا عَرَّضْتُم بِهِ مِنْ خِطْبَةِ النِّسَاءِ أَوْ أَكْنَنتُمْ فِي أَنفُسِكُمْ ۚ عَلِمَ اللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ سَتَذْكُرُونَهُنَّ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تُوَاعِدُوهُنَّ سِرًّا إِلَّا أَن تَقُولُوا قَوْلًا مَّعْرُوفًا ۚ وَلَا تَعْزِمُوا عُقْدَةَ النِّكَاحِ حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ الْكِتَابُ أَجَلَهُ ۚ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي أَنفُسِكُمْ فَاحْذَرُوهُ ۚ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ
quran.translation: There is no blame upon you for that to which you [indirectly] allude concerning a proposal to women or for what you conceal within yourselves. Allāh knows that you will have them in mind. But do not promise them secretly except for saying a proper saying. And do not determine to undertake a marriage contract until the decreed period reaches its end. And know that Allāh knows what is within yourselves, so beware of Him. And know that Allāh is Forgiving and Forbearing.

quran.note: Allah holds the heavens and the earth in place, and He is Forbearing and Forgiving.
quran.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُمْسِكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ أَن تَزُولَا ۚ وَلَئِن زَالَتَا إِنْ أَمْسَكَهُمَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ مِّن بَعْدِهِ ۚ إِنَّهُ كَانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورًا
quran.translation: Indeed, Allāh holds the heavens and the earth, lest they cease. And if they should cease, no one could hold them [in place] after Him. Indeed, He is Forbearing and Forgiving.

quran.note: A good loan to Allah is multiplied; He is Appreciative and Forbearing.
quran.arabic: إِن تُقْرِضُوا اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا يُضَاعِفْهُ لَكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ۚ وَاللَّهُ شَكُورٌ حَلِيمٌ
quran.translation: If you loan Allāh a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you. And Allāh is [most] Appreciative and Forbearing,

hadith.text: In times of distress the Prophet ﷺ would say: "There is no god but Allah, al-'Azim, al-Halim. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the mighty Throne. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth and Lord of the noble Throne."
The Prophet ﷺ said: "No one is more patient with hurtful words he hears than Allah. They claim He has a son, yet He still gives them well-being and provision."

scholars.text: Al-Halim keeps pouring blessings, outward and inward, upon His creation despite their sins and their many slips, and He is forbearing and does not repay the sinners for their disobedience.
scholars.book: Tafsir Asma' Allah al-Husna li-s-Sa'di (his explanations collected from his works), p. 189, from his Tafsir 5/630

scholars.text: Halim means He is patient and unhurried; He does not rush to punish His servants for their sins.

notes: Allah's forbearance is not from weakness: He is fully able to punish, yet He shows the perfection of His forbearance and forgiveness by giving sinners time and not hastening the punishment of the disobedient (al-Sa'di on 35:41).

lessons.text: Forbearance is loved by Allah: the Prophet ﷺ told Ashajj of 'Abd al-Qays, "You have two qualities that Allah loves: forbearance and deliberation."
Do not be deceived by Allah's delay; use the time He gives you to repent, for He is Forbearing and Forgiving.

dua.text: There is no god but Allah, al-'Azim, al-Halim. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the mighty Throne. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth and Lord of the noble Throne.

names.summary: Allah is al-'Azim, the Magnificent: nothing is greater or more magnificent than Him. Before His greatness the might of tyrants shrinks and the pride of kings becomes small, so the believer glorifies Him in every prayer.

quran.note: Ayat al-Kursi ends with al-'Aliyy al-'Azim.
quran.arabic: اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ ۚ لَّهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ ۗ مَن ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِندَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَئُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ
quran.translation: Allāh - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursī extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.

quran.note: Everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him.
quran.arabic: لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ ۖ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ
quran.translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and He is the Most High, the Most Great.

quran.note: The command to glorify the Name of Allah, al-'Azim; repeated in 56:96.
quran.arabic: فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ
quran.translation: So exalt the name of your Lord, the Most Great.

quran.note: Describes the one who did not believe in Allah, al-'Azim.
quran.arabic: إِنَّهُ كَانَ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ
quran.translation: Indeed, he did not used to believe in Allāh, the Most Great,

hadith.text: Hudhayfah prayed a long night prayer with the Prophet ﷺ. In bowing he said: "Subhana Rabbiya al-'Azim" (Glory be to my Lord, the Magnificent), and in prostration: "Subhana Rabbiya al-A'la" (Glory be to my Lord, the Most High).
The Prophet ﷺ said: "As for bowing, glorify the greatness of the Lord in it. As for prostration, strive hard in supplication, for it is most fitting that you will be answered."
The Prophet ﷺ said: "Two phrases are light on the tongue, heavy on the Scale and beloved to ar-Rahman: Subhan Allahi al-'Azim, subhan Allahi wa bihamdihi."

scholars.text: Al-'Azim is the One before whose greatness the might of the tyrants shrinks, and beside whose majesty the pride of overpowering kings becomes small.
He is the Magnificent, than whom none is more magnificent; the Most High, than whom none is higher; the Most Great, than whom none is greater. Exalted, holy and far above every fault is He.

notes: Every prayer contains the glorification of al-'Azim: in bowing, the believer says "Subhana Rabbiya al-'Azim", as the Prophet ﷺ did.

lessons.text: Glorify Allah's greatness in your bowing, and do not rush through it.
Honouring what Allah has made sacred comes from the taqwa of the heart.

dua.text: Subhan Allahi al-'Azim, subhan Allahi wa bihamdihi (Glory be to Allah, the Magnificent; glory be to Allah, and praise be to Him).

names.summary: Allah is al-Ghafur: He forgives sins, however many and however great, for whoever turns back to Him in repentance. Forgiveness is a permanent Attribute of His that never leaves Him.

quran.note: The Prophet ﷺ is told to inform Allah's servants of His forgiveness and mercy.
quran.arabic: نَبِّئْ عِبَادِي أَنِّي أَنَا الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ
quran.translation: [O Muḥammad], inform My servants that it is I who am the Forgiving, the Merciful,

quran.note: Addressed to those who have wronged themselves: never despair of Allah's mercy.
quran.arabic: قُلْ يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِهِمْ لَا تَقْنَطُوا مِن رَّحْمَةِ اللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا ۚ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ
quran.translation: Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allāh. Indeed, Allāh forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful."

quran.note: Al-Ghafur together with al-Wadud, the Loving.
quran.arabic: وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الْوَدُودُ
quran.translation: And He is the Forgiving, the Affectionate,

quran.note: Whoever does wrong and then seeks forgiveness will find Allah forgiving and merciful.
quran.arabic: وَمَن يَعْمَلْ سُوءًا أَوْ يَظْلِمْ نَفْسَهُ ثُمَّ يَسْتَغْفِرِ اللَّهَ يَجِدِ اللَّهَ غَفُورًا رَّحِيمًا
quran.translation: And whoever does a wrong or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness of Allāh will find Allāh Forgiving and Merciful.

hadith.text: Abu Bakr asked the Prophet ﷺ to teach him a supplication to say in his prayer. He said: "Say: O Allah, I have wronged myself greatly, and no one forgives sins except You. So forgive me with forgiveness from You, and have mercy on me. You are al-Ghafur, ar-Rahim."

The Prophet ﷺ said that a servant committed a sin and said: "My Lord, I have sinned, so forgive me." His Lord said: "My servant knows that he has a Lord who forgives sins and also punishes for them. I have forgiven My servant." And so it went each time he sinned and turned back.

scholars.text: Forgiveness and mercy are His description: two Attributes that belong to His essence and never leave Him, and their effects have never stopped flowing through all existence, filling all that exists.
This noble verse is a call to all sinners, disbelievers and others, to repent and turn back to Allah, and news that Allah forgives all sins for whoever repents from them.
Ibn Abbas and others said about the people of Paradise: He forgave them their many bad deeds and appreciated their few good deeds.

notes: Ibn Kathir explains that the forgiveness of all sins in 39:53 is for the one who repents. The call includes the disbelievers, so even shirk is forgiven when a person repents from it, but it is not forgiven for one who does not repent (see 4:48).

lessons.text: Never despair of Allah's mercy, however great your sins; turn back to Him in repentance.
Seek forgiveness often: the Prophet ﷺ said that he asked Allah's forgiveness and repented to Him more than seventy times a day.
When you slip, remember that you have a Lord who forgives sins, and ask Him for forgiveness at once.

dua.text: O Allah, I have wronged myself greatly, and no one forgives sins except You. So forgive me with forgiveness from You, and have mercy on me. You are al-Ghafur, ar-Rahim.

names.summary: Allah is ash-Shakur, the Appreciative: He accepts even a small good deed, rewards it many times over and forgives many slips. No good done sincerely for His sake is ever lost with Him.

quran.note: Those who recite Allah's Book, pray and spend receive their full reward and more.
quran.arabic: لِيُوَفِّيَهُمْ أُجُورَهُمْ وَيَزِيدَهُم مِّن فَضْلِهِ ۚ إِنَّهُ غَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ
quran.translation: That He may give them in full their rewards and increase for them of His bounty. Indeed, He is Forgiving and Appreciative.

quran.note: The words of the people of Paradise praising their Lord.
quran.arabic: وَقَالُوا الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَذْهَبَ عَنَّا الْحَزَنَ ۖ إِنَّ رَبَّنَا لَغَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ
quran.translation: And they will say, "Praise to Allāh, who has removed from us [all] sorrow. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative -

quran.note: Whoever earns a good deed, Allah increases its good.
quran.arabic: ذَٰلِكَ الَّذِي يُبَشِّرُ اللَّهُ عِبَادَهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ ۗ قُل لَّا أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْرًا إِلَّا الْمَوَدَّةَ فِي الْقُرْبَىٰ ۗ وَمَن يَقْتَرِفْ حَسَنَةً نَّزِدْ لَهُ فِيهَا حُسْنًا ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ
quran.translation: It is that of which Allāh gives good tidings to His servants who believe and do righteous deeds. Say, [O Muḥammad], "I do not ask you for it [i.e., this message] any payment [but] only good will through [i.e., due to] kinship." And whoever commits a good deed - We will increase for him good therein. Indeed, Allāh is Forgiving and Appreciative.

quran.note: A good loan to Allah is multiplied and sins are forgiven.
quran.arabic: إِن تُقْرِضُوا اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا يُضَاعِفْهُ لَكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ۚ وَاللَّهُ شَكُورٌ حَلِيمٌ
quran.translation: If you loan Allāh a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you. And Allāh is [most] Appreciative and Forbearing,

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: "While a man was walking along a road, he found a thorny branch on it and moved it aside. Allah appreciated his deed and forgave him."

The Prophet ﷺ told of a thirsty man who drank from a well, then saw a dog panting from thirst. He went down again, filled his shoe with water and gave the dog to drink. "Allah appreciated his deed and forgave him." The Companions asked whether there is reward even for kindness to animals, and he said: "There is reward for kindness to every living creature."

scholars.text: Among His Names are ash-Shakir and ash-Shakur: He appreciates a small deed that is sincere, pure and beneficial, and He pardons many slips. He never lets the reward of anyone who does good go to waste; rather He multiplies it many times over, without count or reckoning.
scholars.book: Tafsir Asma' Allah al-Husna li-s-Sa'di (his explanations collected from his works), p. 210

scholars.text: Ibn Abbas and others said about the people of Paradise: He forgave them their many bad deeds and appreciated their few good deeds.
He appreciates a small act of obedience and rewards it with great reward. He gives abundant blessings and is pleased with a little thanks.

notes: Allah has no need of our deeds, yet He appreciates them: He accepts the little, rewards it with much and forgives much. His appreciation is real and befits His majesty.

lessons.text: Never think little of any good deed, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face.
Thank people for their kindness: whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah.
Be grateful to Allah, for gratitude brings more of His favour.

dua.text: O Allah, help me to remember You, to thank You and to worship You well. (The Prophet ﷺ told Mu'adh never to leave it after any prayer.)

names.summary: Allah is al-'Aliyy, the Most High, high in every way: high by His essence above His Throne and above all His creation, high in status through the perfection of His Attributes, and high in His power over everything.

quran.note: Ayat al-Kursi ends with al-'Aliyy al-'Azim.
quran.arabic: اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ ۚ لَّهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ ۗ مَن ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِندَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَئُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ
quran.translation: Allāh - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursī extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.

quran.note: Allah is the Truth, al-'Aliyy, al-Kabir.
quran.arabic: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ وَأَنَّ مَا يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ هُوَ الْبَاطِلُ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْكَبِيرُ
quran.translation: That is because Allāh is the True Reality, and that which they call upon other than Him is falsehood, and because Allāh is the Most High, the Grand.

quran.note: The command to glorify the Name of Allah as al-A'la, the Most High.
quran.arabic: سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَى
quran.translation: Exalt the name of your Lord, the Most High,

quran.note: Allah is the Supreme One above His servants.
quran.arabic: وَهُوَ الْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ ۚ وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ
quran.translation: And He is the subjugator over His servants. And He is the Wise, the Aware.

quran.note: The angels fear their Lord above them.
quran.arabic: يَخَافُونَ رَبَّهُم مِّن فَوْقِهِمْ وَيَفْعَلُونَ مَا يُؤْمَرُونَ
quran.translation: They fear their Lord above them, and they do what they are commanded.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ asked a slave girl: "Where is Allah?" She said: "In the heaven." He asked: "Who am I?" She said: "You are the Messenger of Allah." He said: "Free her, for she is a believer."
Zaynab bint Jahsh used to say proudly to the other wives of the Prophet ﷺ: "Your families married you off, but Allah married me from above the seven heavens."

The Prophet ﷺ said that when Allah decrees a matter in the heaven, the angels beat their wings in submission to His word. When the fear leaves their hearts, they ask what their Lord said, and the answer comes: "The truth, and He is al-'Aliyy, al-Kabir."

scholars.text: Al-'Aliyy: high by His essence above His Throne, high in His power over all creatures, and high in His status through the perfection of His Attributes.
He has absolute highness in every respect: highness of essence, highness of status and Attributes, and highness of power.
scholars.book: Tafsir al-Sa'di 5/487 (Dar al-Madani ed.), quoted in ad-Durar as-Saniyyah's al-Mawsu'ah al-'Aqadiyyah 1/489

scholars.text: He is the Most High, than whom none is higher, and the Magnificent and Most Great, than whom none is greater.

notes: Ahl as-Sunnah affirm that Allah is above His creation by His essence, above His Throne, as well as high in status and in power. His highness is real and befits Him, without likening Him to creation and without asking how.

lessons.text: In every prostration, glorify your Lord, the Most High, as the Prophet ﷺ did.
Humble yourself for Allah, and He will raise you: no one humbles himself for Allah except that Allah raises him.

dua.text: Subhana Rabbiya al-A'la (Glory be to my Lord, the Most High), said in prostration.

names.summary: Allah is al-Kabir, the Most Great: great in His essence, His Names and His Attributes, and greater than everything. All greatness and pride belong to Him alone, and we declare it in every prayer by saying "Allahu Akbar".

quran.note: Knower of the unseen and the seen, al-Kabir, al-Muta'al.
quran.arabic: عَالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ الْكَبِيرُ الْمُتَعَالِ
quran.translation: [He is] Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Grand, the Exalted.

quran.note: Allah is the Truth, al-'Aliyy, al-Kabir.
quran.arabic: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ وَأَنَّ مَا يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ هُوَ الْبَاطِلُ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْكَبِيرُ
quran.translation: That is because Allāh is the True Reality, and that which they call upon other than Him is falsehood, and because Allāh is the Most High, the Grand.

quran.note: The angels' words after Allah speaks.
quran.arabic: وَلَا تَنفَعُ الشَّفَاعَةُ عِندَهُ إِلَّا لِمَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ ۚ حَتَّىٰ إِذَا فُزِّعَ عَن قُلُوبِهِمْ قَالُوا مَاذَا قَالَ رَبُّكُمْ ۖ قَالُوا الْحَقَّ ۖ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْكَبِيرُ
quran.translation: And intercession does not benefit with Him except for one whom He permits. [And those wait] until, when terror is removed from their hearts, they will say [to one another], "What has your Lord said?" They will say, "The truth." And He is the Most High, the Grand.

quran.note: Judgment belongs to Allah, al-'Aliyy, al-Kabir.
quran.arabic: ذَٰلِكُم بِأَنَّهُ إِذَا دُعِيَ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ كَفَرْتُمْ ۖ وَإِن يُشْرَكْ بِهِ تُؤْمِنُوا ۚ فَالْحُكْمُ لِلَّهِ الْعَلِيِّ الْكَبِيرِ
quran.translation: [They will be told], "That is because, when Allāh was called upon alone, you disbelieved; but if others were associated with Him, you believed. So the judgement is with Allāh, the Most High, the Grand."

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said that when Allah decrees a matter in the heaven, the angels beat their wings in submission to His word. When the fear leaves their hearts, they ask what their Lord said, and the answer comes: "The truth, and He is al-'Aliyy, al-Kabir."
The Prophet ﷺ said: "Might is His lower garment and pride is His cloak. [Allah says:] Whoever competes with Me in them, I will punish him."

A man praying behind the Prophet ﷺ said: "Allahu akbaru kabira, wal-hamdu lillahi kathira, wa subhan Allahi bukratan wa asila." The Prophet ﷺ said: "I marvelled at it: the gates of heaven were opened for it." Ibn Umar said he never stopped saying it after that.

scholars.text: Al-Kabir is the One who is greater than everything; al-Muta'al is high above everything, who has encompassed all things in knowledge and subdued all things.
Al-Kabir is great in His essence, His Names and His Attributes; al-Muta'al is high above all His creation by His essence, His power and His might.
He is the Most Great, than whom none is greater; exalted, holy and far above is He.

notes: Saying "Allahu Akbar" declares that Allah is greater than everything. Pride and supremacy belong to Him alone, so the servant's part is humility.

lessons.text: Beware of arrogance: no one with an atom's weight of pride in his heart will enter Paradise.
Declare Allah's greatness often, as He commanded at the end of Surah al-Isra'.

dua.text: Allahu akbaru kabira, wal-hamdu lillahi kathira, wa subhan Allahi bukratan wa asila (Allah is the Most Great, truly great; much praise belongs to Allah; and glory be to Allah, morning and evening).

names.summary: Allah is al-Hafiz: He guards and preserves all things. He protects His servants, keeps a full record of everything they say and do, and will repay them for it in full.

quran.note: Hud tells his people that his Lord is Guardian over all things.
quran.arabic: فَإِن تَوَلَّوْا فَقَدْ أَبْلَغْتُكُم مَّا أُرْسِلْتُ بِهِ إِلَيْكُمْ ۚ وَيَسْتَخْلِفُ رَبِّي قَوْمًا غَيْرَكُمْ وَلَا تَضُرُّونَهُ شَيْئًا ۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ حَفِيظٌ
quran.translation: But if you turn away, then I have already conveyed that with which I was sent to you. My Lord will give succession to a people other than you, and you will not harm Him at all. Indeed my Lord is, over all things, Guardian."

quran.note: Your Lord is Guardian over all things.
quran.arabic: وَمَا كَانَ لَهُ عَلَيْهِم مِّن سُلْطَانٍ إِلَّا لِنَعْلَمَ مَن يُؤْمِنُ بِالْآخِرَةِ مِمَّنْ هُوَ مِنْهَا فِي شَكٍّ ۗ وَرَبُّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ حَفِيظٌ
quran.translation: And he had over them no authority except [it was decreed] that We might make evident who believes in the Hereafter from who is thereof in doubt. And your Lord, over all things, is Guardian.

quran.note: Allah keeps watch over those who take protectors besides Him.
quran.arabic: وَالَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِن دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَاءَ اللَّهُ حَفِيظٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَمَا أَنتَ عَلَيْهِم بِوَكِيلٍ
quran.translation: And those who take as allies other than Him - Allāh is [yet] Guardian over them; and you, [O Muḥammad], are not over them a manager -

quran.note: Ya'qub entrusts his son to Allah, the best of guardians (related form hafiz).
quran.arabic: قَالَ هَلْ آمَنُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ إِلَّا كَمَا أَمِنتُكُمْ عَلَىٰ أَخِيهِ مِن قَبْلُ ۖ فَاللَّهُ خَيْرٌ حَافِظًا ۖ وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ
quran.translation: He said, "Should I entrust you with him except [under coercion] as I entrusted you with his brother before? But Allāh is the best guardian, and He is the most merciful of the merciful."

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said to the young Ibn Abbas: "Be mindful of Allah, and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah, and you will find Him before you. When you ask, ask Allah; and when you seek help, seek help from Allah."

When going to bed, the Prophet ﷺ taught us to say: "In Your Name, my Lord, I lay down my side, and by You I raise it. If You keep my soul, have mercy on it, and if You send it back, protect it with that by which You protect Your righteous servants."

scholars.text: Allah witnesses and guards the words and deeds of His servants, and He will repay them for them: good with good, and evil with evil.
He guards His servants, He keeps their deeds recorded against them, and He keeps their reward safe, then gives it to them in full, complete and abundant.

notes: Two meanings meet in this Name, as Ibn Kathir and al-Sa'di explain: Allah protects His servants, and He keeps a complete record of their deeds, so that nothing is lost and no one is wronged.
Allah also guards His believing servants in a special way: whoever is mindful of Allah's commands, Allah protects him, as the Prophet ﷺ taught Ibn Abbas.

lessons.text: Guard Allah's limits and His rights, and He will guard you.
Entrust what you love and fear for to Allah, as Ya'qub did, for He is the best of guardians.
Watch your words and deeds, for Allah keeps every one of them and will repay them.
Before you sleep, hand your soul to Allah and ask Him to protect it as He protects His righteous servants.

dua.text: In Your Name, my Lord, I lay down my side, and by You I raise it. If You keep my soul, have mercy on it, and if You send it back, protect it with that by which You protect Your righteous servants.

names.summary: Allah is al-Muqit: He gives every creature the food (qut) it lives by, He has full power over all things, and He keeps watch over every deed.

quran.note: After speaking of good and bad intercession, Allah says He is Muqit over all things.
quran.arabic: مَّن يَشْفَعْ شَفَاعَةً حَسَنَةً يَكُن لَّهُ نَصِيبٌ مِّنْهَا ۖ وَمَن يَشْفَعْ شَفَاعَةً سَيِّئَةً يَكُن لَّهُ كِفْلٌ مِّنْهَا ۗ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُّقِيتًا
quran.translation: Whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a share [i.e., reward] therefrom; and whoever intercedes for an evil cause will have a portion [i.e., burden] therefrom. And ever is Allāh, over all things, a Keeper.

hadith.text: Ibn Umar asked his steward whether the slaves had been given their food. When he said no, Ibn Umar told him to go and give it to them, and reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: "It is sin enough for a person to hold back the food of those in his care."
The Prophet ﷺ prayed: "O Allah, give the family of Muhammad provision that is just enough to live on (qut)."

scholars.scholar: Ibn Abbas, Ata, Atiyyah, Qatadah and Matar al-Warraq
scholars.text: Muqit means Hafiz: the Guardian.

scholars.scholar: Sa'id ibn Jubayr, as-Suddi and Ibn Zayd
scholars.text: Muqit means Qadir: the One who has full power.
Al-Muqit is ar-Razzaq, the Provider.
Allah is Witness, Guardian and Reckoner over these deeds, and He will repay each person what he deserves.

notes: The word qut, the food a creature lives on, comes from the same root as al-Muqit.

Ibn Kathir reports several explanations from the Salaf: the Guardian, the Witness, the All-Powerful and the Provider. Each of these is true of Allah, and together they explain the meaning "the Powerful Sustainer".

lessons.text: Do not hold back the food and needs of those in your care; neglecting them is sin enough.
Be content with what is enough, as the Prophet ﷺ asked Allah for his own family.
Intercede only for what is good, for Allah watches over every intercession and what comes of it.

names.summary: Allah is al-Hasib: He keeps account of every deed, small or great, and will judge it with justice and grace. He is also enough for whoever relies on Him.

quran.note: At the end of the rules on orphans' wealth: Allah is enough as Reckoner.
quran.arabic: وَابْتَلُوا الْيَتَامَىٰ حَتَّىٰ إِذَا بَلَغُوا النِّكَاحَ فَإِنْ آنَسْتُم مِّنْهُمْ رُشْدًا فَادْفَعُوا إِلَيْهِمْ أَمْوَالَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا تَأْكُلُوهَا إِسْرَافًا وَبِدَارًا أَن يَكْبَرُوا ۚ وَمَن كَانَ غَنِيًّا فَلْيَسْتَعْفِفْ ۖ وَمَن كَانَ فَقِيرًا فَلْيَأْكُلْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ ۚ فَإِذَا دَفَعْتُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ أَمْوَالَهُمْ فَأَشْهِدُوا عَلَيْهِمْ ۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِاللَّهِ حَسِيبًا
quran.translation: And test the orphans [in their abilities] until they reach marriageable age. Then if you perceive in them sound judgement, release their property to them. And do not consume it excessively and quickly, [anticipating] that they will grow up. And whoever, [when acting as guardian], is self-sufficient should refrain [from taking a fee]; and whoever is poor - let him take according to what is acceptable. Then when you release their property to them, bring witnesses upon them. And sufficient is Allāh as Accountant.

quran.note: On returning greetings: Allah keeps account of all things.
quran.arabic: وَإِذَا حُيِّيتُم بِتَحِيَّةٍ فَحَيُّوا بِأَحْسَنَ مِنْهَا أَوْ رُدُّوهَا ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ حَسِيبًا
quran.translation: And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet [in return] with one better than it or [at least] return it [in a like manner]. Indeed Allāh is ever, over all things, an Accountant.

quran.note: Those who deliver Allah's messages fear none but Him; Allah is enough as Reckoner.
quran.arabic: الَّذِينَ يُبَلِّغُونَ رِسَالَاتِ اللَّهِ وَيَخْشَوْنَهُ وَلَا يَخْشَوْنَ أَحَدًا إِلَّا اللَّهَ ۗ وَكَفَىٰ بِاللَّهِ حَسِيبًا
quran.translation: [Allāh praises] those who convey the messages of Allāh and fear Him and do not fear anyone but Allāh. And sufficient is Allāh as Accountant.

quran.note: The believers' answer when warned about a gathered enemy (related word hasb, sufficient).
quran.arabic: الَّذِينَ قَالَ لَهُمُ النَّاسُ إِنَّ النَّاسَ قَدْ جَمَعُوا لَكُمْ فَاخْشَوْهُمْ فَزَادَهُمْ إِيمَانًا وَقَالُوا حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ
quran.translation: Those to whom people [i.e., hypocrites] said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them." But it [merely] increased them in faith, and they said, "Sufficient for us is Allāh, and [He is] the best Disposer of affairs."

hadith.text: A man praised another in front of the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "You have cut your companion's neck." Then he said that if one of you must praise his brother, let him say, only if he believes it: "I consider him to be so, and Allah is his Hasib (the One who will reckon him), and I do not declare anyone pure before Allah."

Ibn Abbas said that "Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs" was said by Ibrahim when he was thrown into the fire, and by Muhammad ﷺ when people told him that a great army had gathered against them.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever is brought to account will be punished." Aisha asked about the easy reckoning that Allah mentions (84:8), and he said: "That is only the showing of deeds. But whoever is questioned closely in the reckoning will be ruined."

scholars.text: Allah is enough as the One who takes account, as Witness and as Watcher over the guardians while they look after the orphans.
He keeps the servants' deeds recorded, the good and the bad, the small and the great, then repays them as His grace, His justice and His praiseworthy judgment require.

notes: The word hasb, "enough", comes from the same root, as in the words of Ibrahim and Muhammad ﷺ: "Allah is sufficient for us." The One who will take account of everything is also the One who is enough for those who rely on Him.

lessons.text: Do not overpraise people or declare them pure; say: "I consider him so, and Allah is his Reckoner."
When you are afraid, rely on Allah and say: "Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."
Take care with the rights of others, such as orphans' wealth, for Allah is the Reckoner over it.
Prepare for the reckoning, knowing that whoever is questioned closely on that Day is ruined.

dua.text: Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.

names.summary: Al-Jalil means the Majestic. Allah's majesty (al-jalal) is affirmed in His Name Dhul-Jalali wal-Ikram, the Owner of majesty and honour, who deserves to be revered and never disobeyed.
names.established_note: Al-Jalil does not occur as a Name of Allah in the Quran or in an authentic hadith; it comes in the weak enumeration narration, and Ibn Uthaymeen did not include it among the 99 Names he gathered from the Quran and Sunnah (al-Qawa'id al-Muthla). What is established is Allah's Attribute of majesty in the Name Dhul-Jalali wal-Ikram (55:27, 55:78), which IslamQA counts among His Names.

quran.note: Allah's Face remains after everyone on earth perishes; He is the Owner of majesty and honour (related form al-jalal).
quran.arabic: وَيَبْقَىٰ وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ
quran.translation: And there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor.

quran.note: Surah ar-Rahman closes by blessing the Name of Allah, Owner of majesty and honour (al-jalal).
quran.arabic: تَبَارَكَ اسْمُ رَبِّكَ ذِي الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ
quran.translation: Blessed is the name of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said that on the Day of Resurrection Allah will say: "Where are those who loved one another for the sake of My majesty? Today I will shade them in My shade, on a day when there is no shade but Mine."
After finishing the prayer, the Prophet ﷺ would say: "O Allah, You are as-Salam and from You is peace. Blessed are You, O Owner of majesty and honour."

scholars.text: He is worthy of being revered, so that He is not disobeyed, and of being obeyed, so that He is not opposed.
Owner of majesty means the Owner of greatness, grandeur and glory, who is magnified, honoured and revered for His own sake.
I have gathered ninety-nine Names from what became clear to me in the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ.
scholars.book: al-Qawa'id al-Muthla (al-Jalil is not in his list)

scholars.text: Dhul-Jalali wal-Ikram is one of Allah's Names.

notes: The meaning "the Majestic" is true of Allah: majesty is His real Attribute, affirmed in the Quran and the Sunnah. The question is only whether the word al-Jalil itself is counted among His Names.
When calling on Allah by His majesty, use the wording that is established: "O Owner of majesty and honour."

lessons.text: Love others for the sake of Allah's majesty, and hope for His shade on the Day of Resurrection.
