Revere Allah so that you do not disobey Him, and obey Him so that you do not oppose Him.
After every prayer, praise Allah as the Owner of majesty and honour, as the Prophet ﷺ did.

dua.text: O Allah, You are as-Salam and from You is peace. Blessed are You, O Owner of majesty and honour.

names.summary: Allah is al-Karim: the Most Generous, abundant in good. He needs nothing from anyone, yet His goodness reaches the grateful and the ungrateful, and He does not turn back empty the hands raised to Him.

quran.note: Sulayman, seeing the throne brought to him, says his Lord is Free of need and Generous.
quran.arabic: قَالَ الَّذِي عِندَهُ عِلْمٌ مِّنَ الْكِتَابِ أَنَا آتِيكَ بِهِ قَبْلَ أَن يَرْتَدَّ إِلَيْكَ طَرْفُكَ ۚ فَلَمَّا رَآهُ مُسْتَقِرًّا عِندَهُ قَالَ هَٰذَا مِن فَضْلِ رَبِّي لِيَبْلُوَنِي أَأَشْكُرُ أَمْ أَكْفُرُ ۖ وَمَن شَكَرَ فَإِنَّمَا يَشْكُرُ لِنَفْسِهِ ۖ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ رَبِّي غَنِيٌّ كَرِيمٌ
quran.translation: Said one who had knowledge from the Scripture, "I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you." And when [Solomon] saw it placed before him, he said, "This is from the favor of my Lord to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful. And whoever is grateful - his gratitude is only for [the benefit of] himself. And whoever is ungrateful - then indeed, my Lord is Free of need and Generous."

quran.note: Man is asked what deceived him about his Lord, al-Karim.
quran.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الْإِنسَانُ مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ الْكَرِيمِ
quran.translation: O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous,

quran.note: In the first revelation: your Lord is al-Akram, the Most Generous.
quran.arabic: اقْرَأْ وَرَبُّكَ الْأَكْرَمُ
quran.translation: Recite, and your Lord is the most Generous -

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Your Lord, Blessed and Exalted, is Shy and Generous (Karim). He is shy, when His servant raises his hands to Him, to turn them back empty."
The Prophet ﷺ was the most generous of people, and he was at his most generous in Ramadan, when Jibril met him every night to study the Quran with him.

scholars.text: He is Free of need of his deeds, and Generous, abundant in good, which reaches both the grateful and the ungrateful. But gratitude for His blessings calls for more of them, and ingratitude calls for their loss.
The ayah means: what has deceived you, son of Adam, about your Lord, the Generous? This is a warning, and not, as some people imagine, a hint at the answer because He said "the Generous".

notes: Allah's generosity is a reason to love Him and thank Him, never an excuse to disobey Him. Ibn Kathir explains that 82:6 is a warning to the one who is careless, not an invitation to say that His generosity deceived him.

lessons.text: Raise your hands to Allah with hope, for He is too generous to turn them back empty.
Be generous with people, as the Prophet ﷺ was, and most of all in Ramadan.
Thank Allah for His gifts: gratitude brings more, and ingratitude brings loss.
Do not let Allah's generosity make you careless about sin.

names.summary: Allah is ar-Raqib: He watches over His servants at every moment. He sees their movement and their stillness, what they hide and what they show, and nothing about them escapes Him.

quran.note: After commanding taqwa and care for the ties of kinship, Allah says He is Watcher over you.
quran.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنْهُمَا رِجَالًا كَثِيرًا وَنِسَاءً ۚ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي تَسَاءَلُونَ بِهِ وَالْأَرْحَامَ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيبًا
quran.translation: O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women. And fear Allāh, through whom you ask one another, and the wombs. Indeed Allāh is ever, over you, an Observer.

quran.note: Isa's answer to Allah about his people.
quran.arabic: مَا قُلْتُ لَهُمْ إِلَّا مَا أَمَرْتَنِي بِهِ أَنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبَّكُمْ ۚ وَكُنتُ عَلَيْهِمْ شَهِيدًا مَّا دُمْتُ فِيهِمْ ۖ فَلَمَّا تَوَفَّيْتَنِي كُنتَ أَنتَ الرَّقِيبَ عَلَيْهِمْ ۚ وَأَنتَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ
quran.translation: I said not to them except what You commanded me - to worship Allāh, my Lord and your Lord. And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them; but when You took me up, You were the Observer over them, and You are, over all things, Witness.

quran.note: Allah is Watcher over all things.
quran.arabic: لَّا يَحِلُّ لَكَ النِّسَاءُ مِن بَعْدُ وَلَا أَن تَبَدَّلَ بِهِنَّ مِنْ أَزْوَاجٍ وَلَوْ أَعْجَبَكَ حُسْنُهُنَّ إِلَّا مَا مَلَكَتْ يَمِينُكَ ۗ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ رَّقِيبًا
quran.translation: Not lawful to you, [O Muḥammad], are [any additional] women after [this], nor [is it] for you to exchange them for [other] wives, even if their beauty were to please you, except what your right hand possesses. And ever is Allāh, over all things, an Observer.

hadith.text: Jibril asked the Prophet ﷺ about ihsan, and he said: "It is to worship Allah as though you see Him, and though you do not see Him, He sees you."

The Prophet ﷺ said that on the Day of Resurrection, when some of his followers are driven away and he is told that they changed the religion after him, he will say what the righteous servant Isa said: that Allah was the Watcher over them after he left them.

scholars.text: He watches over all your deeds and all your states.
He sees His servants in their movement and their stillness, in what they keep secret and what they show, and in all their states.

notes: Remembering that Allah sees you is the meaning of ihsan, as the Prophet ﷺ explained to Jibril. It makes a person do his best in worship, in private and in public.

lessons.text: Worship Allah as though you see Him, and remember that even when you do not see Him, He sees you.
Keep your duty to Allah and to your relatives, for He is watching over you.
Hold fast to the religion as the Prophet ﷺ left it, and do not change it.

names.summary: Allah is al-Mujib: He answers those who call on Him. He is near to whoever calls on Him, in asking or in worship, and He answers them by giving what they ask, accepting their worship and rewarding it.

quran.note: Salih calls his people to seek forgiveness, for his Lord is Near and Responsive.
quran.arabic: وَإِلَىٰ ثَمُودَ أَخَاهُمْ صَالِحًا ۚ قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُ ۖ هُوَ أَنشَأَكُم مِّنَ الْأَرْضِ وَاسْتَعْمَرَكُمْ فِيهَا فَاسْتَغْفِرُوهُ ثُمَّ تُوبُوا إِلَيْهِ ۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي قَرِيبٌ مُّجِيبٌ
quran.translation: And to Thamūd [We sent] their brother Ṣāliḥ. He said, "O my people, worship Allāh; you have no deity other than Him. He has produced you from the earth and settled you in it, so ask forgiveness of Him and then repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is near and responsive."

quran.note: Among the ayat on fasting, Allah tells of His nearness and His answer to those who call on Him (verb form ujibu).
quran.arabic: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ ۖ أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ الدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ ۖ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا لِي وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا بِي لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْشُدُونَ
quran.translation: And when My servants ask you, [O Muḥammad], concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me [by obedience] and believe in Me that they may be [rightly] guided.

quran.note: Allah commands His servants to call on Him and promises to answer (verb form).
quran.arabic: وَقَالَ رَبُّكُمُ ادْعُونِي أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِي سَيَدْخُلُونَ جَهَنَّمَ دَاخِرِينَ
quran.translation: And your Lord says, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you." Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell [rendered] contemptible.

quran.note: Nuh called on Allah, and Allah praises Himself as the best of those who answer.
quran.arabic: وَلَقَدْ نَادَانَا نُوحٌ فَلَنِعْمَ الْمُجِيبُونَ
quran.translation: And Noah had certainly called Us, and [We are] the best of responders.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Our Lord, Blessed and Exalted, descends every night to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains, and He says: Who is calling on Me, so that I may answer him? Who is asking of Me, so that I may give him? Who is seeking My forgiveness, so that I may forgive him?"
The Prophet ﷺ said: "The supplication of any of you is answered as long as he is not hasty, saying: I prayed, but I was not answered."

scholars.text: He is near to whoever calls on Him, whether the call is asking or worship. He answers him by giving him what he asked for, accepting his worship and rewarding him for it with the finest reward.
The meaning is that Allah does not let any caller's supplication fail, and nothing keeps Him busy from it; rather, He hears every supplication.

notes: Ahl as-Sunnah affirm that Allah descends to the lowest heaven in the last third of every night, in a way that befits His majesty, without asking how and without likening it to the descent of creation.

lessons.text: Call on Allah in the last third of the night, when He asks who is calling on Him so that He may answer.
Do not be hasty or give up, saying you prayed and were not answered.
Answer Allah's call by obeying Him and believing in Him, and your call will be answered.
Turn to Allah with forgiveness-seeking and repentance, for He is near and answers.

names.summary: Allah is al-Wasi': vast in His Attributes, His bounty and His mercy. His giving never runs short, His mercy is wide enough for all things, and He knows who deserves His favour.

quran.note: On the direction of prayer; the ayah ends with al-Wasi' and al-'Alim.
quran.arabic: وَلِلَّهِ الْمَشْرِقُ وَالْمَغْرِبُ ۚ فَأَيْنَمَا تُوَلُّوا فَثَمَّ وَجْهُ اللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ
quran.translation: And to Allāh belongs the east and the west. So wherever you [might] turn, there is the Face of Allāh. Indeed, Allāh is all-Encompassing and Knowing.

quran.note: On the multiplied reward of spending in Allah's way.
quran.arabic: مَّثَلُ الَّذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ حَبَّةٍ أَنبَتَتْ سَبْعَ سَنَابِلَ فِي كُلِّ سُنبُلَةٍ مِّائَةُ حَبَّةٍ ۗ وَاللَّهُ يُضَاعِفُ لِمَن يَشَاءُ ۗ وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ
quran.translation: The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allāh is like a seed [of grain] which grows seven spikes; in each spike is a hundred grains. And Allāh multiplies [His reward] for whom He wills. And Allāh is all-Encompassing and Knowing.

quran.note: Allah says His mercy encompasses all things.
quran.arabic: وَاكْتُبْ لَنَا فِي هَٰذِهِ الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ إِنَّا هُدْنَا إِلَيْكَ ۚ قَالَ عَذَابِي أُصِيبُ بِهِ مَنْ أَشَاءُ ۖ وَرَحْمَتِي وَسِعَتْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ ۚ فَسَأَكْتُبُهَا لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكَاةَ وَالَّذِينَ هُم بِآيَاتِنَا يُؤْمِنُونَ
quran.translation: And decree for us in this world [that which is] good and [also] in the Hereafter; indeed, we have turned back to You." [Allāh] said, "My punishment - I afflict with it whom I will, but My mercy encompasses all things." So I will decree it [especially] for those who fear Me and give zakāh and those who believe in Our verses-

quran.note: The angels who carry the Throne praise Allah for encompassing all things in mercy and knowledge.
quran.arabic: الَّذِينَ يَحْمِلُونَ الْعَرْشَ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهُ يُسَبِّحُونَ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّهِمْ وَيُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ وَيَسْتَغْفِرُونَ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا رَبَّنَا وَسِعْتَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ رَّحْمَةً وَعِلْمًا فَاغْفِرْ لِلَّذِينَ تَابُوا وَاتَّبَعُوا سَبِيلَكَ وَقِهِمْ عَذَابَ الْجَحِيمِ
quran.translation: Those [angels] who carry the Throne and those around it exalt [Allāh] with praise of their Lord and believe in Him and ask forgiveness for those who have believed, [saying], "Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who have repented and followed Your way and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah's right Hand is full; spending night and day does not lessen it. Do you see what He has spent since He created the heavens and the earth? It has not lessened what is in His right Hand." He also said that Allah's Throne is over the water, and that in His other Hand is the outpouring (or, the narrator was unsure, the withholding), and He raises and lowers.

In a hadith qudsi, Allah says: "If the first and the last of you, mankind and jinn, stood on one plain and asked of Me, and I gave each one what he asked, that would not lessen what I have, except as a needle lessens the sea when it is dipped into it."
A Bedouin prayed: "O Allah, have mercy on me and on Muhammad, and on no one else with us." The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "You have narrowed something vast," meaning the mercy of Allah.

scholars.text: He, the Exalted, is vast in bounty, and His Attributes are vast and great, and He knows your secrets and your intentions.
His bounty is vast and plentiful, greater than His creation, and He knows who deserves it and who does not.

notes: The hadith of al-Bukhari mentions Allah's right Hand and His other Hand. Ahl as-Sunnah affirm Allah's Hands as real, as befits His majesty, unlike the hands of creation, without asking how and without explaining them away.

lessons.text: Spend in Allah's way and do not fear poverty, for His Hand is full and His giving never lessens it.
Never narrow Allah's mercy, for yourself or for others.
Ask Allah for much, for giving everyone all they ask would not lessen what He has.

dua.text: O Allah, I ask You of Your bounty (said when leaving the mosque).

names.summary: Allah is al-Hakim: the All-Wise, whose wisdom is perfect. He creates nothing except for a wise purpose, and nothing in His creation or His commands is outside His wisdom.

quran.note: The angels admit they know only what Allah taught them, and praise Him as al-'Alim and al-Hakim.
quran.arabic: قَالُوا سُبْحَانَكَ لَا عِلْمَ لَنَا إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمْتَنَا ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ الْعَلِيمُ الْحَكِيمُ
quran.translation: They said, "Exalted are You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, it is You who is the Knowing, the Wise."

quran.note: Allah's highness above His servants is mentioned together with His wisdom and His knowledge.
quran.arabic: وَهُوَ الْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ ۚ وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ
quran.translation: And He is the subjugator over His servants. And He is the Wise, the Aware.

quran.note: Allah knows what is good for His servants even when they dislike it.
quran.arabic: كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِتَالُ وَهُوَ كُرْهٌ لَّكُمْ ۖ وَعَسَىٰ أَن تَكْرَهُوا شَيْئًا وَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ ۖ وَعَسَىٰ أَن تُحِبُّوا شَيْئًا وَهُوَ شَرٌّ لَّكُمْ ۗ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ وَأَنتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
quran.translation: Battle has been enjoined upon you while it is hateful to you. But perhaps you hate a thing and it is good for you; and perhaps you love a thing and it is bad for you. And Allāh knows, while you know not.

hadith.text: A Bedouin asked the Prophet ﷺ for words to say. He taught him: "There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. Allah is the Greatest, very great. Much praise be to Allah. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. There is no might and no power except by Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise." When the man asked what to say for himself, he taught him: "O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me and provide for me."

The Prophet ﷺ said: "How wonderful is the affair of the believer! All of it is good for him, and this is for no one but the believer. If something good happens to him, he is thankful, and that is good for him. If harm befalls him, he is patient, and that is good for him."

scholars.text: Al-Hakim is the One who has perfect wisdom: no creature is outside it and no command departs from it. He has created nothing except for a wise purpose, and He has commanded nothing except for a wise purpose.
He is wise in all that He does, and aware of the right places of things, so He gives only to the one who deserves it and withholds only from the one who deserves that.

notes: As al-Sa'di's words show, Allah's wisdom covers both what He creates and decrees and what He commands in His law. A servant may not see the wisdom in every event, but he knows that Allah does nothing without it.

lessons.text: Meet ease with thanks and hardship with patience, trusting Allah's wisdom in both; then all of it is good for you.
Trust Allah's choice for you even when it is not what you wanted, for He knows what is good for you.
Admit, as the angels did, that you know only what Allah has taught you.

dua.text: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. Allah is the Greatest, very great. Much praise be to Allah. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. There is no might and no power except by Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise.

names.summary: Allah is al-Wadud: He loves His prophets and His believing servants, and He is loved by them more than anything else. His love is real, befitting His majesty and unlike the love of creation.

quran.note: Al-Wadud is mentioned together with al-Ghafur.
quran.arabic: وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الْوَدُودُ
quran.translation: And He is the Forgiving, the Affectionate,

quran.note: Shu'ayb calls his people to seek forgiveness, for his Lord is Merciful and Loving.
quran.arabic: وَاسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ ثُمَّ تُوبُوا إِلَيْهِ ۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي رَحِيمٌ وَدُودٌ
quran.translation: And ask forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Affectionate."

quran.note: Allah's love for a people and their love for Him are both affirmed.
quran.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَن يَرْتَدَّ مِنكُمْ عَن دِينِهِ فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِي اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ أَذِلَّةٍ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَعِزَّةٍ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ يُجَاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلَا يَخَافُونَ لَوْمَةَ لَائِمٍ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَن يَشَاءُ ۚ وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ
quran.translation: O you who have believed, whoever of you should revert from his religion - Allāh will bring forth [in place of them] a people He will love and who will love Him [who are] humble toward the believers, strong against the disbelievers; they strive in the cause of Allāh and do not fear the blame of a critic. That is the favor of Allāh; He bestows it upon whom He wills. And Allāh is all-Encompassing and Knowing.

quran.note: Following the Prophet ﷺ is the way to Allah's love.
quran.arabic: قُلْ إِن كُنتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ اللَّهَ فَاتَّبِعُونِي يُحْبِبْكُمُ اللَّهُ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ ۗ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ
quran.translation: Say, [O Muḥammad], "If you should love Allāh, then follow me, [so] Allāh will love you and forgive you your sins. And Allāh is Forgiving and Merciful."

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: "When Allah loves a servant, He calls Jibril: Allah loves so-and-so, so love him. Then Jibril loves him and calls out to the people of heaven: Allah loves so-and-so, so love him. Then the people of heaven love him, and acceptance is placed for him on earth."

In a hadith qudsi, Allah says: "My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory on him, and My servant keeps drawing near to Me with voluntary deeds until I love him." Then Allah gives him what he asks and grants him refuge when he seeks it.

scholars.text: Al-Wadud is al-Habib, the Beloved.
Al-Wadud is the One whom His beloved ones love with a love that nothing resembles, just as nothing resembles Him in His Attributes of majesty and beauty, in their meanings and in His actions.
And He, the Exalted, is al-Wadud in the sense that He loves His beloved ones, as He says in 5:54.

notes: Al-Wadud carries both meanings, as al-Sa'di explains: Allah loves His servants, and He is the One they love.
Ahl as-Sunnah affirm Allah's love as a real Attribute: He loves and He is loved, in a way that befits His majesty and is unlike the love of creation. It is not explained away as mere reward or will.

lessons.text: Follow the Prophet ﷺ, for that is the way to Allah's love and forgiveness.
Draw near to Allah first with the obligatory deeds, then with voluntary deeds, until He loves you.
Love Allah and His Messenger ﷺ above all else, and love people for Allah's sake, to taste the sweetness of faith.
After a sin, seek forgiveness and repent, for your Lord is Merciful and Loving.

names.summary: Allah is al-Majid: the Glorious, great and vast in His Attributes. He has every Attribute of perfection in its fullest and most complete form, and He is praised and glorified in His Essence and His Attributes.

quran.note: The angels' words to the household of Ibrahim end with al-Hamid and al-Majid.
quran.arabic: قَالُوا أَتَعْجَبِينَ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ ۖ رَحْمَتُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ عَلَيْكُمْ أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ ۚ إِنَّهُ حَمِيدٌ مَّجِيدٌ
quran.translation: They said, "Are you amazed at the decree of Allāh? May the mercy of Allāh and His blessings be upon you, people of the house. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Honorable."

quran.note: Allah, Owner of the Throne, is described as al-Majid.
quran.arabic: ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ
quran.translation: Honorable Owner of the Throne,

hadith.text: The Companions asked how to send salah upon the Prophet ﷺ, and he taught them: "O Allah, send Your salah upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You sent Your salah upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; You are Praiseworthy, Glorious (Hamid, Majid). O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; You are Praiseworthy, Glorious."
In a hadith qudsi about al-Fatihah, when the servant recites the ayah about the Day of Judgment (1:4), Allah says: "My servant has glorified Me."

scholars.text: He is the Praiseworthy, praised in all His actions and words, and glorified in His Attributes and His Essence.
Majd is the greatness and vastness of the Attributes. He has the Attributes of perfection, and of every Attribute of perfection He has the fullest, most complete and most comprehensive.

notes: This Name, al-Majīd, is established in the Quran and the Sunnah. It is a different word from al-Mājid, which comes later in the famous list.

lessons.text: Send salah upon the Prophet ﷺ in the words he taught, which end by praising Allah as Hamid and Majid.
Recite al-Fatihah with a present heart, for Allah answers each part of it, and when you reach the ayah about the Day of Judgment, He says that His servant has glorified Him.

dua.text: O Allah, send Your salah upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You sent Your salah upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.

names.summary: Al-Ba'ith means the Resurrector. Allah will raise all the dead from their graves for the reckoning, and He is the One who sent the messengers to mankind.
names.established_note: The Quran mentions this as Allah's action (the verb yab'athu, e.g. 22:7), not as a Name, and no authentic hadith names Him al-Ba'ith. Some scholars counted it among the Names, such as al-Khattabi, al-Bayhaqi and Ibn Mandah (as IslamQA 536167 reports), while Ibn Uthaymeen did not include it in the 99 Names he gathered (al-Qawa'id al-Muthla); IslamQA notes that affirming a Name is narrower than affirming an action.

quran.note: The certainty of the Hour and of Allah raising those in the graves (verb form yab'athu).
quran.arabic: وَأَنَّ السَّاعَةَ آتِيَةٌ لَّا رَيْبَ فِيهَا وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَبْعَثُ مَن فِي الْقُبُورِ
quran.translation: And [that they may know] that the Hour is coming - no doubt about it - and that Allāh will resurrect those in the graves.

quran.note: Allah brought some of the Children of Israel back to life after they died (verb form).
quran.arabic: ثُمَّ بَعَثْنَاكُم مِّن بَعْدِ مَوْتِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ
quran.translation: Then We revived you after your death that perhaps you would be grateful.

quran.note: The dead, rising from their graves, ask who raised them (verb form).
quran.arabic: قَالُوا يَا وَيْلَنَا مَن بَعَثَنَا مِن مَّرْقَدِنَا ۜ ۗ هَٰذَا مَا وَعَدَ الرَّحْمَٰنُ وَصَدَقَ الْمُرْسَلُونَ
quran.translation: They will say, "O woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping place?" [The reply will be], "This is what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers told the truth."

quran.note: Allah sent a Messenger among the unlettered people (verb form ba'atha).
quran.arabic: هُوَ الَّذِي بَعَثَ فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ رَسُولًا مِّنْهُمْ يَتْلُو عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتِهِ وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ الْكِتَابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ وَإِن كَانُوا مِن قَبْلُ لَفِي ضَلَالٍ مُّبِينٍ
quran.translation: It is He who has sent among the unlettered [Arabs] a Messenger from themselves reciting to them His verses and purifying them and teaching them the Book [i.e., the Qur’ān] and wisdom [i.e., the sunnah] - although they were before in clear error -

hadith.text: When the Prophet ﷺ wanted to sleep, he placed his right hand under his cheek and said: "O Allah, protect me from Your punishment on the Day You resurrect Your servants."
When he woke up, the Prophet ﷺ would say: "Praise be to Allah, who gave us life after He had caused us to die, and to Him is the rising."
The Prophet ﷺ said: "I have been sent, and the Hour, like these two," and he joined his two fingers.

scholars.text: He will bring them back after they have become decayed remains in their graves, and bring them into being after they were nothing.
There is no disagreement that Allah is the One who sends the messengers to His servants, and the One who raises the bodies on the Day of Calling.
A group of scholars counted al-Ba'ith among Allah's Beautiful Names.
Scholars discuss the affirming of Allah's Names specifically, because affirming the Beautiful Names is a narrower matter than affirming actions.

notes: Among the meanings of ba'th are raising the dead to life and sending the messengers. Both are Allah's actions, and belief in the resurrection is part of faith, as the Prophet ﷺ told Jibril (Sahih al-Bukhari 50).

lessons.text: Before you sleep, ask Allah to protect you from His punishment on the Day He resurrects His servants.
Let sleep and waking remind you of death and the rising, and praise Allah each morning for giving you life again.
Prepare for the Hour, for the Prophet ﷺ was sent close to it.

dua.text: O Allah, protect me from Your punishment on the Day You resurrect Your servants.

names.summary: Allah is ash-Shahid: He witnesses everything, the open and the hidden, with His knowledge, hearing and sight. Nothing anyone says or does escapes Him, and His own testimony is enough.

quran.note: About the mission of the Prophet ﷺ: Allah's own witness is enough.
quran.arabic: مَّا أَصَابَكَ مِنْ حَسَنَةٍ فَمِنَ اللَّهِ ۖ وَمَا أَصَابَكَ مِن سَيِّئَةٍ فَمِن نَّفْسِكَ ۚ وَأَرْسَلْنَاكَ لِلنَّاسِ رَسُولًا ۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا
quran.translation: What comes to you of good is from Allāh, but what comes to you of evil, [O man], is from yourself. And We have sent you, [O Muḥammad], to the people as a messenger, and sufficient is Allāh as Witness.

quran.note: Allah bears witness to what He sent down to the Prophet ﷺ.
quran.arabic: لَّٰكِنِ اللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ بِمَا أَنزَلَ إِلَيْكَ ۖ أَنزَلَهُ بِعِلْمِهِ ۖ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ يَشْهَدُونَ ۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا
quran.translation: But Allāh bears witness to that which He has revealed to you. He has sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness [as well]. And sufficient is Allāh as Witness.

quran.note: The Prophet ﷺ asks people for no reward; Allah witnesses all things.
quran.arabic: قُلْ مَا سَأَلْتُكُم مِّنْ أَجْرٍ فَهُوَ لَكُمْ ۖ إِنْ أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى اللَّهِ ۖ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ
quran.translation: Say, "Whatever payment I might have asked of you - it is yours. My payment is only from Allāh, and He is, over all things, Witness."

quran.note: Allah will judge between all religious groups on the Day of Resurrection.
quran.arabic: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَالَّذِينَ هَادُوا وَالصَّابِئِينَ وَالنَّصَارَىٰ وَالْمَجُوسَ وَالَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ
quran.translation: Indeed, those who have believed and those who were Jews and the Sabeans and the Christians and the Magians and those who associated with Allāh - Allāh will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed Allāh is, over all things, Witness.

quran.note: Allah witnessed all that was done to the believers of the trench.
quran.arabic: الَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۚ وَاللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ
quran.translation: To whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And Allāh, over all things, is Witness.

quran.note: People forget their deeds, but Allah has counted them and witnesses all.
quran.arabic: يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعًا فَيُنَبِّئُهُم بِمَا عَمِلُوا ۚ أَحْصَاهُ اللَّهُ وَنَسُوهُ ۚ وَاللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ
quran.translation: On the Day when Allāh will resurrect them all and inform them of what they did. Allāh had enumerated it, while they forgot it; and Allāh is, over all things, Witness.

hadith.text: On the Day of Sacrifice at Mina, the Prophet ﷺ reminded the people that their lives and their wealth are sacred to one another. Then he asked: "Have I conveyed the message?" and said: "O Allah, bear witness. Let the one who is present inform the one who is absent."

The Prophet ﷺ told of a man from the Children of Israel who asked another man to lend him a thousand dinars. The lender said: "Bring me witnesses." He answered: "Allah is enough as a Witness." The lender said: "Then bring me a guarantor." He answered: "Allah is enough as a Guarantor." The lender accepted, and in the end Allah delivered the money to him on the borrower's behalf.

scholars.text: "He is Witness over all things" means: He knows all matters, including what I tell you about Him sending me to you, and the state that you are in.
Allah is enough as a Witness that He sent you. He is also a Witness between you and them: He knows what you convey to them, and how they turn the truth back out of disbelief and stubbornness.
Allah will repay people for their deeds, which He has preserved, written down and witnessed.
Allah is Witness over all things with His knowledge, His hearing and His sight.

notes: Ash-Shahid carries two meanings in the Quran: Allah sees and knows everything that happens, and Allah bears witness, as He testified to the truth of His Messenger ﷺ and of what He revealed to him (4:79, 4:166).
Ahl as-Sunnah affirm Allah's knowledge, hearing and sight as real Attributes that befit His majesty, unlike those of His creation.

lessons.text: Worship Allah as though you see Him, for even if you do not see Him, He sees you.
What you have forgotten of your deeds, Allah has counted, and He will tell you of it on the Day of Resurrection. Check yourself now.
Be honest in your dealings and keep your trusts. The man who made Allah his Witness kept his word, and Allah fulfilled it for him.
Pass on the truth you have learned, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "Let the one who is present inform the one who is absent."

names.summary: Allah is al-Haqq: the Truth, whose existence is certain and everlasting and whose Names and Attributes are perfect. His word, His promise and His religion are true, and everything worshipped besides Him is false.

quran.note: Allah is the Truth, and all that is called upon besides Him is falsehood.
quran.arabic: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ وَأَنَّ مَا يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ هُوَ الْبَاطِلُ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْكَبِيرُ
quran.translation: That is because Allāh is the True Reality, and that which they call upon other than Him is falsehood, and because Allāh is the Most High, the Grand.

quran.note: Linked with His giving life to the dead and His power over all things.
quran.arabic: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ وَأَنَّهُ يُحْيِي الْمَوْتَىٰ وَأَنَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
quran.translation: That is because Allāh is the True Reality and because He gives life to the dead and because He is over all things competent

quran.note: On the Day of Judgement people will know for certain that Allah is the clear Truth.
quran.arabic: يَوْمَئِذٍ يُوَفِّيهِمُ اللَّهُ دِينَهُمُ الْحَقَّ وَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ الْمُبِينُ
quran.translation: That Day, Allāh will pay them in full their true [i.e., deserved] recompense, and they will know that it is Allāh who is the manifest Truth [i.e., perfect in justice].

quran.note: Allah is exalted, the King, the Truth.
quran.arabic: فَتَعَالَى اللَّهُ الْمَلِكُ الْحَقُّ ۗ وَلَا تَعْجَلْ بِالْقُرْآنِ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُقْضَىٰ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُ ۖ وَقُل رَّبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْمًا
quran.translation: So high [above all] is Allāh, the Sovereign, the Truth. And, [O Muḥammad], do not hasten with [recitation of] the Qur’ān before its revelation is completed to you, and say, "My Lord, increase me in knowledge."

quran.note: After the truth there is nothing but misguidance.
quran.arabic: فَذَٰلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمُ الْحَقُّ ۖ فَمَاذَا بَعْدَ الْحَقِّ إِلَّا الضَّلَالُ ۖ فَأَنَّىٰ تُصْرَفُونَ
quran.translation: For that is Allāh, your Lord, the Truth. And what can be beyond truth except error? So how are you averted?

hadith.text: When the Prophet ﷺ stood to pray at night he would say: "O Allah, to You belongs all praise. You are the Truth, Your promise is true, meeting You is true, Your word is true, Paradise is true, the Fire is true, the prophets are true, Muhammad ﷺ is true, and the Hour is true."
The Prophet ﷺ said that the truest word ever spoken by a poet is the word of Labid: "Truly, everything other than Allah is vain and passing."

scholars.text: Al-Haqq is the One who is firmly established, who has always been and will never cease: the First with nothing before Him, the Last with nothing after Him, perfect in His Names and Attributes.
He is true to His promise: His promise is true, meeting Him is true, His religion is true, and worshipping Him is the truth that benefits and lasts forever.
He is the true deity; no worship is fitting except for Him, because He has the mighty authority. Everything worshipped besides Him is false, because it has no power to harm or to benefit.
Everything is under His dominance, His authority and His greatness. There is no god but Him and no lord besides Him.

notes: Because Allah is the Truth, everything that comes from Him is true: His word, His promise, the meeting with Him, Paradise, the Fire and the Hour. The Prophet ﷺ affirmed all of these together in his night prayer.
Worship directed to anything other than Allah is false, since only He creates, owns and controls all things (22:62).

lessons.text: Direct your worship to Allah alone; anything called upon besides Him can neither harm nor benefit.
Believe firmly in all that Allah has promised: the meeting with Him, Paradise, the Fire and the Hour are all true.
Hold on to the truth once it is clear to you, for after the truth there is only misguidance.

dua.text: O Allah, to You belongs all praise. You are the Truth, Your promise is true, meeting You is true, and Your word is true. O Allah, to You I have submitted, in You I believe, and upon You I rely. (From the night-prayer supplication of the Prophet ﷺ.)

names.summary: Allah is al-Wakil: He has all things in His care, managing the affairs of His creation, providing for them and protecting them night and day. Whoever entrusts his affairs to Him finds Him enough.

quran.note: The believers' answer when they were threatened with a great army.
quran.arabic: الَّذِينَ قَالَ لَهُمُ النَّاسُ إِنَّ النَّاسَ قَدْ جَمَعُوا لَكُمْ فَاخْشَوْهُمْ فَزَادَهُمْ إِيمَانًا وَقَالُوا حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ
quran.translation: Those to whom people [i.e., hypocrites] said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them." But it [merely] increased them in faith, and they said, "Sufficient for us is Allāh, and [He is] the best Disposer of affairs."

quran.note: The Creator of everything has everything in His care.
quran.arabic: ذَٰلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ ۖ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۖ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ فَاعْبُدُوهُ ۚ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَكِيلٌ
quran.translation: That is Allāh, your Lord; there is no deity except Him, the Creator of all things, so worship Him. And He is Disposer of all things.

quran.note: The Lord of the east and the west; take Him alone as the One you rely on.
quran.arabic: رَّبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَاتَّخِذْهُ وَكِيلًا
quran.translation: [He is] the Lord of the East and the West; there is no deity except Him, so take Him as Disposer of [your] affairs.

quran.note: The Prophet ﷺ is told to put his trust in Allah.
quran.arabic: وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ ۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِاللَّهِ وَكِيلًا
quran.translation: And rely upon Allāh; and sufficient is Allāh as Disposer of affairs.

quran.note: Allah is enough for whoever relies on Him.
quran.arabic: وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَحْتَسِبُ ۚ وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بَالِغُ أَمْرِهِ ۚ قَدْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدْرًا
quran.translation: And will provide for him from where he does not expect. And whoever relies upon Allāh - then He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allāh will accomplish His purpose. Allāh has already set for everything a [decreed] extent.

hadith.text: Ibn Abbas said: "Allah is enough for us, and He is the best One to rely on" was said by Ibrahim when he was thrown into the fire, and it was said by Muhammad ﷺ when people told the believers that a great army had gathered against them.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "Seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise without reckoning. They are those who do not ask others for ruqyah, who do not take bad omens, and who put their trust in their Lord."

scholars.text: Take Him as your Wakil means: take Him as the One who guards and manages all of your affairs.
He is the Guardian and Watcher over everything. He manages all that is besides Him, provides for them and protects them by night and by day.
When the believers were frightened with the great number of their enemies, they paid no attention to it. Instead, they relied on Allah and sought His help.
These words were the last thing Ibrahim said when he was thrown into the fire.
scholars.book: Reported by al-Bukhari, quoted by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir 3:173

notes: The Quran tells us both that Allah has everything in His care (6:102) and that the believers should take Him as the One they rely on (73:9). Trust in Allah is an act of the heart that the believer brings to every matter.
Ibrahim and the Prophet ﷺ both met the greatest dangers with the same words of trust, and Allah protected them.

lessons.text: In fear or hardship, say what Ibrahim and Muhammad ﷺ said: "Allah is enough for us, and He is the best One to rely on."
Rely on Allah with all your heart; whoever relies on Him, He is enough for him.
Complete trust in your Lord is one of the qualities of those who enter Paradise without reckoning.

dua.text: Allah is enough for us, and He is the best One to rely on (Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal-Wakil).

names.summary: Allah is al-Qawiyy: all strength belongs to Him. By His strength He created everything, nothing can overpower Him, and no creature has any power or strength except by Him.

quran.note: Those who worship others have not valued Allah as He deserves.
quran.arabic: مَا قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَقَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ
quran.translation: They have not appraised Allāh with true appraisal. Indeed, Allāh is Powerful and Exalted in Might.

quran.note: Allah is kind to His servants and provides for whom He wills.
quran.arabic: اللَّهُ لَطِيفٌ بِعِبَادِهِ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَاءُ ۖ وَهُوَ الْقَوِيُّ الْعَزِيزُ
quran.translation: Allāh is Subtle with His servants; He gives provision to whom He wills. And He is the Powerful, the Exalted in Might.

quran.note: Allah has decreed that He and His messengers will prevail.
quran.arabic: كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَأَغْلِبَنَّ أَنَا وَرُسُلِي ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ
quran.translation: Allāh has written [i.e., decreed], "I will surely overcome, I and My messengers." Indeed, Allāh is Powerful and Exalted in Might.

quran.note: Allah supports whoever supports His religion.
quran.arabic: الَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا مِن دِيَارِهِم بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ إِلَّا أَن يَقُولُوا رَبُّنَا اللَّهُ ۗ وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ اللَّهِ النَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍ لَّهُدِّمَتْ صَوَامِعُ وَبِيَعٌ وَصَلَوَاتٌ وَمَسَاجِدُ يُذْكَرُ فِيهَا اسْمُ اللَّهِ كَثِيرًا ۗ وَلَيَنصُرَنَّ اللَّهُ مَن يَنصُرُهُ ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَقَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ
quran.translation: [They are] those who have been evicted from their homes without right - only because they say, "Our Lord is Allāh." And were it not that Allāh checks the people, some by means of others, there would have been demolished monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which the name of Allāh is much mentioned [i.e., praised]. And Allāh will surely support those who support Him [i.e., His cause]. Indeed, Allāh is Powerful and Exalted in Might.

quran.note: Allah saved Salih and the believers when His punishment came.
quran.arabic: فَلَمَّا جَاءَ أَمْرُنَا نَجَّيْنَا صَالِحًا وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ مِّنَّا وَمِنْ خِزْيِ يَوْمِئِذٍ ۗ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ الْقَوِيُّ الْعَزِيزُ
quran.translation: So when Our command came, We saved Ṣāliḥ and those who believed with him, by mercy from Us, and [saved them] from the disgrace of that day. Indeed, it is your Lord who is the Powerful, the Exalted in Might.

quran.note: On the Day of Judgement the wrongdoers will see that all strength belongs to Allah.
quran.arabic: وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَن يَتَّخِذُ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ أَندَادًا يُحِبُّونَهُمْ كَحُبِّ اللَّهِ ۖ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَشَدُّ حُبًّا لِّلَّهِ ۗ وَلَوْ يَرَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا إِذْ يَرَوْنَ الْعَذَابَ أَنَّ الْقُوَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعَذَابِ
quran.translation: And [yet], among the people are those who take other than Allāh as equals [to Him]. They love them as they [should] love Allāh. But those who believe are stronger in love for Allāh. And if only they who have wronged would consider [that] when they see the punishment, [they will be certain] that all power belongs to Allāh and that Allāh is severe in punishment.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ told his Companions, who were raising their voices in takbir, that they were not calling on one who is deaf or absent but on One who hears and sees. Then he told Abu Musa to say "La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah" (there is no power and no strength except by Allah), and said that it is one of the treasures of Paradise.

scholars.text: He is the Strong, who created everything by His power and His strength.
He is Almighty: He has overcome everything, subdued it and prevailed over it.
He has all strength, so no created being has any power or strength except by Him, and all things submit to Him.

notes: Allah's strength is perfect and is never touched by weakness or tiredness: He created the heavens and the earth and all between them in six days, and no weariness touched Him (50:38).
In the Quran al-Qawiyy is most often joined with al-Aziz, the Almighty (22:74, 42:19, 58:21): His strength is complete and no one can overcome Him.

lessons.text: Say often "La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah", admitting that you have no strength except by Allah; it is a treasure of Paradise.
The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer. Be keen on what benefits you, seek Allah's help and do not give up.
Do not be frightened by the strength of the wrongdoers; Allah has decreed that He and His messengers will prevail.

dua.text: There is no power and no strength except by Allah (La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah).

names.summary: Allah is al-Matin: the Firm, whose strength is intense and complete. His power never weakens and nothing can resist it; whatever He wills happens, and whatever He does not will does not happen.

quran.note: Allah created jinn and mankind to worship Him; He needs nothing from them, for He is the Provider. The only place the Name occurs.
quran.arabic: وَمَا خَلَقْتُ الْجِنَّ وَالْإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ ۝ مَا أُرِيدُ مِنْهُم مِّن رِّزْقٍ وَمَا أُرِيدُ أَن يُطْعِمُونِ ۝ إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الرَّزَّاقُ ذُو الْقُوَّةِ الْمَتِينُ
quran.translation: And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want them to feed Me. Indeed, it is Allāh who is the [continual] Provider, the firm possessor of strength.

quran.note: Allah gives the deniers time, and His plan against them is firm (matin).
quran.arabic: وَأُمْلِي لَهُمْ ۚ إِنَّ كَيْدِي مَتِينٌ
quran.translation: And I will give them time. Indeed, My plan is firm.

quran.note: On the Day of Judgement the wrongdoers will see that all strength belongs to Allah.
quran.arabic: وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَن يَتَّخِذُ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ أَندَادًا يُحِبُّونَهُمْ كَحُبِّ اللَّهِ ۖ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَشَدُّ حُبًّا لِّلَّهِ ۗ وَلَوْ يَرَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا إِذْ يَرَوْنَ الْعَذَابَ أَنَّ الْقُوَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعَذَابِ
quran.translation: And [yet], among the people are those who take other than Allāh as equals [to Him]. They love them as they [should] love Allāh. But those who believe are stronger in love for Allāh. And if only they who have wronged would consider [that] when they see the punishment, [they will be certain] that all power belongs to Allāh and that Allāh is severe in punishment.

hadith.text: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught him to recite this ayah as: "Indeed, I am the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm (al-Matin)."

scholars.text: "Possessor of strength, al-Matin" means the Possessor of strength who is intense in it. Ibn Abbas said: al-Matin means ash-Shadid, the Intensely Strong.
Most reciters read al-Matin as a description of Allah Himself, and this is the reading he chose, because the reciters agree on it.
He is the One who has all strength and power, by which He brought into being the great bodies of the heavens and the earth.
Whatever Allah wills happens, and whatever He does not will does not happen.

notes: Al-Matin comes once in the Quran, straight after ar-Razzaq (the Provider) and "Possessor of strength": the One who provides for all creation does so by a strength that never runs out, and He needs nothing from His servants (51:56-58).
Al-Matin and al-Qawiyy are close in meaning; at-Tabari, reporting Ibn Abbas, explains al-Matin as intense, firm strength.

lessons.text: You were created to worship Allah. He needs no provision from you, so worship Him sincerely and ask Him alone for your provision.
Do not be deceived when those who deny Allah's signs are given time; His plan is firm.
Love Allah above everything else. Those who love others as they love Allah will see on the Day of Judgement that all strength belongs to Allah.

names.summary: Allah is al-Waliyy: the Protecting Friend who takes charge of His servants. He cares for all creation through His management and decree, and He gives the believers special care, guiding them out of darkness into light and helping them in all their affairs.
names.established_note: This is al-Waliyy (الولي), established in the Quran in 42:9 and 42:28. It is a different word from al-Wali (الوالي, the Governor), which appears separately in the famous list.

quran.note: The polytheists took other protectors, but Allah alone is the true Protector, who gives life to the dead.
quran.arabic: أَمِ اتَّخَذُوا مِن دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَاءَ ۖ فَاللَّهُ هُوَ الْوَلِيُّ وَهُوَ يُحْيِي الْمَوْتَىٰ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
quran.translation: Or have they taken protectors [or allies] besides Him? But Allāh - He is the Protector, and He gives life to the dead, and He is over all things competent.

quran.note: Allah sends down rain after people had lost hope.
quran.arabic: وَهُوَ الَّذِي يُنَزِّلُ الْغَيْثَ مِن بَعْدِ مَا قَنَطُوا وَيَنشُرُ رَحْمَتَهُ ۚ وَهُوَ الْوَلِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ
quran.translation: And it is He who sends down the rain after they had despaired and spreads His mercy. And He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy.

quran.note: Allah brings the believers out of darkness into light.
quran.arabic: اللَّهُ وَلِيُّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يُخْرِجُهُم مِّنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى النُّورِ ۖ وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَوْلِيَاؤُهُمُ الطَّاغُوتُ يُخْرِجُونَهُم مِّنَ النُّورِ إِلَى الظُّلُمَاتِ ۗ أُولَٰئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ ۖ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ
quran.translation: Allāh is the Ally of those who believe. He brings them out from darknesses into the light. And those who disbelieve - their allies are ṭāghūt. They take them out of the light into darknesses. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide eternally therein.

quran.note: Allah is the Protector of the believers.
quran.arabic: إِنَّ أَوْلَى النَّاسِ بِإِبْرَاهِيمَ لَلَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُ وَهَٰذَا النَّبِيُّ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ۗ وَاللَّهُ وَلِيُّ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
quran.translation: Indeed, the most worthy of Abraham among the people are those who followed him [in submission to Allāh] and this prophet [i.e., Muḥammad (ﷺ)] and those who believe [in his message]. And Allāh is the Ally of the believers.

quran.note: Allah, who sent down the Book, takes care of the righteous.
quran.arabic: إِنَّ وَلِيِّيَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي نَزَّلَ الْكِتَابَ ۖ وَهُوَ يَتَوَلَّى الصَّالِحِينَ
quran.translation: Indeed, my protector is Allāh, who has sent down the Book; and He is an ally to the righteous.

quran.note: The friends (awliya') of Allah are those who believe and are mindful of Him.
quran.arabic: أَلَا إِنَّ أَوْلِيَاءَ اللَّهِ لَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ ۝ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَكَانُوا يَتَّقُونَ
quran.translation: Unquestionably, [for] the allies of Allāh there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve - Those who believed and were fearing Allāh.

hadith.text: Among the supplications of the Prophet ﷺ: "O Allah, give my soul its taqwa and purify it, for You are the best to purify it. You are its Protector (Waliyy) and its Master."

The Prophet ﷺ taught al-Hasan ibn Ali to say in the witr: "O Allah, guide me among those You have guided, grant me well-being among those You have granted well-being, and take care of me among those You take care of." And in it: "Whoever You befriend is never humbled."

scholars.text: Allah is al-Waliyy whom His servant takes as his Protector by worshipping Him, obeying Him and drawing near to Him in every way he can.

He takes care of all His servants in general through His management and His decree. And He takes special care of the believers: He brings them out of darkness into light, nurtures them with His kindness and helps them in all their affairs.
Al-Waliyy is the One who takes charge of His servants with every kind of care and management, and looks after the good of their religion and their worldly life.
Allah rebukes the polytheists for taking other gods, and tells that He alone is the true Protector, the only One who deserves worship.

notes: As al-Sa'di explains, Allah's care is of two kinds: a general care for all creation through His management and decree, and a special care for the believers, whom He guides, nurtures and helps.
The way to Allah's special friendship is faith and taqwa (10:62-63), beginning with the obligations and then the voluntary deeds (Sahih al-Bukhari 6502).

lessons.text: Take Allah as your Protector and do not look for protection from anyone besides Him.

Draw near to Allah first with the obligations and then with voluntary deeds. In a hadith qudsi Allah says that His servant keeps drawing near to Him in this way until He loves him, and that whoever shows enmity to a friend of His, He declares war on him.
Ask Allah to take care of you, for whoever He befriends is never humbled.

dua.text: O Allah, give my soul its taqwa and purify it, for You are the best to purify it. You are its Protector and its Master.

names.summary: Allah is al-Hamid: the Praiseworthy, praised in His essence, His Names and Attributes, and in all His actions, words, laws and decrees. Everything He creates, commands and judges deserves praise.

quran.note: The Quran leads to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.
quran.arabic: الر ۚ كِتَابٌ أَنزَلْنَاهُ إِلَيْكَ لِتُخْرِجَ النَّاسَ مِنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى النُّورِ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ
quran.translation: Alif, Lām, Rā. [This is] a Book which We have revealed to you, [O Muḥammad], that you might bring mankind out of darknesses into the light by permission of their Lord - to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy -

quran.note: Gratitude benefits only the grateful; Allah is free of need and praiseworthy.
quran.arabic: وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا لُقْمَانَ الْحِكْمَةَ أَنِ اشْكُرْ لِلَّهِ ۚ وَمَن يَشْكُرْ فَإِنَّمَا يَشْكُرُ لِنَفْسِهِ ۖ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٌ
quran.translation: And We had certainly given Luqmān wisdom [and said], "Be grateful to Allāh." And whoever is grateful is grateful for [the benefit of] himself. And whoever denies [His favor] - then indeed, Allāh is Free of need and Praiseworthy.

quran.note: People are in need of Allah, and He is free of need and praiseworthy.
quran.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ أَنتُمُ الْفُقَرَاءُ إِلَى اللَّهِ ۖ وَاللَّهُ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ
quran.translation: O mankind, you are those in need of Allāh, while Allāh is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.

quran.note: Paired with al-Waliyy after the mention of rain.
quran.arabic: وَهُوَ الَّذِي يُنَزِّلُ الْغَيْثَ مِن بَعْدِ مَا قَنَطُوا وَيَنشُرُ رَحْمَتَهُ ۚ وَهُوَ الْوَلِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ
quran.translation: And it is He who sends down the rain after they had despaired and spreads His mercy. And He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy.

quran.note: The angels' words to the household of Ibrahim.
quran.arabic: قَالُوا أَتَعْجَبِينَ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ ۖ رَحْمَتُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ عَلَيْكُمْ أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ ۚ إِنَّهُ حَمِيدٌ مَّجِيدٌ
quran.translation: They said, "Are you amazed at the decree of Allāh? May the mercy of Allāh and His blessings be upon you, people of the house. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Honorable."

quran.note: The Quran is sent down from One who is Wise and Praiseworthy.
quran.arabic: لَّا يَأْتِيهِ الْبَاطِلُ مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَلَا مِنْ خَلْفِهِ ۖ تَنزِيلٌ مِّنْ حَكِيمٍ حَمِيدٍ
quran.translation: Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it; [it is] a revelation from a [Lord who is] Wise and Praiseworthy.

hadith.text: Ka'b ibn Ujrah said that the Companions asked how to send prayers upon the Prophet ﷺ, and he taught them: "O Allah, send prayers upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You sent prayers upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; You are Praiseworthy, Glorious (Hamidun Majid)."

scholars.text: He is al-Hamid: the One who is praised in all His actions, His words, His law and His decree.
He is free of need of all His creation, while all His creation is in need of Him, and His bounty is vast and what He has never runs out.
He is praiseworthy in His essence and in His attributes. Every one of His attributes deserves the most complete praise, because they are attributes of greatness and perfection.
He is praised for everything He does and creates, for everything He commands and forbids, and for every judgement He makes among His servants in this world and the next.
He is praised for His care and management, for the perfection He has, and for the many kinds of favour He has brought to His creation.

notes: Al-Hamid is often joined with al-Ghani, the Free of need (31:12, 31:26, 35:15). Allah does not need our praise or our charity; when He commands them, the benefit returns to us.
The Quran opens with praise of Allah (1:2), and the Prophet ﷺ taught us to end our salah upon him by calling on Allah as Hamidun Majid.

lessons.text: Praise Allah for every blessing, even a single meal or drink; Allah is pleased with the servant who eats or drinks and then praises Him for it.
Saying "al-hamdu lillah" fills the scale of good deeds.
Your gratitude benefits only you; if anyone is ungrateful, Allah is still free of need and praiseworthy.

dua.text: O Allah, send prayers upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent prayers upon Ibrahim and upon the family of Ibrahim; You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.

names.meaning: The One Who Counts All Things
names.summary: Allah counts all things: He knows the number of every creature and keeps an exact record of every deed, small or great, even what people themselves forget. The Quran affirms this as His action, but al-Muhsi itself is not established as one of His Names.
names.established_note: IslamQA (answer 520630) explains that "al-Muhsi" does not come as a Name in the Quran or the authentic Sunnah; it comes only as a verb (Allah "counted" all things), and the Tirmidhi list that contains it is weak. So we affirm Allah's counting as His action and attribute, without calling al-Muhsi one of His Names.

quran.note: Allah encompasses what is with His messengers and has counted everything (verb form: ahsa).
quran.arabic: لِّيَعْلَمَ أَن قَدْ أَبْلَغُوا رِسَالَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ وَأَحَاطَ بِمَا لَدَيْهِمْ وَأَحْصَىٰ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عَدَدًا
quran.translation: That he [i.e., Muḥammad (ﷺ)] may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord; and He has encompassed whatever is with them and has enumerated all things in number.

quran.note: Every creature in the heavens and the earth is counted and numbered by Him.
quran.arabic: لَّقَدْ أَحْصَاهُمْ وَعَدَّهُمْ عَدًّا
quran.translation: He has enumerated them and counted them a [full] counting.

quran.note: Everything is recorded in a clear register.
quran.arabic: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِي الْمَوْتَىٰ وَنَكْتُبُ مَا قَدَّمُوا وَآثَارَهُمْ ۚ وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَاهُ فِي إِمَامٍ مُّبِينٍ
quran.translation: Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life and record what they have put forth and what they left behind, and all things We have enumerated in a clear register.

quran.note: People forget their deeds, but Allah has counted them.
quran.arabic: يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعًا فَيُنَبِّئُهُم بِمَا عَمِلُوا ۚ أَحْصَاهُ اللَّهُ وَنَسُوهُ ۚ وَاللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ
quran.translation: On the Day when Allāh will resurrect them all and inform them of what they did. Allāh had enumerated it, while they forgot it; and Allāh is, over all things, Witness.

quran.note: The record of deeds leaves out nothing, small or great.
quran.arabic: وَوُضِعَ الْكِتَابُ فَتَرَى الْمُجْرِمِينَ مُشْفِقِينَ مِمَّا فِيهِ وَيَقُولُونَ يَا وَيْلَتَنَا مَالِ هَٰذَا الْكِتَابِ لَا يُغَادِرُ صَغِيرَةً وَلَا كَبِيرَةً إِلَّا أَحْصَاهَا ۚ وَوَجَدُوا مَا عَمِلُوا حَاضِرًا ۗ وَلَا يَظْلِمُ رَبُّكَ أَحَدًا
quran.translation: And the record [of deeds] will be placed [open], and you will see the criminals fearful of that within it, and they will say, "Oh, woe to us! What is this book that leaves nothing small or great except that it has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present [before them]. And your Lord does injustice to no one.

hadith.text: In a hadith qudsi, Allah says: "O My servants, it is only your deeds that I count for you, and then I will repay you for them in full. So whoever finds good, let him praise Allah, and whoever finds something else, let him blame no one but himself."
The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah has ninety-nine Names, one hundred less one. Whoever counts them (ahsaha) will enter Paradise."

scholars.text: Al-Muhsi has not come in the form of a Name in the Quran or the authentic Sunnah. It is affirmed only as a verb.
He is the One who has counted everything with His knowledge. Nothing escapes His knowledge, and He counts the movements, breaths and deeds of His creatures.
scholars.book: Sha'n ad-Du'a 1/79, quoted by IslamQA, answer 520630

scholars.text: He knows their number from the time He created them until the Day of Resurrection: male and female, young and old.

Allah will tell them of the good and evil they did, because He knew it and wrote it in the Preserved Tablet, and He ordered the noble guardian angels to record it. The doers forgot what they did, but Allah counted it.

notes: Allah's counting is part of His perfect knowledge: nothing is too small for it, and nothing is too many for it.
The same word is used for the servant in the authentic hadith about the ninety-nine Names: whoever "counts" them enters Paradise.

lessons.text: Take account of yourself today, before the Day when the record leaves out nothing, small or great.
Your deeds are counted and will be repaid in full; whoever finds good should praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise should blame only himself.
Learn Allah's Names: the Prophet ﷺ promised Paradise to whoever counts the ninety-nine Names.

names.summary: Allah alone began creation from nothing, and He alone will bring it back after death; this meaning is always explained together with al-Mu'id. The Quran affirms beginning creation as Allah's action, but al-Mubdi' itself is not established as one of His Names.
names.established_note: The Quran mentions beginning creation only as Allah's action (He "begins" creation, 85:13, 10:4), never as the Name al-Mubdi'. IslamQA (answer 48964, referring to Ibn Uthaymeen's al-Qawa'id al-Muthla) explains that what comes only as a description or report is affirmed of Allah but not taken as a Name, and the Tirmidhi list that contains al-Mubdi' is weak (IslamQA 72318).

quran.note: Allah begins and restores (verb forms: yubdi'u, yu'idu).
quran.arabic: إِنَّهُ هُوَ يُبْدِئُ وَيُعِيدُ
quran.translation: Indeed, it is He who originates [creation] and repeats.

quran.note: All return to Allah, who began creation, so that He may repay with justice.
quran.arabic: إِلَيْهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ جَمِيعًا ۖ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقًّا ۚ إِنَّهُ يَبْدَأُ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ لِيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ بِالْقِسْطِ ۚ وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَهُمْ شَرَابٌ مِّنْ حَمِيمٍ وَعَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْفُرُونَ
quran.translation: To Him is your return all together. [It is] the promise of Allāh [which is] truth. Indeed, He begins the [process of] creation and then repeats it that He may reward those who have believed and done righteous deeds, in justice. But those who disbelieved will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment for what they used to deny.

quran.note: Restoring creation is even easier for Him; His is the highest description.
quran.arabic: وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَبْدَأُ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَيْهِ ۚ وَلَهُ الْمَثَلُ الْأَعْلَىٰ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ
quran.translation: And it is He who begins creation; then He repeats it, and that is [even] easier for Him. To Him belongs the highest description [i.e., attribute] in the heavens and earth. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

quran.note: People are told to travel and look at how He began creation.
quran.arabic: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا كَيْفَ يُبْدِئُ اللَّهُ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ ۚ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ ۝ قُلْ سِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَانظُرُوا كَيْفَ بَدَأَ الْخَلْقَ ۚ ثُمَّ اللَّهُ يُنشِئُ النَّشْأَةَ الْآخِرَةَ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
quran.translation: Have they not considered how Allāh begins creation and then repeats it? Indeed that, for Allāh, is easy. Say, [O Muḥammad], "Travel through the land and observe how He began creation. Then Allāh will produce the final creation [i.e., development]. Indeed Allāh, over all things, is competent."

quran.note: None of the false partners can begin creation or restore it.
quran.arabic: قُلْ هَلْ مِن شُرَكَائِكُم مَّن يَبْدَأُ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ ۚ قُلِ اللَّهُ يَبْدَأُ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ ۖ فَأَنَّىٰ تُؤْفَكُونَ
quran.translation: Say, "Are there of your 'partners' any who begins creation and then repeats it?" Say, "Allāh begins creation and then repeats it, so how are you deluded?"

hadith.text: In a hadith qudsi, Allah says: "The son of Adam denied Me, and he had no right to do so. His denial is his saying that I will not bring him back as I began him, yet the first creation is no easier for Me than bringing him back."

scholars.text: He alone begins creation and brings it back; no one shares with Him in that.
Through His strength and complete power He begins creation and brings it back as He began it, with nothing to stop or resist Him.

Allah's Names are known only from revelation. What comes in the Quran and Sunnah only as a description or a report of His actions is affirmed, but no Name is taken from it; for example, al-Ja'i (the One who comes) is not counted among His Names.
scholars.book: IslamQA, answer 48964, referring to Ibn Uthaymeen's al-Qawa'id al-Muthla

scholars.text: The hadith in at-Tirmidhi that lists the ninety-nine Names one by one is weak. At-Tirmidhi himself, Ibn Hajar and Ibn Taymiyyah judged it so.

notes: Al-Mubdi' and al-Mu'id belong together: the One who began creation is the One who will bring it back, and the Quran uses the first creation as proof of the second (29:19-20, 30:27).
Ahl as-Sunnah affirm everything Allah said about His actions, but they call Him only by the Names He gave Himself.

lessons.text: Reflect on how Allah began your own creation and the creation around you; it is proof that He will bring you back.
Believe firmly in the resurrection; Allah counts denying it as denying Him.
Worship only the One who begins and restores creation, for none of the false gods can do either.

names.summary: Allah will bring His creation back after death, just as He began it, so that He may repay every soul for its deeds. This meaning is explained together with al-Mubdi'; both are affirmed as Allah's actions in the Quran, but al-Mu'id itself is not established as one of His Names.
names.established_note: Restoring creation comes in the Quran only as Allah's action (He "restores" it, 85:13, 30:27), never as the Name al-Mu'id. IslamQA (answer 48964, referring to Ibn Uthaymeen's al-Qawa'id al-Muthla) explains that what comes only as a description or report is affirmed of Allah but not taken as a Name, and the Tirmidhi list that contains al-Mu'id is weak (IslamQA 72318).

quran.note: Allah begins and restores (verb forms: yubdi'u, yu'idu).
quran.arabic: إِنَّهُ هُوَ يُبْدِئُ وَيُعِيدُ
quran.translation: Indeed, it is He who originates [creation] and repeats.

quran.note: Bringing creation back is even easier for Him.
quran.arabic: وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَبْدَأُ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَيْهِ ۚ وَلَهُ الْمَثَلُ الْأَعْلَىٰ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ
quran.translation: And it is He who begins creation; then He repeats it, and that is [even] easier for Him. To Him belongs the highest description [i.e., attribute] in the heavens and earth. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

quran.note: On the Day the sky is rolled up, creation is brought back as it first began.
quran.arabic: يَوْمَ نَطْوِي السَّمَاءَ كَطَيِّ السِّجِلِّ لِلْكُتُبِ ۚ كَمَا بَدَأْنَا أَوَّلَ خَلْقٍ نُّعِيدُهُ ۚ وَعْدًا عَلَيْنَا ۚ إِنَّا كُنَّا فَاعِلِينَ
quran.translation: The Day when We will fold the heaven like the folding of a [written] sheet for the records. As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. [That is] a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We will do it.

quran.note: Allah begins creation, restores it, and then all return to Him.
quran.arabic: اللَّهُ يَبْدَأُ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ
quran.translation: Allāh begins creation; then He will repeat it; then to Him you will be returned.

quran.note: Creation is restored so that Allah may repay with justice.
quran.arabic: إِلَيْهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ جَمِيعًا ۖ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقًّا ۚ إِنَّهُ يَبْدَأُ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ لِيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ بِالْقِسْطِ ۚ وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَهُمْ شَرَابٌ مِّنْ حَمِيمٍ وَعَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْفُرُونَ
quran.translation: To Him is your return all together. [It is] the promise of Allāh [which is] truth. Indeed, He begins the [process of] creation and then repeats it that He may reward those who have believed and done righteous deeds, in justice. But those who disbelieved will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment for what they used to deny.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: "You will be gathered barefoot, naked and uncircumcised." Then he recited 21:104, about Allah bringing back creation as He began it.

In a hadith qudsi, Allah says: "The son of Adam denied Me, and he had no right to do so. His denial is his saying that I will not bring him back as I began him, yet the first creation is no easier for Me than bringing him back."

scholars.text: Through His strength and complete power He begins creation and brings it back as He began it, with nothing to stop or resist Him.
"It is easier for Him" means: it is simpler for Him.
Bringing back is easier for Him than beginning.
The One who brought creation into being and gave them commands and prohibitions will bring them back after their death and repay them for the deeds they did in this world.

Allah's Names are known only from revelation. What comes in the Quran and Sunnah only as a description or a report of His actions is affirmed, but no Name is taken from it; for example, al-Ja'i (the One who comes) is not counted among His Names.
scholars.book: IslamQA, answer 48964, referring to Ibn Uthaymeen's al-Qawa'id al-Muthla

notes: Mujahid explained "easier for Him" in 30:27 as: bringing back is easier than beginning. In the hadith qudsi Allah makes clear that bringing a person back is no harder for Him than creating him the first time (Sahih al-Bukhari 4974).
The purpose of bringing creation back is justice: every soul will be repaid for what it did (10:4).

lessons.text: Prepare for the Day you will be brought back to Allah and repaid for your deeds with justice.
Remember that you will be gathered barefoot and naked, as you were first created; only your deeds will go with you.
Bringing you back is easy for Allah, so let no doubt about the resurrection enter your heart.

names.summary: Allah gives life: He brought every living thing into being, revives the dead earth with rain, and will raise the dead on the Day of Resurrection. The Quran describes Him as the Giver of life to the dead, but al-Muhyi itself is not firmly established as one of His Names.
names.established_note: The Quran describes Allah as "Muhyi al-Mawta" (the Giver of life to the dead, 30:50, 41:39), but the single Name "al-Muhyi" comes only in the weak Tirmidhi list (IslamQA 72318), and Dr. Muhammad al-Hamud an-Najdi (an-Nahj al-Asma) says that al-Muhyi and al-Mumit are not among Allah's Names because they come as His actions. So giving life is affirmed as Allah's action and description, without listing al-Muhyi as a confirmed Name.

quran.note: After rain revives the dead earth: the same One gives life to the dead (Muhyi al-Mawta).
quran.arabic: فَانظُرْ إِلَىٰ آثَارِ رَحْمَتِ اللَّهِ كَيْفَ يُحْيِي الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا ۚ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ لَمُحْيِي الْمَوْتَىٰ ۖ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
quran.translation: So observe the effects of the mercy of Allāh - how He gives life to the earth after its lifelessness. Indeed, that [same one] will give life to the dead, and He is over all things competent.

quran.note: The dry earth stirs with rain; He who revived it will revive the dead.
quran.arabic: وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ أَنَّكَ تَرَى الْأَرْضَ خَاشِعَةً فَإِذَا أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْهَا الْمَاءَ اهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ ۚ إِنَّ الَّذِي أَحْيَاهَا لَمُحْيِي الْمَوْتَىٰ ۚ إِنَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
quran.translation: And of His signs is that you see the earth stilled, but when We send down upon it rain, it quivers and grows. Indeed, He who has given it life is the Giver of Life to the dead. Indeed, He is over all things competent.

quran.note: Every stage of life and death belongs to Allah.
quran.arabic: كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَكُنتُمْ أَمْوَاتًا فَأَحْيَاكُمْ ۖ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يُحْيِيكُمْ ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ
quran.translation: How can you disbelieve in Allāh when you were lifeless and He brought you to life; then He will cause you to die, then He will bring you [back] to life, and then to Him you will be returned.

quran.note: Giving life and causing death are part of His dominion.
quran.arabic: لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۖ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ ۖ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
quran.translation: His is the dominion of the heavens and earth. He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things competent.

quran.note: The true Protector is the One who gives life to the dead.
quran.arabic: أَمِ اتَّخَذُوا مِن دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَاءَ ۖ فَاللَّهُ هُوَ الْوَلِيُّ وَهُوَ يُحْيِي الْمَوْتَىٰ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
quran.translation: Or have they taken protectors [or allies] besides Him? But Allāh - He is the Protector, and He gives life to the dead, and He is over all things competent.

quran.note: Ibrahim's argument with the king who claimed to give life and death.
quran.arabic: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِي حَاجَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ فِي رَبِّهِ أَنْ آتَاهُ اللَّهُ الْمُلْكَ إِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ رَبِّيَ الَّذِي يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ قَالَ أَنَا أُحْيِي وَأُمِيتُ ۖ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْتِي بِالشَّمْسِ مِنَ الْمَشْرِقِ فَأْتِ بِهَا مِنَ الْمَغْرِبِ فَبُهِتَ الَّذِي كَفَرَ ۗ وَاللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ
quran.translation: Have you not considered the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord [merely] because Allāh had given him kingship? When Abraham said, "My Lord is the one who gives life and causes death," he said, "I give life and cause death." Abraham said, "Indeed, Allāh brings up the sun from the east, so bring it up from the west." So the disbeliever was overwhelmed [by astonishment], and Allāh does not guide the wrongdoing people.

hadith.text: When the Prophet ﷺ lay down to sleep he would say: "In Your Name I die and I live." When he woke up he would say: "All praise is for Allah, who gave us life after He had caused us to die, and to Him is the rising."

The Prophet ﷺ said: "None of you should wish for death because of a harm that has befallen him. If he must, let him say: O Allah, keep me alive as long as life is better for me, and take me when death is better for me."

scholars.text: "That One" is the One who revived the earth after its death. Nothing can resist His power, even what is beyond the power of His creatures, too subtle for their understanding and bewildering to their minds.
The ayah points to His power to bring back the dead. Before the rain, the earth was barren with no plants on it; it was dead.
He is the One able to give life to the dead, and He has power over all things.
"He created death and life" means: He decreed for His servants that He would give them life and then cause them to die.

notes: Giving life and causing death are mentioned together throughout the Quran (2:28, 57:2, 53:44). Both belong to Allah alone, which is why Ibrahim used them as proof against the king who claimed them (2:258).

The Quran mentions several kinds of life that Allah gives: the first creation, reviving the dead earth with rain, and raising the dead (2:28, 30:50). The Prophet ﷺ praised Allah each morning for giving life again after sleep.

lessons.text: When you see rain bring dead land back to life, remember the resurrection.
Begin each day by praising Allah, who gave you life again after sleep.
Ask Allah to keep you alive only as long as life is good for you.

dua.text: All praise is for Allah, who gave us life after He had caused us to die, and to Him is the rising.

names.summary: Allah alone causes death: every soul dies only by His permission, at the term He has written, and by His wisdom. This is explained together with His giving of life; the Quran affirms it as His action, but al-Mumit itself is not established as one of His Names.
names.established_note: Allah's causing death comes in the Quran and Sunnah only in verb form (yumitu, amata: 57:2, 53:44), never as the Name al-Mumit. IslamQA (answer 48964, referring to Ibn Uthaymeen's al-Qawa'id al-Muthla) explains that what comes only as a description or report is affirmed of Allah but not taken as a Name, and the Tirmidhi list that contains al-Mumit is weak (IslamQA 72318).

quran.note: He alone causes death and gives life (verb forms: amata, ahya).
quran.arabic: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَمَاتَ وَأَحْيَا
quran.translation: And that it is He who causes death and gives life

quran.note: Giving life and causing death are part of His dominion.
quran.arabic: لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۖ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ ۖ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
quran.translation: His is the dominion of the heavens and earth. He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things competent.

quran.note: Death and life were created as a test of who is best in deeds.
quran.arabic: الَّذِي خَلَقَ الْمَوْتَ وَالْحَيَاةَ لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ أَيُّكُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًا ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْغَفُورُ
quran.translation: [He] who created death and life to test you [as to] which of you is best in deed - and He is the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving -

quran.note: No soul dies except by Allah's permission, at a written term.
quran.arabic: وَمَا كَانَ لِنَفْسٍ أَن تَمُوتَ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ كِتَابًا مُّؤَجَّلًا ۗ وَمَن يُرِدْ ثَوَابَ الدُّنْيَا نُؤْتِهِ مِنْهَا وَمَن يُرِدْ ثَوَابَ الْآخِرَةِ نُؤْتِهِ مِنْهَا ۚ وَسَنَجْزِي الشَّاكِرِينَ
quran.translation: And it is not [possible] for one to die except by permission of Allāh at a decree determined. And whoever desires the reward of this world - We will give him thereof; and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter - We will give him thereof. And We will reward the grateful.

quran.note: He gave you life, will cause you to die, and will give you life again.
quran.arabic: وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَحْيَاكُمْ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يُحْيِيكُمْ ۗ إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ لَكَفُورٌ
quran.translation: And He is the one who gave you life; then He causes you to die and then will [again] give you life. Indeed, mankind is ungrateful.

quran.note: Allah takes the souls at death and in sleep.
quran.arabic: اللَّهُ يَتَوَفَّى الْأَنفُسَ حِينَ مَوْتِهَا وَالَّتِي لَمْ تَمُتْ فِي مَنَامِهَا ۖ فَيُمْسِكُ الَّتِي قَضَىٰ عَلَيْهَا الْمَوْتَ وَيُرْسِلُ الْأُخْرَىٰ إِلَىٰ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى ۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
quran.translation: Allāh takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die [He takes] during their sleep. Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death and releases the others for a specified term. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.

hadith.text: When the Prophet ﷺ lay down to sleep he would say: "In Your Name I die and I live." When he woke up he would say: "All praise is for Allah, who gave us life after He had caused us to die, and to Him is the rising."

scholars.text: He alone brings into being and brings to an end.
"He causes death and gives life" is like His saying: "who created death and life" (67:2).
He decreed for His servants that He would give them life and then cause them to die, to test them. The best deed is the one that is most sincere and most correct.

Allah's Names are known only from revelation. What comes in the Quran and Sunnah only as a description or a report of His actions is affirmed, but no Name is taken from it; for example, al-Ja'i (the One who comes) is not counted among His Names.
