scholars.book: IslamQA, answer 48964, referring to Ibn Uthaymeen's al-Qawa'id al-Muthla

notes: Death is part of Allah's wise decree, not something outside His control: He created death as He created life, to test people (67:2), and after death everyone returns to Him (22:66).
Causing death and giving life are always understood together. Ahl as-Sunnah affirm both as Allah's actions, exactly as He described Himself, while calling Him only by the Names He gave Himself.

lessons.text: Every soul dies only by Allah's permission at a written term, so trust His decree and prepare for that day.
Use your life for good deeds, for life and death were created to test who is best in deeds.
Do not wish for death because of hardship; ask Allah instead for what is best for you.
Live in this world like a stranger or a traveller, as the Prophet ﷺ taught, and, as Ibn Umar advised, take from your life for your death.

dua.text: O Allah, keep me alive as long as life is better for me, and take me when death is better for me.

names.summary: Allah is al-Hayy: the Ever-Living, whose life is perfect and complete. His life did not begin after death and will never be followed by death, and every attribute of perfection belongs to that perfect life.

quran.note: Ayat al-Kursi, the greatest ayah of the Quran, which brings al-Hayy and al-Qayyum together.
quran.arabic: اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ ۚ لَّهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ ۗ مَن ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِندَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَئُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ
quran.translation: Allāh - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursī extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.

quran.note: The opening of Surah Al Imran, where the two Names come together again.
quran.arabic: اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ
quran.translation: Allāh - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining.

quran.note: On the Day of Judgement every face is humbled before al-Hayy, al-Qayyum.
quran.arabic: وَعَنَتِ الْوُجُوهُ لِلْحَيِّ الْقَيُّومِ ۖ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنْ حَمَلَ ظُلْمًا
quran.translation: And [all] faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. And he will have failed who carries injustice.

quran.note: The command to put one's trust in the Ever-Living who never dies.
quran.arabic: وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى الْحَيِّ الَّذِي لَا يَمُوتُ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِهِ ۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِهِ بِذُنُوبِ عِبَادِهِ خَبِيرًا
quran.translation: And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die, and exalt [Allāh] with His praise. And sufficient is He to be, with the sins of His servants, [fully] Aware -

quran.note: He is al-Hayy, so call on Him with sincere devotion.
quran.arabic: هُوَ الْحَيُّ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَادْعُوهُ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ ۗ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
quran.translation: He is the Ever-Living; there is no deity except Him, so call upon Him, [being] sincere to Him in religion. [All] praise is [due] to Allāh, Lord of the worlds.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ asked Ubayy ibn Ka'b which ayah in the Book of Allah is the greatest. Ubayy answered with Ayat al-Kursi (2:255). The Prophet ﷺ struck him on the chest and said: "May knowledge be a joy for you, Abu al-Mundhir."

Anas reported that a man made du'a after his prayer, praising Allah and calling on Him by His Names, and said in it: "O Ever-Living, O Self-Sustaining." The Prophet ﷺ said: "He has called on Allah by His great Name, by which, when He is called upon, He answers, and when He is asked, He gives."
Asma' bint Yazid reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The greatest Name of Allah is in these two ayahs," and he named 2:163 and the opening of Surah Al Imran (3:1-2), which contains al-Hayy, al-Qayyum.
The Prophet ﷺ used to say: "I seek refuge in Your might, there is no god but You, the One who does not die, while the jinn and mankind die."

scholars.text: Al-Hayy means He is living in Himself and never dies, and al-Qayyum means He keeps everything else in existence.
Al-Hayy is the One who has perfect life, a life that includes all the attributes of His essence, such as hearing, seeing, knowledge and power.
His life did not begin after death, and death will never come to Him after life.
Because of this, some careful scholars said that al-Hayy and al-Qayyum are the greatest Name: when Allah is called by it He answers, and when He is asked by it He gives.

notes: Al-Hayy and al-Qayyum come together three times in the Quran (2:255, 3:2, 20:111). Al-Sa'di explains that al-Hayy includes all the attributes of Allah's essence and al-Qayyum includes all His actions.
Ahl as-Sunnah affirm life as a real attribute of Allah, perfect and befitting His majesty. It is unlike the life of creation, which is given to it, weak, and ends in death.

lessons.text: Put your trust in the Ever-Living who never dies, not in people, who will all die.
When something distresses you, call on Allah by these two Names, as the Prophet ﷺ did.

dua.text: O Ever-Living, O Self-Sustaining, by Your mercy I call for help.

names.summary: Allah is al-Qayyum: He exists by Himself and needs no one, and He keeps everything else in existence. He creates, provides, protects and manages all things, and nothing could stand for a moment without Him.

quran.note: Ayat al-Kursi, which joins this Name with Allah being free of drowsiness, sleep and tiredness.
quran.arabic: اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ ۚ لَّهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ ۗ مَن ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِندَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَئُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ
quran.translation: Allāh - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursī extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.

quran.note: The opening of Surah Al Imran.
quran.arabic: اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ
quran.translation: Allāh - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining.

quran.note: Every face is humbled before al-Hayy, al-Qayyum.
quran.arabic: وَعَنَتِ الْوُجُوهُ لِلْحَيِّ الْقَيُّومِ ۖ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنْ حَمَلَ ظُلْمًا
quran.translation: And [all] faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. And he will have failed who carries injustice.

quran.note: The related word qa'im: Allah stands over every soul and what it earns.
quran.arabic: أَفَمَنْ هُوَ قَائِمٌ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ ۗ وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكَاءَ قُلْ سَمُّوهُمْ ۚ أَمْ تُنَبِّئُونَهُ بِمَا لَا يَعْلَمُ فِي الْأَرْضِ أَم بِظَاهِرٍ مِّنَ الْقَوْلِ ۗ بَلْ زُيِّنَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مَكْرُهُمْ وَصُدُّوا عَنِ السَّبِيلِ ۗ وَمَن يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُ مِنْ هَادٍ
quran.translation: Then is He who is a maintainer of every soul, [knowing] what it has earned, [like any other]? But to Allāh they have attributed partners. Say, "Name them. Or do you inform Him of that which He knows not upon the earth or of what is apparent [i.e., alleged] of speech?" Rather, their [own] plan has been made attractive to those who disbelieve, and they have been averted from the way. And whomever Allāh sends astray - there will be for him no guide.

quran.note: The heavens and the earth stand by His command; Ibn Kathir cites it under this Name.
quran.arabic: وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ أَن تَقُومَ السَّمَاءُ وَالْأَرْضُ بِأَمْرِهِ ۚ ثُمَّ إِذَا دَعَاكُمْ دَعْوَةً مِّنَ الْأَرْضِ إِذَا أَنتُمْ تَخْرُجُونَ
quran.translation: And of His signs is that the heaven and earth stand [i.e., remain] by His command. Then when He calls you with a [single] call from the earth, immediately you will come forth.

quran.note: Allah holds the heavens and the earth in place.
quran.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُمْسِكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ أَن تَزُولَا ۚ وَلَئِن زَالَتَا إِنْ أَمْسَكَهُمَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ مِّن بَعْدِهِ ۚ إِنَّهُ كَانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورًا
quran.translation: Indeed, Allāh holds the heavens and the earth, lest they cease. And if they should cease, no one could hold them [in place] after Him. Indeed, He is Forbearing and Forgiving.

hadith.text: Ibn Abbas reported that when the Prophet ﷺ stood for the night prayer he would say: "O Allah, to You belongs all praise. You are the Sustainer (Qayyim) of the heavens and the earth and all who are in them."
Abu Musa said the Prophet ﷺ stood among them and said: "Allah does not sleep, and it is not fitting for Him to sleep. He lowers the scale and raises it."
A man ended his du'a with "O Ever-Living, O Self-Sustaining," and the Prophet ﷺ said he had called on Allah by His great Name, by which He answers when called and gives when asked.

scholars.text: Al-Qayyum is the One who exists by Himself and keeps all others in existence.

All that Allah does as He wills, such as rising over the Throne, descending, speaking, creating, providing, causing death and giving life, and every other kind of managing: all of this is part of Allah being al-Qayyum.
Everything that exists is in need of Him while He has no need of it, and nothing can stand without His command.
Part of His perfect sustaining is that neither drowsiness nor sleep ever comes over Him.
Al-Qayyum is the One who takes care of everything: He guards it, provides for it, manages it and directs it as He wills and loves.
These two noble Names, al-Hayy and al-Qayyum, point to all the other beautiful Names.

notes: Allah's being al-Qayyum has two sides: He stands by Himself and needs no one, and He keeps up everyone and everything else.
Al-Hayy and al-Qayyum are always explained together; see al-Hayy for the hadiths about the greatest Name.

lessons.text: Seek forgiveness with these Names: whoever says "I seek the forgiveness of Allah, there is no god but He, al-Hayy, al-Qayyum, and I turn to Him in repentance" is forgiven, even if he had fled from the battlefield.
Allah stands over every soul and what it earns, so be mindful of Him in private and in public.
Never feel alone with your needs: the One who manages the heavens and the earth never sleeps.

dua.text: I seek the forgiveness of Allah, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, and I turn to Him in repentance.

names.summary: Al-Wajid is not confirmed as one of Allah's Names, but its meaning is true: Allah is the Rich who has everything and lacks nothing, and all that He gives never lessens what He has.
names.established_note: Ibn al-Qayyim said Allah is called al-Wajid only in the hadith that lists the 99 Names, and that the correct view is that this list is not the words of the Prophet ﷺ, although the meaning is correct (Madarij as-Salikin 3/384, quoted by IslamQA 265776). So it is explained here as a true description of Allah, not as a confirmed Name.

quran.note: People are in need of Allah, and He is al-Ghani, the Rich, free of all need.
quran.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ أَنتُمُ الْفُقَرَاءُ إِلَى اللَّهِ ۖ وَاللَّهُ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ
quran.translation: O mankind, you are those in need of Allāh, while Allāh is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.

quran.note: Allah uses the verb wajada (found) of Himself, and tells how He gave His Messenger ﷺ shelter, guidance and wealth.
quran.arabic: أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيمًا فَآوَىٰ ۝ وَوَجَدَكَ ضَالًّا فَهَدَىٰ ۝ وَوَجَدَكَ عَائِلًا فَأَغْنَىٰ
quran.translation: Did He not find you an orphan and give [you] refuge? And He found you lost and guided [you], And He found you poor and made [you] self-sufficient.

hadith.text: In a hadith qudsi, Allah says: "O My servants, if the first and the last of you, of mankind and jinn, stood on one plain and asked Me, and I gave every person what he asked for, that would not decrease what I have, except as a needle decreases the sea when it is dipped into it."

The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah's Right Hand is full; spending night and day does not lessen it. Do you see what He has spent since He created the heavens and the earth? It has not lessened what is in His Right Hand."

scholars.text: Allah is called al-Wajid only in the hadith that lists the beautiful Names, and the correct view is that this list is not the words of the Prophet ﷺ.
Its meaning is correct, because Allah is the Possessor of wujd, which is wealth and freedom from need.
Al-Wajid is the Rich. Wujd means wealth, and the Arabs say of a man: he is rich, wajid.
scholars.book: Tafsir Asma' Allah al-Husna, p. 57, quoted by IslamQA 265776

scholars.text: He is the Rich with a complete and absolute richness, after which there is no poverty.

notes: IslamQA explains that al-Wajid means al-Ghani, the Rich, so its meaning is covered by the confirmed Name al-Ghani (35:15).
Allah's Right Hand, mentioned in the hadith, is affirmed as real and befitting His majesty, without likening it to the hands of creation and without asking how.

lessons.text: Ask Allah for all your needs, big and small, because what He has never runs out.
Remember your need of Allah: all people are poor before Him, and He alone is Rich and Praiseworthy.

dua.text: O Allah, I ask You for guidance, piety, chastity and freedom from need.

names.summary: Al-Majid (الماجد), spelled this way, is not firmly established as a Name, but its meaning is true: Allah is al-Majid (المجيد), the Most Glorious, whose attributes are vast and great, and who is glorified in His essence and His attributes.
names.established_note: Scholars differ: Ibn Mandah (at-Tawhid) listed al-Majid among the Names, and Shaykh al-Fawzan counted it as a Name from the hadith "that is because I am Generous, Majid" (at-Tirmidhi 2495, called hasan by at-Tirmidhi and judged weak by al-Albani), while Shaykh Alawi as-Saqqaf said it is not one of His Names and IslamQA (201274) judged it safer not to use it as a Name. Its meaning is firmly established through the Quranic Name al-Majid spelled مجيد (11:73).

quran.note: The angels' words to the household of Ibrahim, describing Allah as Hamid and Majid (the related form مجيد).
quran.arabic: قَالُوا أَتَعْجَبِينَ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ ۖ رَحْمَتُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ عَلَيْكُمْ أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ ۚ إِنَّهُ حَمِيدٌ مَّجِيدٌ
quran.translation: They said, "Are you amazed at the decree of Allāh? May the mercy of Allāh and His blessings be upon you, people of the house. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Honorable."

quran.note: In the reading of Hafs, al-Majid (مجيد) here describes Allah; Ibn Kathir says both readings give a correct meaning.
quran.arabic: ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ
quran.translation: Honorable Owner of the Throne,

quran.note: When the servant recites this ayah, Allah says: "My servant has glorified Me" (Sahih Muslim 395).
quran.arabic: مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ
quran.translation: Sovereign of the Day of Recompense.

hadith.text: Ka'b ibn Ujrah reported that the Prophet ﷺ taught them to send blessings on him: "O Allah, send prayers on Muhammad and on the family of Muhammad, as You sent prayers on Ibrahim and on the family of Ibrahim; You are Hamid, Majid. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; You are Hamid, Majid."
In a hadith qudsi about al-Fatihah, when the servant recites its fourth ayah (1:4), Allah says: "My servant has glorified Me."

scholars.text: Al-Majid (spelled الماجد) is not one of the Names of Allah.
scholars.book: Sifat Allah al-Waridah fil-Kitab was-Sunnah, p. 196, quoted by IslamQA 201274

scholars.text: No authentic hadith from the Prophet ﷺ names the ninety-nine Names one by one.
The safer course is not to use al-Majid as a Name or to name someone Abd al-Majid, although this is a matter of ijtihad where differing is acceptable.
Majd is the greatness and vastness of the attributes. Allah has every attribute of perfection, and of each one He has the most complete, perfect and all-embracing.
Al-Majid in 85:15 has two readings: with damma it describes the Lord, and with kasra it describes the Throne, and both meanings are correct.

notes: الماجد and المجيد come from the same root, majd: glory, honour and greatness of attributes. The confirmed form in the Quran and Sunnah is المجيد.

lessons.text: Recite al-Fatihah with a present heart, glorifying Allah, for He answers: "My servant has glorified Me."
Send prayers on the Prophet ﷺ in the words he taught, which end by praising Allah as Hamid and Majid.
Call on Allah by His beautiful Names, and keep away from deviating in them by keeping to the Names that are confirmed.

dua.text: O Allah, send prayers on Muhammad and on the family of Muhammad, as You sent prayers on Ibrahim and on the family of Ibrahim; You are Hamid, Majid. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; You are Hamid, Majid.

names.summary: Allah is al-Wahid: the One, alone in His essence, His Names, His Attributes and His actions. He has no partner, no equal and nothing like Him, and He alone deserves to be worshipped.

quran.note: Allah, the Creator of all things, is al-Wahid, al-Qahhar.
quran.arabic: قُلْ مَن رَّبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ قُلِ اللَّهُ ۚ قُلْ أَفَاتَّخَذْتُم مِّن دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَاءَ لَا يَمْلِكُونَ لِأَنفُسِهِمْ نَفْعًا وَلَا ضَرًّا ۚ قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمَىٰ وَالْبَصِيرُ أَمْ هَلْ تَسْتَوِي الظُّلُمَاتُ وَالنُّورُ ۗ أَمْ جَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكَاءَ خَلَقُوا كَخَلْقِهِ فَتَشَابَهَ الْخَلْقُ عَلَيْهِمْ ۚ قُلِ اللَّهُ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُوَ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ
quran.translation: Say, "Who is Lord of the heavens and earth?" Say, "Allāh." Say, "Have you then taken besides Him allies not possessing [even] for themselves any benefit or any harm?" Say, "Is the blind equivalent to the seeing? Or is darkness equivalent to light? Or have they attributed to Allāh partners who created like His creation so that the creation [of each] seemed similar to them?" Say, "Allāh is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Prevailing."

quran.note: On the Day the earth is changed, all creatures come out before al-Wahid, al-Qahhar.
quran.arabic: يَوْمَ تُبَدَّلُ الْأَرْضُ غَيْرَ الْأَرْضِ وَالسَّمَاوَاتُ ۖ وَبَرَزُوا لِلَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ
quran.translation: [It will be] on the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth, and the heavens [as well], and they [i.e., all creatures] will come out before Allāh, the One, the Prevailing,

quran.note: Allah is far above having a son; He is al-Wahid, al-Qahhar.
quran.arabic: لَّوْ أَرَادَ اللَّهُ أَن يَتَّخِذَ وَلَدًا لَّاصْطَفَىٰ مِمَّا يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَاءُ ۚ سُبْحَانَهُ ۖ هُوَ اللَّهُ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ
quran.translation: If Allāh had intended to take a son, He could have chosen from what He creates whatever He willed. Exalted is He; He is Allāh, the One, the Prevailing.

quran.note: On the Last Day all sovereignty belongs to Allah, al-Wahid, al-Qahhar.
quran.arabic: يَوْمَ هُم بَارِزُونَ ۖ لَا يَخْفَىٰ عَلَى اللَّهِ مِنْهُمْ شَيْءٌ ۚ لِّمَنِ الْمُلْكُ الْيَوْمَ ۖ لِلَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ
quran.translation: The Day they come forth nothing concerning them will be concealed from Allāh. To whom belongs [all] sovereignty this Day? To Allāh, the One, the Prevailing.

quran.note: Yusuf asks his prison companions whether many lords are better than Allah, al-Wahid, al-Qahhar.
quran.arabic: يَا صَاحِبَيِ السِّجْنِ أَأَرْبَابٌ مُّتَفَرِّقُونَ خَيْرٌ أَمِ اللَّهُ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ
quran.translation: O [my] two companions of prison, are separate lords better or Allāh, the One, the Prevailing?

quran.note: Your god is only one; this is one of the two ayahs linked to the greatest Name (Sunan Abi Dawud 1496).
quran.arabic: وَإِلَٰهُكُمْ إِلَٰهٌ وَاحِدٌ ۖ لَّا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الرَّحْمَٰنُ الرَّحِيمُ
quran.translation: And your god is one God. There is no deity [worthy of worship] except Him, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

hadith.text: Mihjan ibn al-Adra' reported that the Prophet ﷺ heard a man say at the end of his prayer: "O Allah, I ask You, O Allah, as You are al-Wahid, al-Ahad, as-Samad, who neither begot nor was begotten, and to whom no one is equal, to forgive my sins; You are the Forgiving, the Merciful." The Prophet ﷺ said three times: "He has been forgiven."
The Prophet ﷺ said: "On the Day of Resurrection Allah will grasp the earth, and the heavens will be in His Right Hand, then He will say: I am the King."

scholars.text: He is al-Wahid in His essence, in His Names, in His Attributes and in His actions, and nothing resembles Him or equals Him in any of these.
His oneness and His all-subduing power go together: the One must be the Subduer, and the Subduer must be the One, and this rules out any partner in any way.
Allah tells us that He alone is god, with no partner and no equal; He is Allah, al-Wahid, al-Ahad, al-Fard, as-Samad.

notes: Al-Wahid and al-Ahad both tell us that Allah is One, with nothing like Him in any way; see al-Ahad for Surah al-Ikhlas. In the Quran al-Wahid is joined with al-Qahhar six times (12:39, 13:16, 14:48, 38:65, 39:4, 40:16).
His oneness means more than being one in number: He is alone in lordship, alone in deserving worship, and alone in His Names and Attributes.

lessons.text: Give all your worship to the One. Many false lords can never compare with Allah, al-Wahid, al-Qahhar.
Hold firmly to tawhid until death: "Whoever dies knowing that there is no god but Allah will enter Paradise."
Ask forgiveness by mentioning His oneness, as the man did whom the Prophet ﷺ said was forgiven.

dua.text: O Allah, I ask You, O Allah, as You are al-Wahid, al-Ahad, as-Samad, who neither begot nor was begotten, and to whom no one is equal, to forgive my sins; You are the Forgiving, the Merciful.

names.summary: Allah is al-Ahad: alone in His essence, His Names, His Attributes and His actions, with nothing like Him in any way.

quran.note: The opening of Surah al-Ikhlas.
quran.arabic: قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ
quran.translation: Say, "He is Allāh, [who is] One,

quran.note: There is none comparable to Him.
quran.arabic: وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ
quran.translation: Nor is there to Him any equivalent."

hadith.text: In a hadith qudsi, Allah says that the son of Adam insults Him by claiming that Allah has taken a son, "while I am al-Ahad, as-Samad. I neither begot nor was I begotten, and there is none equal to Me."

The Prophet ﷺ heard a man pray: "O Allah, I ask You, bearing witness that You are Allah, there is no god but You, al-Ahad, as-Samad, who neither begot nor was begotten, and to whom no one is equal." He said the man had asked Allah by the Name with which, when He is asked, He gives, and when He is called upon, He answers.
About Surah al-Ikhlas the Prophet ﷺ said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, it equals a third of the Quran."

scholars.text: He is the One, al-Ahad, who has no equal and no helper, no rival, no likeness and no counterpart. This word is not used in an affirmative sentence for anyone but Allah, because He alone is perfect in all His attributes and actions.
Oneness belongs to Him alone. He is al-Ahad, unique in His perfection, to whom belong the most beautiful Names and the perfect, highest Attributes.

lessons.text: Worship Allah alone and compare nothing to Him, for there is none comparable to Him.
Loving Allah's Names brings His love: a Companion used to end his recitation in prayer with Surah al-Ikhlas because it describes ar-Rahman, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "Tell him that Allah loves him."

dua.text: O Allah, I ask You, bearing witness that You are Allah, there is no god but You, al-Ahad, as-Samad, who neither begot nor was begotten, and to whom no one is equal.

names.summary: Allah is as-Samad: the perfect Master to whom all of creation turns in every need, while He Himself needs no one.

quran.note: Surah al-Ikhlas.
quran.arabic: اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ
quran.translation: Allāh, the Eternal Refuge.

quran.note: People are in need of Allah, and Allah is free of need.
quran.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ أَنتُمُ الْفُقَرَاءُ إِلَى اللَّهِ ۖ وَاللَّهُ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ
quran.translation: O mankind, you are those in need of Allāh, while Allāh is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.

hadith.text: In a hadith qudsi, Allah says: "I am al-Ahad, as-Samad. I neither begot nor was I begotten, and there is none equal to Me."
The man who called on Allah as "al-Ahad, as-Samad" was told by the Prophet ﷺ that he had asked by the Name with which Allah gives when He is asked.

scholars.text: As-Samad is the One to whom all creatures turn with their needs and their requests.
In another report: He is the Master whose mastery is complete, perfect in His nobility, greatness, forbearance, knowledge and wisdom.
He is the One who remains after His creation, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, who never ceases.
Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and others said: He is the One who has no hollow inside Him.
All of these meanings are correct, and they are all attributes of our Lord, the Mighty and Majestic.
scholars.book: Kitab as-Sunnah, quoted by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir 112:2

scholars.text: As-Samad is the One sought in every need. Everyone in the heavens and on the earth is in complete need of Him and asks Him for what they need, because He is perfect in all His attributes.

lessons.text: "When you ask, ask Allah; and when you seek help, seek help from Allah."
Turn to Allah first in every need, big or small, because all of creation needs Him and He needs no one.

dua.text: O Allah, I ask You, bearing witness that You are Allah, there is no god but You, al-Ahad, as-Samad, who neither begot nor was begotten, and to whom no one is equal.

names.summary: Allah is al-Qadir: the Able, whose power is complete. Nothing in the heavens or on earth can escape Him or defeat Him; He created everything, He will bring the dead back to life, and He punishes and rewards as He wills.

quran.note: Allah is described as al-Qadir, able to send punishment from every direction.
quran.arabic: قُلْ هُوَ الْقَادِرُ عَلَىٰ أَن يَبْعَثَ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابًا مِّن فَوْقِكُمْ أَوْ مِن تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِكُمْ أَوْ يَلْبِسَكُمْ شِيَعًا وَيُذِيقَ بَعْضَكُم بَأْسَ بَعْضٍ ۗ انظُرْ كَيْفَ نُصَرِّفُ الْآيَاتِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَفْقَهُونَ
quran.translation: Say, "He is the [one] Able to send upon you affliction from above you or from beneath your feet or to confuse you [so you become] sects and make you taste the violence of one another." Look how We diversify the signs that they might understand.

quran.note: The One who created the heavens and the earth is able to create people like them again.
quran.arabic: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّ اللَّهَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ قَادِرٌ عَلَىٰ أَن يَخْلُقَ مِثْلَهُمْ وَجَعَلَ لَهُمْ أَجَلًا لَّا رَيْبَ فِيهِ فَأَبَى الظَّالِمُونَ إِلَّا كُفُورًا
quran.translation: Do they not see that Allāh, who created the heavens and earth, is [the one] Able to create the likes of them? And He has appointed for them a term, about which there is no doubt. But the wrongdoers refuse except disbelief.

quran.note: A question that proves His power to bring the dead back to life.
quran.arabic: أَلَيْسَ ذَٰلِكَ بِقَادِرٍ عَلَىٰ أَن يُحْيِيَ الْمَوْتَىٰ
quran.translation: Is not that [Creator] Able to give life to the dead?

quran.note: He is able to bring man back after death.
quran.arabic: إِنَّهُ عَلَىٰ رَجْعِهِ لَقَادِرٌ
quran.translation: Indeed, He [i.e., Allāh], to return him [to life], is Able.

hadith.text: About the last man to enter Paradise, the Prophet ﷺ said that Allah asks him: "Would it please you if I gave you the world and the like of it with it?" The man asks whether Allah is mocking him, and Allah says: "I am not mocking you, but I am able to do whatever I will."

Abu Mas'ud was beating his slave when he heard a voice behind him: "Know, Abu Mas'ud!" It was the Prophet ﷺ, and he threw the whip from his hand. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Know, Abu Mas'ud, that Allah has more power over you than you have over this boy." Abu Mas'ud said: "I will never beat a slave after this."

Uthman ibn Abi al-As complained of a pain in his body. The Prophet ﷺ told him to put his hand on the place of pain, say "Bismillah" three times, and say seven times: "I seek refuge in Allah and His power from the evil of what I feel and what I fear."

scholars.text: He is able to send punishment upon you from every direction.
He is able to do all of that, so beware of staying on disobedience to Him.
Allah is al-Qadir, able to do whatever He wills; nothing can ever defeat Him, and nothing He seeks ever escapes Him.
scholars.book: Tafsir Asma' Allah al-Husna by az-Zajjaj, p. 59

scholars.text: The One who created man and moved him through all these stages: yes, He has power over all things.

notes: Three Names affirm Allah's power: al-Qadir, al-Qadeer (القدير) and al-Muqtadir. Al-Qadeer is the form found most often in the Quran, and al-Muqtadir is the strongest in meaning.
Allah's power is real and complete. It covers everything, and nothing in the heavens or on earth can ever defeat Him (35:44).

lessons.text: Do not misuse your power over those under you, because Allah's power over you is greater.
When you are in pain, put your hand on it and seek refuge in Allah's power, as the Prophet ﷺ taught.
Be certain of the resurrection: the One who created you the first time is able to bring you back.

dua.text: I seek refuge in Allah and His power from the evil of what I feel and what I fear.

names.summary: Allah is al-Muqtadir: the All-Powerful, whose power is complete and without limit. The Name is a stronger form of al-Qadir. He seizes those who deny His signs with mighty power, and He honours the righteous in His presence.

quran.note: Pharaoh's people denied all the signs and were seized by the Mighty, the All-Powerful.
quran.arabic: كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا كُلِّهَا فَأَخَذْنَاهُمْ أَخْذَ عَزِيزٍ مُّقْتَدِرٍ
quran.translation: They denied Our signs, all of them, so We seized them with a seizure of one Exalted in Might and Perfect in Ability.

quran.note: The reward of the righteous: an honoured seat near the All-Powerful King.
quran.arabic: فِي مَقْعَدِ صِدْقٍ عِندَ مَلِيكٍ مُّقْتَدِرٍ
quran.translation: In a seat of honor near a Sovereign, Perfect in Ability.

quran.note: The parable of this world ends by stating that Allah has full power over all things.
quran.arabic: وَاضْرِبْ لَهُم مَّثَلَ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا كَمَاءٍ أَنزَلْنَاهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ فَاخْتَلَطَ بِهِ نَبَاتُ الْأَرْضِ فَأَصْبَحَ هَشِيمًا تَذْرُوهُ الرِّيَاحُ ۗ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُّقْتَدِرًا
quran.translation: And present to them the example of the life of this world, [its being] like rain which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it and [then] it becomes dry remnants, scattered by the winds. And Allāh is ever, over all things, Perfect in Ability.

quran.note: Allah has full power over those who deny.
quran.arabic: أَوْ نُرِيَنَّكَ الَّذِي وَعَدْنَاهُمْ فَإِنَّا عَلَيْهِم مُّقْتَدِرُونَ
quran.translation: Or whether [or not] We show you that which We have promised them, indeed, We are Perfect in Ability.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ told of a man who had wronged himself greatly. Before he died he told his sons to burn his body and scatter the ashes. Allah commanded the earth: "Gather what you hold of him," and it did, and he stood before Allah. Allah asked him why he did it, and he said: "Out of fear of You, my Lord." And Allah forgave him.
The Prophet ﷺ said: "On the Day of Resurrection Allah will grasp the earth, and the heavens will be in His Right Hand, then He will say: I am the King."

scholars.text: In the presence of the Great King, the Creator of all things who sets the measure of everything, and who is able to do whatever He wills of all that they ask for and desire.
He has power over this state and over that state, meaning the growing and the withering of the plant in the parable.
Al-Muqtadir is a stronger and fuller way of describing power. In Arabic, added letters in a word add to its meaning.
scholars.book: Tafsir Asma' Allah al-Husna by az-Zajjaj, p. 59

scholars.text: The word al-Muqtadir is formed from qudrah (power), but iqtidar is more emphatic and more general, because it implies power without any restriction.

notes: Allah's Right Hand in the hadith is affirmed as real and befitting His majesty, without likening it to creation and without asking how.

lessons.text: Do not be fooled by this world: it turns green and then dries up, and Allah has power over both states.
Fear the way Allah seized those who denied His signs, and hope for the honoured seat of the righteous near the All-Powerful King.
Never lose hope in Allah: the man who feared Him was gathered by His power and forgiven by His mercy.

dua.text: O Allah, by Your knowledge of the unseen and Your power over creation, keep me alive as long as You know that life is better for me, and take my soul when You know that death is better for me.

names.summary: Allah is al-Muqaddim: the One who brings forward whatever and whoever He wills, in creation, in rank and in time, by His knowledge and wisdom. This Name is mentioned together with al-Mu'akhkhir, the One who puts back.

quran.note: An example of His giving precedence: Allah raised some messengers above others in rank.
quran.arabic: تِلْكَ الرُّسُلُ فَضَّلْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ ۘ مِّنْهُم مَّن كَلَّمَ اللَّهُ ۖ وَرَفَعَ بَعْضَهُمْ دَرَجَاتٍ ۚ وَآتَيْنَا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ الْبَيِّنَاتِ وَأَيَّدْنَاهُ بِرُوحِ الْقُدُسِ ۗ وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ مَا اقْتَتَلَ الَّذِينَ مِن بَعْدِهِم مِّن بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْهُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ وَلَٰكِنِ اخْتَلَفُوا فَمِنْهُم مَّنْ آمَنَ وَمِنْهُم مَّن كَفَرَ ۚ وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ مَا اقْتَتَلُوا وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَفْعَلُ مَا يُرِيدُ
quran.translation: Those messengers - some of them We caused to exceed others. Among them were those to whom Allāh spoke, and He raised some of them in degree. And We gave Jesus, the son of Mary, clear proofs, and We supported him with the Pure Spirit [i.e., Gabriel]. If Allāh had willed, those [generations] succeeding them would not have fought each other after the clear proofs had come to them. But they differed, and some of them believed and some of them disbelieved. And if Allāh had willed, they would not have fought each other, but Allāh does what He intends.

quran.note: Allah uses the related verb qaddama of Himself: He had sent the warning ahead.
quran.arabic: قَالَ لَا تَخْتَصِمُوا لَدَيَّ وَقَدْ قَدَّمْتُ إِلَيْكُم بِالْوَعِيدِ
quran.translation: [Allāh] will say, "Do not dispute before Me, while I had already presented to you the threat [i.e., warning].

quran.note: When people's term comes, they cannot put it back or bring it forward by an hour.
quran.arabic: وَلَوْ يُؤَاخِذُ اللَّهُ النَّاسَ بِظُلْمِهِم مَّا تَرَكَ عَلَيْهَا مِن دَابَّةٍ وَلَٰكِن يُؤَخِّرُهُمْ إِلَىٰ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى ۖ فَإِذَا جَاءَ أَجَلُهُمْ لَا يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ سَاعَةً ۖ وَلَا يَسْتَقْدِمُونَ
quran.translation: And if Allāh were to impose blame on the people for their wrongdoing, He would not have left upon it [i.e., the earth] any creature, but He defers them for a specified term. And when their term has come, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede [it].

hadith.text: Ibn Abbas reported that in the du'a of his night prayer the Prophet ﷺ said: "You are al-Muqaddim and You are al-Mu'akhkhir; there is no god but You."

Ali reported that between the tashahhud and the taslim the Prophet ﷺ would ask Allah to forgive what he had sent before and left behind, hidden and open, and end with: "You are al-Muqaddim and You are al-Mu'akhkhir; there is no god but You."

Abu Musa al-Ash'ari reported a du'a of the Prophet ﷺ asking forgiveness for his sins, earlier and later, hidden and open, which ends: "You are al-Muqaddim, You are al-Mu'akhkhir, and You have power over all things."

scholars.text: Al-Muqaddim is the One who puts things in their proper places: He brings forward what He wills of them and puts back what He wills.
No one can bring forward what He has put back, and no one can put back what He has brought forward. Mentioning these two Names together is better than separating them.
Allah brings forward whatever should be brought forward, in His rulings and in His actions, as He loves and in the way He loves.
scholars.book: IslamQA, answer 11366 (from Sharh Asma' Allah al-Husna by Dr. Hissah as-Saghir)

scholars.text: Bringing forward in creation: such as bringing some creatures before others, causes before their effects, and conditions before what depends on them.
Bringing forward in the religion: such as preferring some prophets over others, and preferring all of them over the rest of creation.

notes: Al-Muqaddim and al-Mu'akhkhir are a pair. The Prophet ﷺ always mentioned them together, and al-Khattabi said joining them is better, so read this entry together with al-Mu'akhkhir.
Whatever Allah brings forward or puts back, He does it with perfect knowledge and wisdom; nothing in it is random or unjust.

lessons.text: Ask Allah to forgive what you have sent ahead and what you have left behind, as the Prophet ﷺ did at the end of his prayer.
Do not wish for what Allah has given others in preference to you; ask Him from His bounty instead.

dua.text: O Allah, forgive me what I have sent before and what I have left behind, what I have hidden and what I have done openly, what I have done in excess, and what You know better than I. You are al-Muqaddim and You are al-Mu'akhkhir; there is no god but You.

names.summary: Allah is al-Mu'akhkhir: the One who puts back and delays whatever and whoever He wills, by His knowledge and wisdom. He is mentioned together with al-Muqaddim: no one can bring forward what He delays, or delay what He brings forward.

quran.note: Allah does not punish people at once; He defers them to an appointed term (the verb yu'akhkhiru).
quran.arabic: وَلَوْ يُؤَاخِذُ اللَّهُ النَّاسَ بِظُلْمِهِم مَّا تَرَكَ عَلَيْهَا مِن دَابَّةٍ وَلَٰكِن يُؤَخِّرُهُمْ إِلَىٰ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى ۖ فَإِذَا جَاءَ أَجَلُهُمْ لَا يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ سَاعَةً ۖ وَلَا يَسْتَقْدِمُونَ
quran.translation: And if Allāh were to impose blame on the people for their wrongdoing, He would not have left upon it [i.e., the earth] any creature, but He defers them for a specified term. And when their term has come, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede [it].

quran.note: Allah is not unaware of the wrongdoers; He only defers them to a Day that is coming.
quran.arabic: وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ اللَّهَ غَافِلًا عَمَّا يَعْمَلُ الظَّالِمُونَ ۚ إِنَّمَا يُؤَخِّرُهُمْ لِيَوْمٍ تَشْخَصُ فِيهِ الْأَبْصَارُ
quran.translation: And never think that Allāh is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them [i.e., their account] for a Day when eyes will stare [in horror].

quran.note: Allah never defers a soul once its appointed time has come.
quran.arabic: وَلَن يُؤَخِّرَ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِذَا جَاءَ أَجَلُهَا ۚ وَاللَّهُ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ
quran.translation: But never will Allāh delay a soul when its time has come. And Allāh is Aware of what you do.

hadith.text: In the du'a of his night prayer the Prophet ﷺ said: "You are al-Muqaddim and You are al-Mu'akhkhir; there is no god but You."

Between the tashahhud and the taslim the Prophet ﷺ would ask Allah to forgive what he had sent before and left behind, and end with: "You are al-Muqaddim and You are al-Mu'akhkhir; there is no god but You."
A du'a of the Prophet ﷺ for forgiveness ends: "You are al-Muqaddim, You are al-Mu'akhkhir, and You have power over all things."

scholars.text: He delays a thing past the time it was expected, because He knows the wisdom in how it will end. So no one can bring forward what He delays, and no one can delay what He brings forward.
scholars.book: IslamQA, answer 11366 (from Sharh Asma' Allah al-Husna by Dr. Hissah as-Saghir)

scholars.text: He puts things in their proper places: He brings forward what He wills and puts back what He wills.
Mentioning these two Names together is better than separating them, as we said about some of the Names before.

notes: Read this entry together with al-Muqaddim; the two Names are a pair and are not separated.
When Allah delays the punishment of wrongdoers, it is not because He is unaware of them. It is a respite until a fixed Day (14:42).

lessons.text: Do not be fooled when wrongdoers seem to escape; Allah is only giving them time until a coming Day.
Use your life well and give in charity now, because when your time comes it will not be put back.
When something you hoped for is delayed, trust Allah: you may dislike a thing that is good for you, and Allah knows while you do not.

dua.text: O Allah, forgive me my mistakes, my ignorance, my excess in my affairs, and what You know better than I. O Allah, forgive me what I did in earnest and in jest, by mistake and on purpose, for all of that is in me. O Allah, forgive me what I have sent before and what I have left behind, what I have hidden and what I have done openly, and what You know better than I. You are al-Muqaddim, You are al-Mu'akhkhir, and You have power over all things.

names.summary: Allah is al-Awwal: the First, before whom there is nothing. He existed before all things, with no beginning, and everything else came into being by His creation.

quran.note: The four Names al-Awwal, al-Akhir, az-Zahir and al-Batin together, followed by His knowledge of all things.
quran.arabic: هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ وَالظَّاهِرُ وَالْبَاطِنُ ۖ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ
quran.translation: He is the First and the Last, the Ascendant and the Intimate, and He is, of all things, Knowing.

hadith.text: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet ﷺ taught a du'a for going to sleep, which includes: "O Allah, You are the First, there is nothing before You; You are the Last, there is nothing after You; You are az-Zahir, there is nothing above You; You are al-Batin, there is nothing beneath You. Settle our debts for us and free us from poverty."
Imran ibn Husayn reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah existed and there was nothing other than Him, and His Throne was over the water."

scholars.text: Al-Awwal is the One before whom there is nothing.
He is the First, before everything, without any limit.
He is described this way because He existed when nothing else existed, and He will remain after all things have passed away.
Al-Awwal is the One who came before all things, who has always existed before creation came to be.

notes: The Prophet ﷺ himself explained this Name: "You are the First, there is nothing before You" (Sahih Muslim 2713). His being First has no beginning, while everything other than Him was created.

The four Names in 57:3 belong together: al-Awwal and al-Akhir tell us that nothing is before Allah and nothing is after Him, and az-Zahir and al-Batin tell us that nothing is above Him and nothing is beyond Him (Sahih Muslim 2713).

lessons.text: Every blessing you have comes from Allah, who existed before you and gave you all you have, so thank Him.
Say the du'a of the Prophet ﷺ when you go to sleep, praising Allah by these four Names and asking Him to settle your debts.

dua.text: O Allah, You are the First, there is nothing before You; You are the Last, there is nothing after You; You are az-Zahir, there is nothing above You; You are al-Batin, there is nothing beneath You. Settle our debts for us and free us from poverty.

names.summary: Allah is al-Akhir: the Last, after whom there is nothing. All creation will perish, and He alone remains forever, without end; to Him everything returns.

quran.note: The four Names al-Awwal, al-Akhir, az-Zahir and al-Batin together.
quran.arabic: هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ وَالظَّاهِرُ وَالْبَاطِنُ ۖ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ
quran.translation: He is the First and the Last, the Ascendant and the Intimate, and He is, of all things, Knowing.

quran.note: All on earth will perish, while the Face of Allah, Owner of majesty and honour, remains.
quran.arabic: كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍ ۝ وَيَبْقَىٰ وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ
quran.translation: Everyone upon it [i.e., the earth] will perish, And there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor.

quran.note: Everything perishes except His Face, and to Him is the return.
quran.arabic: وَلَا تَدْعُ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا آخَرَ ۘ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۚ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ هَالِكٌ إِلَّا وَجْهَهُ ۚ لَهُ الْحُكْمُ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ
quran.translation: And do not invoke with Allāh another deity. There is no deity except Him. Everything will be destroyed except His Face. His is the judgement, and to Him you will be returned.

hadith.text: In the du'a for going to sleep, the Prophet ﷺ said: "You are the First, there is nothing before You; You are the Last, there is nothing after You; You are az-Zahir, there is nothing above You; You are al-Batin, there is nothing beneath You."
The Prophet ﷺ used to say: "I seek refuge in Your might, there is no god but You, the One who does not die, while the jinn and mankind die."

scholars.text: Al-Akhir is the One after whom there is nothing.
And He is the Last, after everything, without any end.
He existed when nothing else existed, and He will remain after all things have passed away.
All the people of the earth will go and die. The Lord, exalted and holy is He, does not die; He is the Ever-Living who never dies.

notes: The Prophet ﷺ explained this Name: "You are the Last, there is nothing after You" (Sahih Muslim 2713). His being Last does not mean He ends; it means He remains after all things, without end.
Allah's Face, mentioned in 55:27 and 28:88, is affirmed as a real attribute, befitting His majesty and unlike the faces of creation.

lessons.text: Work for what lasts: everything perishes except Allah, and to Him you will return.
You are striving toward your Lord and you will meet Him, so prepare for that meeting.
Seek refuge in the Ever-Living who never dies, as the Prophet ﷺ did.

dua.text: O Allah, You are the First, there is nothing before You; You are the Last, there is nothing after You; You are az-Zahir, there is nothing above You; You are al-Batin, there is nothing beneath You. Settle our debts for us and free us from poverty.

names.summary: Allah is az-Zahir: the One above whom there is nothing. He is high above all His creation, over His Throne, and He prevails over everything beneath Him; nothing is higher than He.

quran.note: The four Names al-Awwal, al-Akhir, az-Zahir and al-Batin together.
quran.arabic: هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ وَالظَّاهِرُ وَالْبَاطِنُ ۖ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ
quran.translation: He is the First and the Last, the Ascendant and the Intimate, and He is, of all things, Knowing.

quran.note: Allah is above His servants and prevails over them.
quran.arabic: وَهُوَ الْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ ۚ وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ
quran.translation: And He is the subjugator over His servants. And He is the Wise, the Aware.

quran.note: The angels fear their Lord who is above them.
quran.arabic: يَخَافُونَ رَبَّهُم مِّن فَوْقِهِمْ وَيَفْعَلُونَ مَا يُؤْمَرُونَ
quran.translation: They fear their Lord above them, and they do what they are commanded.

quran.note: Allah's rising over His Throne (istiwa'), real and befitting His majesty.
quran.arabic: الرَّحْمَٰنُ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ اسْتَوَىٰ
quran.translation: The Most Merciful [who is] above the Throne established.

quran.note: The command to glorify the Name of the Most High.
quran.arabic: سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَى
quran.translation: Exalt the name of your Lord, the Most High,

hadith.text: In the du'a for going to sleep, the Prophet ﷺ said: "You are the First, there is nothing before You; You are the Last, there is nothing after You; You are az-Zahir, there is nothing above You; You are al-Batin, there is nothing beneath You."

Mu'awiyah ibn al-Hakam brought his slave girl to the Prophet ﷺ, who asked her: "Where is Allah?" She said: "In the heaven." He asked: "Who am I?" She said: "You are the Messenger of Allah." He said: "Free her, for she is a believer."

scholars.text: Az-Zahir is the One above whom there is nothing.
He is above and prevails over everything beneath Him. He is the Most High above all things, and nothing is higher than He.
Worshipping Allah by this Name means knowing that He is above His servants, directing every affair from the heaven to the earth.
scholars.book: Tariq al-Hijratayn, pp. 20-22, quoted in the Dorar.net creed encyclopedia

notes: The Prophet ﷺ explained az-Zahir himself: "nothing is above You" (Sahih Muslim 2713). So this Name includes Allah's highness above His creation: the highness of His essence, of His status and of His power.

Ahl as-Sunnah affirm that Allah is above the heavens, over His Throne, separate from His creation, without asking how and without likening Him to anything created. This highness does not stop His knowledge and nearness from reaching everything, as explained under al-Batin.

lessons.text: Humble yourself before the Most High in prostration, saying: "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High."
Fear Allah who is above you, as the angels fear their Lord above them.
Know where your Lord is, as the slave girl did: when asked "Where is Allah?" she said "In the heaven," and the Prophet ﷺ called her a believer.

dua.text: O Allah, You are the First, there is nothing before You; You are the Last, there is nothing after You; You are az-Zahir, there is nothing above You; You are al-Batin, there is nothing beneath You. Settle our debts for us and free us from poverty.

names.summary: Allah is al-Batin: there is nothing beneath Him and nothing hidden from Him. He knows every secret and hidden thing, and He is near to His creation in a way that befits Him, while He is above all things.

quran.note: The four Names al-Awwal, al-Akhir, az-Zahir and al-Batin together, followed by His knowledge of all things.
quran.arabic: هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ وَالظَّاهِرُ وَالْبَاطِنُ ۖ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ
quran.translation: He is the First and the Last, the Ascendant and the Intimate, and He is, of all things, Knowing.

quran.note: The same passage tells of His rising over the Throne and that He is with you wherever you are, seeing what you do.
quran.arabic: هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ اسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا يَلِجُ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَا يَخْرُجُ مِنْهَا وَمَا يَنزِلُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ وَمَا يَعْرُجُ فِيهَا ۖ وَهُوَ مَعَكُمْ أَيْنَ مَا كُنتُمْ ۚ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ
quran.translation: It is He who created the heavens and earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne. He knows what penetrates into the earth and what emerges from it and what descends from the heaven and what ascends therein; and He is with you wherever you are. And Allāh, of what you do, is Seeing.

quran.note: Allah is near and answers the one who calls on Him.
quran.arabic: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ ۖ أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ الدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ ۖ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا لِي وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا بِي لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْشُدُونَ
quran.translation: And when My servants ask you, [O Muḥammad], concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me [by obedience] and believe in Me that they may be [rightly] guided.

quran.note: Allah's perfect awareness of all things, while no sight can fully grasp Him.
quran.arabic: لَّا تُدْرِكُهُ الْأَبْصَارُ وَهُوَ يُدْرِكُ الْأَبْصَارَ ۖ وَهُوَ اللَّطِيفُ الْخَبِيرُ
quran.translation: Vision perceives Him not, but He perceives [all] vision; and He is the Subtle, the Aware.

hadith.text: In the du'a for going to sleep, the Prophet ﷺ said: "You are the First, there is nothing before You; You are the Last, there is nothing after You; You are az-Zahir, there is nothing above You; You are al-Batin, there is nothing beneath You."

Abu Musa reported that on a journey people raised their voices loudly with takbir. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Be gentle with yourselves. You are not calling on one who is deaf or absent; you are calling on One who hears all and is near, and He is with you."

scholars.text: Al-Batin is the One beneath whom there is nothing. His knowledge encompasses the outward and the inward, secrets and hidden matters, and what came before and what comes after.
He is al-Batin of all things, so nothing is nearer to anything than He is.
He is above everything, so He is over it, and He is al-Batin, so He is nearer to everything than it is to itself.
scholars.book: Tariq al-Hijratayn, pp. 20-22, quoted in the Dorar.net creed encyclopedia

notes: The Prophet ﷺ explained this Name himself: "You are al-Batin, there is nothing beneath You" (Sahih Muslim 2713), meaning nothing is beyond Him or hidden from Him.

Al-Batin does not mean that Allah is inside His creation or mixed with it. Ahl as-Sunnah affirm that He is above His Throne, and that His knowledge, hearing and nearness reach everything. Ibn al-Qayyim joins the two: He is above everything, and nearer to everything than it is to itself.

lessons.text: Call on Allah with humility and a gentle voice, because the One you call hears all and is near.
Ask Allah directly for what you need; He is near and answers the one who calls Him.
Keep your inner thoughts and intentions pure, because He is with you wherever you are and sees what you do.

dua.text: O Allah, You are the First, there is nothing before You; You are the Last, there is nothing after You; You are az-Zahir, there is nothing above You; You are al-Batin, there is nothing beneath You. Settle our debts for us and free us from poverty.

names.summary: Al-Wali carries the meaning of the One who takes charge of the affairs of His creation. Besides Allah, no one can truly manage people's affairs, bring them what is good or keep harm away from them.
names.established_note: In the Quran this word comes only as the indefinite noun "wal" (13:11), not as a Name, and the well-known list that contains it is not authentically from the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn Uthaymeen did not include it among the Names he gathered from the Quran (al-Qawa'id al-Muthla). Its meaning is true and affirmed.

quran.note: The word "wal": besides Allah, people have no one to take charge of their affairs.
quran.arabic: لَهُ مُعَقِّبَاتٌ مِّن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ يَحْفَظُونَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُغَيِّرُ مَا بِقَوْمٍ حَتَّىٰ يُغَيِّرُوا مَا بِأَنفُسِهِمْ ۗ وَإِذَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ سُوءًا فَلَا مَرَدَّ لَهُ ۚ وَمَا لَهُم مِّن دُونِهِ مِن وَالٍ
quran.translation: For him [i.e., each one] are successive [angels] before and behind him who protect him by the decree of Allāh. Indeed, Allāh will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when Allāh intends for a people ill, there is no repelling it. And there is not for them besides Him any patron.

quran.note: The related established Name al-Waliyy (الولي), the Protecting Friend, comes with al-Hamid.
quran.arabic: وَهُوَ الَّذِي يُنَزِّلُ الْغَيْثَ مِن بَعْدِ مَا قَنَطُوا وَيَنشُرُ رَحْمَتَهُ ۚ وَهُوَ الْوَلِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ
quran.translation: And it is He who sends down the rain after they had despaired and spreads His mercy. And He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ used to pray: "O Allah, give my soul its piety and purify it, for You are the best to purify it. You are its Guardian and its Master."

The supplication of a person in distress: "O Allah, it is Your mercy that I hope for, so do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye, and set right all of my affairs. There is no god but You."

scholars.text: Here "wal" means someone who takes charge of them and looks after their affairs, including their punishment. Besides Allah, they have no such one.
Besides Allah, they have no one to take charge of their affairs, to bring them what they love and to keep away from them what they dislike.
The Prophet ﷺ did not authentically name which Names make up the ninety-nine, and the hadith reported from him listing them is weak.

notes: Among the Names Ibn Uthaymeen gathered from the Quran, he included al-Waliyy (الولي) and al-Mawla, but not al-Wali (الوالي).
So a Muslim affirms the meaning: Allah alone runs the affairs of His creation, and calls upon Him by His established Names.

lessons.text: Rely on Allah to set your affairs right, and ask Him not to leave you to yourself even for a moment.
Begin with yourself: Allah ties a change in a people's state to the change they make in themselves, so turn back to Him with repentance and good deeds.

dua.text: O Allah, it is Your mercy that I hope for, so do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye, and set right all of my affairs. There is no god but You.

names.summary: Allah is al-Muta'ali: the Most High, exalted above all of His creation by His essence, by His status and by His power, and far above every flaw and every likeness to His creation.

quran.note: Allah knows the unseen and the seen; here He is named al-Kabir, al-Muta'al.
quran.arabic: عَالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ الْكَبِيرُ الْمُتَعَالِ
quran.translation: [He is] Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Grand, the Exalted.

quran.note: Allah declares Himself far exalted above what the disbelievers say (the verb form "ta'ala").
quran.arabic: سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَىٰ عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ عُلُوًّا كَبِيرًا
quran.translation: Exalted is He and high above what they say by great sublimity.

quran.note: The angels fear their Lord above them.
quran.arabic: يَخَافُونَ رَبَّهُم مِّن فَوْقِهِمْ وَيَفْعَلُونَ مَا يُؤْمَرُونَ
quran.translation: They fear their Lord above them, and they do what they are commanded.

hadith.text: Before sleeping, the Prophet ﷺ would praise Allah saying: "You are the First, nothing is before You; You are the Last, nothing is after You; You are az-Zahir, nothing is above You; You are al-Batin, nothing is beyond You."
The Prophet ﷺ asked a slave girl, "Where is Allah?" She said, "In the heaven." He asked, "Who am I?" She said, "You are the Messenger of Allah." He said, "Free her, for she is a believer."
In his prostration, the Prophet ﷺ would say: "Subhana Rabbiyal-A'la", glory be to my Lord, the Most High.

scholars.text: Al-Kabir is great in His essence, His Names and His Attributes; al-Muta'al is high above all of His creation by His essence, His power and His might over them.
Al-Ali and al-A'la is the One who has highness without limit in every way: highness of essence, highness of status and attributes, and highness of power over all.
scholars.book: Tafsir al-Sa'di 5/487 (Dar al-Madani ed.), quoted in ad-Durar as-Saniyyah's al-Mawsu'ah al-'Aqadiyyah 1/489

scholars.text: Al-Kabir is greater than everything, and al-Muta'al is high above everything. He encompasses all things in His knowledge and has subdued all things.
He counted al-Muta'ali among the ninety-nine Names he gathered from the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ.

notes: Ahl as-Sunnah affirm that Allah is truly above His creation, over His Throne, in a way that befits Him and is unlike anything created. His highness is not only of rank and power, but of His essence as well.
His highness never makes Him distant: He knows the unseen and the seen (13:9).

lessons.text: Remember Allah's highness in every prostration: the lowest position of the body is joined with praise of the Most High.
Know that your Lord is above His creation: the slave girl answered that Allah is in the heaven, and the Prophet ﷺ declared her a believer.

dua.text: O Allah, You are the First, nothing is before You; You are the Last, nothing is after You; You are az-Zahir, nothing is above You; You are al-Batin, nothing is beyond You. Settle our debts for us and free us from poverty.

names.summary: Allah is al-Barr: the One whose goodness and kindness reach His servants in countless ways. He is gentle with them, multiplies their good deeds and grants the believers His pleasure and Paradise.

quran.note: The people of Paradise say they used to call on Allah before, for He is al-Barr, ar-Rahim.
quran.arabic: إِنَّا كُنَّا مِن قَبْلُ نَدْعُوهُ ۖ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْبَرُّ الرَّحِيمُ
quran.translation: Indeed, we used to supplicate Him before. Indeed, it is He who is the Beneficent, the Merciful."

hadith.text: Allah wrote good and bad deeds. Whoever intends a good deed and does not do it, Allah writes it as a full good deed. If he does it, He writes it as ten to seven hundred good deeds or more. Whoever intends a bad deed and does not do it, Allah writes it as a full good deed, and if he does it, He writes it as one bad deed.
In a hadith qudsi Allah says: "I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he comes to Me walking, I come to him running."

scholars.text: "He is al-Barr" means the One who is gentle and kind to His servants.
He explained al-Barr as al-Latif, the Gentle and Kind.
On the words of the people of Paradise: it is out of His goodness and mercy to us that He granted us His pleasure and Paradise, and protected us from His anger and the Fire.

notes: The people of Paradise call Allah al-Barr after seeing the result of their calling on Him in this life: their worship and their asking were answered with His goodness.

lessons.text: Call on Allah often in this life, as the people of Paradise did before they entered it.
Show goodness to your parents: the Prophet ﷺ named it the most beloved deed to Allah after prayer on time.
Be truthful, for truthfulness leads to goodness, and goodness leads to Paradise.

dua.text: O Allah, set right for me my religion, which is the safeguard of my affairs; set right for me my worldly life, in which I live; set right for me my Hereafter, to which I will return; make life an increase for me in every good, and make death a rest for me from every evil.

names.summary: Allah is at-Tawwab: He turns to His servants again and again. He opens the door of repentance for them, helps them to repent, then accepts their repentance and forgives their sins, however often they return to Him.

quran.note: Adam received words from his Lord, and Allah accepted his repentance.
quran.arabic: فَتَلَقَّىٰ آدَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِ كَلِمَاتٍ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ ۚ إِنَّهُ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ
quran.translation: Then Adam received from his Lord [some] words, and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, it is He who is the Accepting of Repentance, the Merciful.

quran.note: Allah accepts repentance from His servants.
quran.arabic: أَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ يَقْبَلُ التَّوْبَةَ عَنْ عِبَادِهِ وَيَأْخُذُ الصَّدَقَاتِ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ
quran.translation: Do they not know that it is Allāh who accepts repentance from His servants and receives charities and that it is Allāh who is the Accepting of Repentance, the Merciful?

quran.note: Allah turned to the three Companions who stayed behind, so that they would repent.
quran.arabic: وَعَلَى الثَّلَاثَةِ الَّذِينَ خُلِّفُوا حَتَّىٰ إِذَا ضَاقَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الْأَرْضُ بِمَا رَحُبَتْ وَضَاقَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ أَنفُسُهُمْ وَظَنُّوا أَن لَّا مَلْجَأَ مِنَ اللَّهِ إِلَّا إِلَيْهِ ثُمَّ تَابَ عَلَيْهِمْ لِيَتُوبُوا ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ
quran.translation: And [He also forgave] the three who were left alone [i.e., boycotted, regretting their error] to the point that the earth closed in on them in spite of its vastness and their souls confined [i.e., anguished] them and they were certain that there is no refuge from Allāh except in Him. Then He turned to them so they could repent. Indeed, Allāh is the Accepting of Repentance, the Merciful.

quran.note: Glorify your Lord and seek His forgiveness; He is ever accepting of repentance.
quran.arabic: فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَاسْتَغْفِرْهُ ۚ إِنَّهُ كَانَ تَوَّابًا
quran.translation: Then exalt [Him] with praise of your Lord and ask forgiveness of Him. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of Repentance.

hadith.text: Allah is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than a man who lost his camel, carrying his food and drink, in a barren desert. Losing all hope, he lay down in the shade of a tree, and then found it standing beside him. In his great joy he said by mistake: "O Allah, You are my servant and I am Your lord."

Allah stretches out His Hand at night so that the one who sinned during the day may repent, and He stretches out His Hand during the day so that the one who sinned at night may repent, until the sun rises from the west.
Ibn Umar said that in a single sitting they would count the Prophet ﷺ saying a hundred times: "My Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance, for You are at-Tawwab, ar-Rahim."

scholars.text: He accepts the repentance of whoever turns to Him and comes back to Him.
This is from His kindness to His creation and His mercy to His servants. There is no god but He, at-Tawwab, ar-Rahim.
On "then He turned to them so that they would repent": He allowed their repentance and gave them the success to make it.
At-Tawwab is the One who turns much to His servants, pardoning and forgiving their slips and their disobedience.
Allah's turning to His servant in forgiveness is the greatest of goals and the highest of ends.

notes: In 9:118 Allah turned to the three Companions first, so that they would repent: the servant's repentance itself is a gift from Allah, and then Allah accepts it.

lessons.text: Never lose hope after a sin: return to Allah, for He is more pleased with your repentance than the man who found his lost camel.
Do not delay repentance: the door is open by night and by day, but it closes when the sun rises from the west.
Make asking for forgiveness a daily habit, as the Prophet ﷺ did, a hundred times in one sitting.
Even after success and good deeds, glorify Allah and seek His forgiveness, for He is ever accepting of repentance.

dua.text: My Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance, for You are at-Tawwab, ar-Rahim.

names.meaning: The One Who Takes Just Retribution
names.summary: Allah takes just retribution from the criminals who deserve it, such as those who turn away from His signs after they have been made clear to them. His retribution is pure justice: He wrongs no one, and He gives respite before He seizes.
names.established_note: In the Quran this comes only in a restricted form tied to the criminals, "inna min al-mujrimina muntaqimun" (32:22), and as "Mighty, Owner of retribution" (3:4). Ibn Taymiyyah and Ibn Uthaymeen said al-Muntaqim is therefore not one of Allah's established Names (IslamQA 516634).

quran.note: Allah will take retribution from the criminals (the plural form "muntaqimun").
quran.arabic: وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّن ذُكِّرَ بِآيَاتِ رَبِّهِ ثُمَّ أَعْرَضَ عَنْهَا ۚ إِنَّا مِنَ الْمُجْرِمِينَ مُنتَقِمُونَ
quran.translation: And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord; then he turns away from them? Indeed We, from the criminals, will take retribution.

quran.note: The day of the great seizure, when Allah takes retribution.
quran.arabic: يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ الْبَطْشَةَ الْكُبْرَىٰ إِنَّا مُنتَقِمُونَ
quran.translation: The Day We will strike with the greatest assault, indeed, We will take retribution.

quran.note: Allah is Mighty, the Owner of retribution, against those who reject His signs.
quran.arabic: مِن قَبْلُ هُدًى لِّلنَّاسِ وَأَنزَلَ الْفُرْقَانَ ۗ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ ۗ وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ ذُو انتِقَامٍ
quran.translation: Before, as guidance for the people. And He revealed the Criterion [i.e., the Qur’ān]. Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of Allāh will have a severe punishment, and Allāh is Exalted in Might, the Owner of Retribution.

hadith.text: Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer, but when He seizes him He does not let him escape. Then the Prophet ﷺ recited 11:102.
On the Day of Resurrection rights will be given back to their owners, even the hornless sheep will be given its due from the horned sheep.
In a hadith qudsi Allah says: "O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another."

scholars.text: The name al-Muntaqim is not one of the beautiful Names established from the Prophet ﷺ. It comes in the Quran only in a restricted form.

Al-Muntaqim is not one of Allah's Names, because Allah only mentioned this description of Himself in a restricted way. A description that comes restricted is not a Name, because Allah's Names are perfect without any restriction.
No one is more unjust than a person whom Allah reminded of His signs and made them clear to him, and who then turned away from them.
Such a person is among the greatest criminals, who deserve severe retribution.

notes: In 32:22 and 44:16 the word comes as "muntaqimun", in the plural that Allah uses for Himself to show His greatness, and never as the single Name "al-Muntaqim".
Allah's retribution falls only on those who deserve it, as a just recompense for their crimes. He has forbidden injustice for Himself.
So we describe Allah as the Quran does: He takes retribution from the criminals, and He is Mighty, the Owner of retribution.

lessons.text: Never wrong anyone, for every right will be returned to its owner on the Day of Resurrection.
Do not be deceived when a wrongdoer seems to go unpunished: Allah gives respite, but when He seizes, there is no escape.
Do not turn away from Allah's reminders once they have been made clear to you.

dua.text: O Allah, I have wronged myself greatly, and no one forgives sins but You. So forgive me with forgiveness from You and have mercy on me, for You are al-Ghafur, ar-Rahim.

names.summary: Allah is al-'Afuw: He pardons His servants' slips and even their great sins, wiping them away and covering them, though He is fully able to punish. He loves to pardon, and He honours those who pardon others.

quran.note: Allah is ever Pardoning and All-Powerful.
quran.arabic: إِن تُبْدُوا خَيْرًا أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ أَوْ تَعْفُوا عَن سُوءٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَفُوًّا قَدِيرًا
quran.translation: If [instead] you show [some] good or conceal it or pardon an offense - indeed, Allāh is ever Pardoning and Competent.

quran.note: Allah may pardon the weak who could not emigrate; He is ever Pardoning, Forgiving.
quran.arabic: فَأُولَٰئِكَ عَسَى اللَّهُ أَن يَعْفُوَ عَنْهُمْ ۚ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَفُوًّا غَفُورًا
quran.translation: For those it is expected that Allāh will pardon them, and Allāh is ever Pardoning and Forgiving.

quran.note: Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving.
quran.arabic: ذَٰلِكَ وَمَنْ عَاقَبَ بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقِبَ بِهِ ثُمَّ بُغِيَ عَلَيْهِ لَيَنصُرَنَّهُ اللَّهُ ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ غَفُورٌ
quran.translation: That [is so]. And whoever responds [to injustice] with the equivalent of that with which he was harmed and then is tyrannized - Allāh will surely aid him. Indeed, Allāh is Pardoning and Forgiving.

quran.note: Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving.
quran.arabic: الَّذِينَ يُظَاهِرُونَ مِنكُم مِّن نِّسَائِهِم مَّا هُنَّ أُمَّهَاتِهِمْ ۖ إِنْ أُمَّهَاتُهُمْ إِلَّا اللَّائِي وَلَدْنَهُمْ ۚ وَإِنَّهُمْ لَيَقُولُونَ مُنكَرًا مِّنَ الْقَوْلِ وَزُورًا ۚ وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ غَفُورٌ
quran.translation: Those who pronounce ẓihār among you [to separate] from their wives - they are not [consequently] their mothers. Their mothers are none but those who gave birth to them. And indeed, they are saying an objectionable statement and a falsehood. But indeed, Allāh is Pardoning and Forgiving.

hadith.text: Aisha asked the Prophet ﷺ what she should say if she knew which night was Laylat al-Qadr. He said: "Say: O Allah, You are 'Afuw, You love to pardon, so pardon me."
Charity does not decrease wealth. Allah increases a servant who pardons others only in honour, and whoever humbles himself for Allah, Allah raises him.

scholars.text: It is one of His attributes that He pardons His servants even though He is able to punish them.
He pardons the slips of His servants and their great sins, and lets His covering fall over them.
Then He treats them with His complete pardon, which comes from His power.

notes: In 4:149 Allah joins al-'Afuw with al-Qadir: His pardon comes from complete power, not from weakness.

lessons.text: Pardon those who wrong you: it brings honour from Allah, not humiliation.
Pardon and overlook, hoping that Allah will forgive you.
Ask Allah often for pardon, especially in the nights when Laylat al-Qadr is sought.

dua.text: O Allah, You are 'Afuw, You love to pardon, so pardon me.

names.summary: Allah is ar-Ra'uf: His mercy towards His servants is intense and tender. Out of His kindness He completes the favours He began for them and does not let their faith and good deeds go to waste.

quran.note: Allah would not let the believers' faith be lost; He is Kind and Merciful to people.
quran.arabic: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلْنَاكُمْ أُمَّةً وَسَطًا لِّتَكُونُوا شُهَدَاءَ عَلَى النَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ الرَّسُولُ عَلَيْكُمْ شَهِيدًا ۗ وَمَا جَعَلْنَا الْقِبْلَةَ الَّتِي كُنتَ عَلَيْهَا إِلَّا لِنَعْلَمَ مَن يَتَّبِعُ الرَّسُولَ مِمَّن يَنقَلِبُ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيْهِ ۚ وَإِن كَانَتْ لَكَبِيرَةً إِلَّا عَلَى الَّذِينَ هَدَى اللَّهُ ۗ وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ إِيمَانَكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِالنَّاسِ لَرَءُوفٌ رَّحِيمٌ
quran.translation: And thus We have made you a median [i.e., just] community that you will be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you. And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face except that We might make evident who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels. And indeed, it is difficult except for those whom Allāh has guided. And never would Allāh have caused you to lose your faith [i.e., your previous prayers]. Indeed Allāh is, to the people, Kind and Merciful.

quran.note: Allah turned to the Prophet ﷺ and the believers in the hour of hardship.
quran.arabic: لَّقَد تَّابَ اللَّهُ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ وَالْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَالْأَنصَارِ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُ فِي سَاعَةِ الْعُسْرَةِ مِن بَعْدِ مَا كَادَ يَزِيغُ قُلُوبُ فَرِيقٍ مِّنْهُمْ ثُمَّ تَابَ عَلَيْهِمْ ۚ إِنَّهُ بِهِمْ رَءُوفٌ رَّحِيمٌ
quran.translation: Allāh has already forgiven the Prophet and the Muhājireen and the Anṣār who followed him in the hour of difficulty after the hearts of a party of them had almost inclined [to doubt], and then He forgave them. Indeed, He was to them Kind and Merciful.

quran.note: Allah sends down clear signs to bring people out of darkness into light.
quran.arabic: هُوَ الَّذِي يُنَزِّلُ عَلَىٰ عَبْدِهِ آيَاتٍ بَيِّنَاتٍ لِّيُخْرِجَكُم مِّنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى النُّورِ ۚ وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُمْ لَرَءُوفٌ رَّحِيمٌ
quran.translation: It is He who sends down upon His Servant [Muḥammad (ﷺ)] verses of clear evidence that He may bring you out from darknesses into the light. And indeed, Allāh is to you Kind and Merciful.

quran.note: The supplication of those who came after the Muhajirun and Ansar.
quran.arabic: وَالَّذِينَ جَاءُوا مِن بَعْدِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لَنَا وَلِإِخْوَانِنَا الَّذِينَ سَبَقُونَا بِالْإِيمَانِ وَلَا تَجْعَلْ فِي قُلُوبِنَا غِلًّا لِّلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا رَبَّنَا إِنَّكَ رَءُوفٌ رَّحِيمٌ
quran.translation: And [there is a share for] those who come after them, saying, "Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith and put not in our hearts [any] resentment toward those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful."

hadith.text: Some Muslims died before the qiblah was changed to the Ka'bah, and people did not know what to say about them. Then Allah revealed that He would never let their faith be lost (2:143).

A man found a dog panting from thirst. He filled his shoe with water and gave it to drink, so Allah thanked him and forgave him. The Prophet ﷺ said there is a reward for kindness to every living being.

scholars.text: Ra'fah is the highest kind of mercy. It covers all of creation in this world, and some of them in the Hereafter.
Ar-Ra'uf means intense and great in mercy towards them.
From His kindness and mercy towards them is that He completes for them the favour He began for them.
"Your faith" means your prayers towards Bayt al-Maqdis before the change; their reward is not lost with Allah.

notes: Ar-Ra'uf often comes together with ar-Rahim in the Quran, as in 2:143 and 59:10.

lessons.text: Be kind to every living creature, for there is reward in it.
Keep your heart free of ill feeling towards the believers, and pray for those who came before you.
Trust that no deed done sincerely for Allah is ever lost with Him.

dua.text: O Allah, it is Your mercy that I hope for, so do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye, and set right all of my affairs. There is no god but You.

names.summary: Allah is Malik al-Mulk: the Owner of all dominion. All kingship in the heavens and on earth belongs to Him alone. He gives power to whom He wills and takes it from whom He wills, and no one can hold back His decree.

quran.note: The Prophet ﷺ is told to call on Allah as Malik al-Mulk, who gives and takes away dominion.
quran.arabic: قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ مَالِكَ الْمُلْكِ تُؤْتِي الْمُلْكَ مَن تَشَاءُ وَتَنزِعُ الْمُلْكَ مِمَّن تَشَاءُ وَتُعِزُّ مَن تَشَاءُ وَتُذِلُّ مَن تَشَاءُ ۖ بِيَدِكَ الْخَيْرُ ۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
quran.translation: Say, "O Allāh, Owner of Sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty away from whom You will. You honor whom You will and You humble whom You will. In Your hand is [all] good. Indeed, You are over all things competent.

quran.note: Continues the same address: Allah's control over night and day, life and death, and provision.
quran.arabic: تُولِجُ اللَّيْلَ فِي النَّهَارِ وَتُولِجُ النَّهَارَ فِي اللَّيْلِ ۖ وَتُخْرِجُ الْحَيَّ مِنَ الْمَيِّتِ وَتُخْرِجُ الْمَيِّتَ مِنَ الْحَيِّ ۖ وَتَرْزُقُ مَن تَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
quran.translation: You cause the night to enter the day, and You cause the day to enter the night; and You bring the living out of the dead, and You bring the dead out of the living. And You give provision to whom You will without account [i.e., limit or measure]."

quran.note: On the Day of Resurrection all dominion is declared to belong to Allah, the One, the Prevailing.
quran.arabic: يَوْمَ هُم بَارِزُونَ ۖ لَا يَخْفَىٰ عَلَى اللَّهِ مِنْهُمْ شَيْءٌ ۚ لِّمَنِ الْمُلْكُ الْيَوْمَ ۖ لِلَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ
quran.translation: The Day they come forth nothing concerning them will be concealed from Allāh. To whom belongs [all] sovereignty this Day? To Allāh, the One, the Prevailing.

hadith.text: Allah will grasp the earth and fold up the heavens in His Right Hand, then He will say: "I am the King. Where are the kings of the earth?"
The most despicable name with Allah is that of a man who calls himself "King of kings". In one report: there is no owner except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

scholars.text: You are the King, the Owner of all kingdoms; absolute kingship is Yours.
