Gaining power and losing it both follow the will of Allah.
You are the Giver and You are the Withholder. Whatever You will happens, and whatever You do not will does not happen.
You are the One who disposes of Your creation as You please, doing whatever You will.
A group of scholars, among them al-Khattabi, Ibn al-Qayyim and Ibn al-Wazir, counted Malik al-Mulk among the Names. It is one of the added Names.
scholars.book: IslamQA 536457, citing al-Tamimi, Mu'taqad Ahl as-Sunnah, p. 204

notes: Malik al-Mulk is an added Name made of two words, and Allah is called upon by it, as in 3:26.

lessons.text: Never call yourself or anyone else "King of kings": that title belongs to Allah alone.
Do not envy people for power or position; Allah gives it and takes it away by His will and wisdom.
Remember that every earthly kingdom ends; on the Day of Resurrection Allah alone will say: "I am the King."

dua.text: O Allah, to You belongs all praise. You are the Sustainer of the heavens and the earth and all who are in them. To You belongs all praise; Yours is the dominion of the heavens and the earth and all who are in them.

names.meaning: The Possessor of Majesty and Generosity
names.summary: Allah is Dhul-Jalali wal-Ikram: the Possessor of majesty and greatness, who deserves to be revered and never disobeyed, and the Possessor of vast generosity and grace, who honours His devoted servants.

quran.note: Everything on earth perishes, and the Face of your Lord remains, Dhul-Jalali wal-Ikram.
quran.arabic: وَيَبْقَىٰ وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ
quran.translation: And there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor.

quran.note: The last ayah of Surah ar-Rahman: blessed is the Name of your Lord, Dhil-Jalali wal-Ikram.
quran.arabic: تَبَارَكَ اسْمُ رَبِّكَ ذِي الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ
quran.translation: Blessed is the name of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor.

hadith.text: Anas reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Hold fast to saying: Ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram."
When the Prophet ﷺ finished his prayer, he would ask Allah's forgiveness three times and say: "O Allah, You are as-Salam, and from You is peace. Blessed are You, O Possessor of majesty and honour."

scholars.text: In this ayah Allah described His noble Face as Dhul-Jalali wal-Ikram.
He is worthy to be revered so that He is not disobeyed, and to be obeyed so that He is not opposed.
Dhul-Jalal means the Possessor of greatness and supreme grandeur.
He is the Possessor of greatness, grandeur and glory, for which He is honoured and revered.
Al-Ikram is His vast grace and generosity.
Dhul-Jalali wal-Ikram is one of Allah's Names, unlike al-Burhan and al-Jami'.

notes: Ahl as-Sunnah affirm the Face of Allah as a real attribute that befits His majesty, unlike the faces of creation. In 55:27 it is described with majesty and honour.

lessons.text: Call upon Allah often with "Ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram".
After every prayer, ask forgiveness three times and praise Allah with the words the Prophet ﷺ used.
Everything on earth will perish and only your Lord's Face remains, so tie your heart to what lasts.

dua.text: O Allah, You are as-Salam, and from You is peace. Blessed are You, O Possessor of majesty and honour.

names.summary: Al-Muqsit carries the meaning of the One who is perfectly just. Allah upholds justice in all He decrees, weighs the deeds of His servants with exact scales and wrongs no one, and He loves those who are just.
names.established_note: Scholars differ. Al-Khattabi, Ibn Mandah, Ibn al-Qayyim and others counted al-Muqsit among the Names, and Salih Al ash-Shaykh affirmed it; but it does not come in the Quran as a Name for Allah, so the author of Mu'taqad Ahl as-Sunnah (Muhammad al-Tamimi) preferred that it is not a Name (IslamQA 330932). What is firmly established is Allah's justice (qist), in the Quran and Sunnah.

quran.note: Allah bears witness to His oneness, maintaining justice.
quran.arabic: شَهِدَ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ وَأُولُو الْعِلْمِ قَائِمًا بِالْقِسْطِ ۚ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ
quran.translation: Allāh witnesses that there is no deity except Him, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge - [that He is] maintaining [creation] in justice. There is no deity except Him, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

quran.note: The just scales on the Day of Resurrection; no soul will be wronged in the least.
quran.arabic: وَنَضَعُ الْمَوَازِينَ الْقِسْطَ لِيَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ فَلَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْئًا ۖ وَإِن كَانَ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِّنْ خَرْدَلٍ أَتَيْنَا بِهَا ۗ وَكَفَىٰ بِنَا حَاسِبِينَ
quran.translation: And We place the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be treated unjustly at all. And if there is [even] the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as accountant.

quran.note: Allah loves those who act justly (al-muqsitin).
quran.arabic: وَإِن طَائِفَتَانِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ اقْتَتَلُوا فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُمَا ۖ فَإِن بَغَتْ إِحْدَاهُمَا عَلَى الْأُخْرَىٰ فَقَاتِلُوا الَّتِي تَبْغِي حَتَّىٰ تَفِيءَ إِلَىٰ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ ۚ فَإِن فَاءَتْ فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُمَا بِالْعَدْلِ وَأَقْسِطُوا ۖ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُقْسِطِينَ
quran.translation: And if two factions among the believers should fight, then make settlement between the two. But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight against the one that oppresses until it returns to the ordinance of Allāh. And if it returns, then make settlement between them in justice and act justly. Indeed, Allāh loves those who act justly.

hadith.text: Allah does not sleep, and it is not fitting for Him to sleep. He lowers the scale and raises it. The deeds of the night are raised to Him before the deeds of the day, and the deeds of the day before the deeds of the night.

The just will be with Allah on pulpits of light at the right of ar-Rahman, and both of His Hands are right: those who are just in their rulings, with their families and in whatever they are put in charge of.

scholars.text: Allah tells of His just judgment and His fair decree between His servants when He gathers them on the Day of Resurrection.
No soul is wronged: none of its good deeds is reduced, and none is added to its bad deeds.
"Maintaining justice" describes His state, and He is like this in every state.
The author of Mu'taqad Ahl as-Sunnah preferred that al-Muqsit is not one of the Names, because it does not come in the Quran in the form of a Name for Allah.
scholars.book: IslamQA 330932, citing al-Tamimi, Mu'taqad Ahl as-Sunnah

notes: Allah's justice is complete: He never wrongs anyone, and the scales of the Day of Resurrection will weigh even the smallest deed (21:47).

lessons.text: Be just in your rulings, with your family and in whatever you are responsible for, to be among those on the pulpits of light.
Make peace between believers who quarrel, and do it with justice, for Allah loves those who are just.
Prepare for the scales: no good deed will be lost and no wrong will be added.

names.summary: Al-Jami' carries the meaning of the One who gathers. Allah will gather all of mankind on a Day about which there is no doubt, judge between them in what they differed over and repay each person for his deeds.
names.established_note: Al-Jami' on its own does not come as a Name in the Quran or authentic Sunnah. It comes in an added form: "Jami' an-nas" (3:9) and "Jami' al-munafiqin wal-kafirin" (4:140). IslamQA concludes that al-Jami' alone is not a Name, while "Jami' an-nas li-yawmin la rayba fih" is an added Name by which Allah may be called upon (IslamQA 516431, 535598).

quran.note: The supplication of those firm in knowledge: Allah will gather mankind for a Day about which there is no doubt.
quran.arabic: رَبَّنَا إِنَّكَ جَامِعُ النَّاسِ لِيَوْمٍ لَّا رَيْبَ فِيهِ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُخْلِفُ الْمِيعَادَ
quran.translation: Our Lord, surely You will gather the people for a Day about which there is no doubt. Indeed, Allāh does not fail in His promise."

quran.note: Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers in Hell.
quran.arabic: وَقَدْ نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ أَنْ إِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ يُكْفَرُ بِهَا وَيُسْتَهْزَأُ بِهَا فَلَا تَقْعُدُوا مَعَهُمْ حَتَّىٰ يَخُوضُوا فِي حَدِيثٍ غَيْرِهِ ۚ إِنَّكُمْ إِذًا مِّثْلُهُمْ ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ جَامِعُ الْمُنَافِقِينَ وَالْكَافِرِينَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ جَمِيعًا
quran.translation: And it has already come down to you in the Book [i.e., the Qur’ān] that when you hear the verses of Allāh [recited], they are denied [by them] and ridiculed; so do not sit with them until they enter into another conversation. Indeed, you would then be like them. Indeed, Allāh will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers in Hell all together -

quran.note: The Day of Gathering, when Allah brings all people together.
quran.arabic: يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُكُمْ لِيَوْمِ الْجَمْعِ ۖ ذَٰلِكَ يَوْمُ التَّغَابُنِ ۗ وَمَن يُؤْمِن بِاللَّهِ وَيَعْمَلْ صَالِحًا يُكَفِّرْ عَنْهُ سَيِّئَاتِهِ وَيُدْخِلْهُ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا ۚ ذَٰلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ
quran.translation: The Day He will assemble you for the Day of Assembly - that is the Day of Deprivation. And whoever believes in Allāh and does righteousness - He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. That is the great attainment.

quran.note: Our Lord will bring us together, then judge between us in truth.
quran.arabic: قُلْ يَجْمَعُ بَيْنَنَا رَبُّنَا ثُمَّ يَفْتَحُ بَيْنَنَا بِالْحَقِّ وَهُوَ الْفَتَّاحُ الْعَلِيمُ
quran.translation: Say, "Our Lord will bring us together; then He will judge between us in truth. And He is the Knowing Judge."

hadith.text: On the Day of Resurrection Allah will gather the first and the last of mankind on one plain, where the caller can make them all hear and the eye can see them all.

scholars.text: They say in their supplication: You, our Lord, will gather Your creation on the Day of their Return.
You will judge between them in what they differed over, and repay each one for his deeds, good and bad, from his life in this world.
He will repay them for their deeds, the good and the bad.

Likewise His added Names, such as Arham ar-Rahimin, Khayr al-Ghafirin, Rabb al-'Alamin and Jami' an-nas li-yawmin la rayba fih, are established in the Book and the Sunnah, and calling on Allah by them is agreed upon by the Muslims.
Dhul-Jalali wal-Ikram is one of Allah's Names, unlike al-Burhan and al-Jami'.

notes: The gathering is followed by judgment: in 34:26 the Messenger ﷺ is told to say that our Lord will bring us all together and then judge between us in truth.

lessons.text: Prepare for the Day when all people will stand together before Allah, and ask Him, as those firm in knowledge do, to keep your heart steady on His guidance.
Do not sit with those who mock Allah's signs while they are doing so, for 4:140 warns that whoever does is like them.

names.summary: Allah is al-Ghani: perfectly free of need in every way. He needs nothing from His creation, while every created being needs Him at every moment.

quran.note: All people are in need of Allah, and He is free of all need.
quran.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ أَنتُمُ الْفُقَرَاءُ إِلَى اللَّهِ ۖ وَاللَّهُ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ
quran.translation: O mankind, you are those in need of Allāh, while Allāh is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.

quran.note: Said about spending in Allah's cause: whoever holds back only holds back from himself.
quran.arabic: هَا أَنتُمْ هَٰؤُلَاءِ تُدْعَوْنَ لِتُنفِقُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَمِنكُم مَّن يَبْخَلُ ۖ وَمَن يَبْخَلْ فَإِنَّمَا يَبْخَلُ عَن نَّفْسِهِ ۚ وَاللَّهُ الْغَنِيُّ وَأَنتُمُ الْفُقَرَاءُ ۚ وَإِن تَتَوَلَّوْا يَسْتَبْدِلْ قَوْمًا غَيْرَكُمْ ثُمَّ لَا يَكُونُوا أَمْثَالَكُم
quran.translation: Here you are - those invited to spend in the cause of Allāh - but among you are those who withhold [out of greed]. And whoever withholds only withholds [benefit] from himself; and Allāh is the Free of need, while you are the needy. And if you turn away [i.e., refuse], He will replace you with another people; then they will not be the likes of you.

quran.note: Everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him.
quran.arabic: لَّهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ ۗ وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَهُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ
quran.translation: To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is on the earth. And indeed, Allāh is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.

quran.note: Whoever strives does so for his own good; Allah does not need the worlds.
quran.arabic: وَمَن جَاهَدَ فَإِنَّمَا يُجَاهِدُ لِنَفْسِهِ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَغَنِيٌّ عَنِ الْعَالَمِينَ
quran.translation: And whoever strives only strives for [the benefit of] himself. Indeed, Allāh is Free from need of the worlds.

quran.note: People's disbelief does not harm Allah, though He is not pleased with it for His servants.
quran.arabic: إِن تَكْفُرُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ عَنكُمْ ۖ وَلَا يَرْضَىٰ لِعِبَادِهِ الْكُفْرَ ۖ وَإِن تَشْكُرُوا يَرْضَهُ لَكُمْ ۗ وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ ۗ ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُم مَّرْجِعُكُمْ فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ ۚ إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ
quran.translation: If you disbelieve - indeed, Allāh is Free from need of you. And He does not approve for His servants disbelief. And if you are grateful, He approves [i.e., likes] it for you; and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.

hadith.text: In a hadith qudsi, Allah says: "O My servants, you can never reach the point of harming Me, nor of benefiting Me." He also says that if all of mankind and jinn, from the first to the last, stood in one place and each asked Him, and He gave every one of them what he asked, it would reduce what He has no more than a needle reduces the sea when it is dipped into it.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "The Hand of Allah is full. Spending does not decrease it; He gives generously night and day. Do you see what He has spent since He created the heavens and the earth? It has not decreased what is in His Hand."
When praying for rain, the Prophet ﷺ said: "O Allah, You are Allah; there is no god but You. You are al-Ghani, and we are the poor."

scholars.text: He alone has true freedom from need, with no partner, and He is the Praiseworthy in all that He does and says, all that He decrees and all that He legislates.

Al-Ghani is the One who has complete freedom from need in every respect, so He needs nothing of what His creation needs. And part of His richness is that He enriches the creation in this world and the Hereafter.
Al-Ghani is the One who has no need of the creation, nor of their help and support for His dominion. He has no need of them at all.

notes: Allah's freedom from need belongs to His very essence. It did not begin at some point and it will never end, just as the creation's need of Him never ends (35:15).
Allah commands worship and charity not because He needs them. Their benefit returns to the servant himself (29:6, 47:38).

lessons.text: Real richness is contentment: "Richness is not having many possessions; true richness is richness of the soul."
Spend in Allah's cause, knowing that He does not need your money; whoever holds back only holds back from himself.
Your obedience does not benefit Allah and your sins do not harm Him; your deeds are recorded for you and you will be repaid for them, so turn to Him in humility.

dua.text: O Allah, You are Allah; there is no god but You. You are al-Ghani, and we are the poor. Send down the rain upon us, and make what You send down a strength for us and a provision for a while.

names.summary: Allah is the One who enriches whom He wills. All wealth, provision and contentment that anyone has comes from Him, and He alone can free a person from need.
names.established_note: "Al-Mughni" does not come as a Name in the Quran or the authentic Sunnah; Allah's enriching comes there as a verb (53:48, 93:8). Some scholars, such as al-Khattabi, al-Qurtubi and al-Sa'di, counted it among the Names (IslamQA 535598), while Ibn Uthaymeen did not include it in his list (al-Qawa'id al-Muthla).

quran.note: Allah is the One who enriches and grants lasting wealth (the verb form of this Name).
quran.arabic: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَغْنَىٰ وَأَقْنَىٰ
quran.translation: And that it is He who enriches and suffices

quran.note: Allah's favour on the Prophet ﷺ: He took him from poverty to sufficiency (verb form).
quran.arabic: وَوَجَدَكَ عَائِلًا فَأَغْنَىٰ
quran.translation: And He found you poor and made [you] self-sufficient.

quran.note: A promise to believers who feared poverty that Allah would enrich them from His bounty.
quran.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّمَا الْمُشْرِكُونَ نَجَسٌ فَلَا يَقْرَبُوا الْمَسْجِدَ الْحَرَامَ بَعْدَ عَامِهِمْ هَٰذَا ۚ وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ عَيْلَةً فَسَوْفَ يُغْنِيكُمُ اللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ إِن شَاءَ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ
quran.translation: O you who have believed, indeed the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Ḥarām after this, their [final] year. And if you fear privation, Allāh will enrich you from His bounty if He wills. Indeed, Allāh is Knowing and Wise.

quran.note: Poverty should not prevent marriage; Allah enriches from His bounty.
quran.arabic: وَأَنكِحُوا الْأَيَامَىٰ مِنكُمْ وَالصَّالِحِينَ مِنْ عِبَادِكُمْ وَإِمَائِكُمْ ۚ إِن يَكُونُوا فُقَرَاءَ يُغْنِهِمُ اللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ ۗ وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ
quran.translation: And marry the unmarried among you and the righteous among your male slaves and female slaves. If they should be poor, Allāh will enrich them from His bounty, and Allāh is all-Encompassing and Knowing.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever seeks to keep himself from asking, Allah will keep him chaste; whoever seeks to be free of need, Allah will make him free of need; and whoever strives to be patient, Allah will give him patience. No one has been given a gift better and more vast than patience."
The Prophet ﷺ used to say: "O Allah, I ask You for guidance, piety, chastity and freedom from need."
In the supplication the Prophet ﷺ taught for bedtime, after praising Allah as the First, the Last, az-Zahir and al-Batin, he asked: "Settle our debts for us and make us free of poverty."

scholars.text: Allah enriched His servants by making their living easy for them through trade and all kinds of earning, crafts and other work, and He gave them wealth of every kind so that they come to own it.
This is one of His blessings on His servants: every blessing comes from Him, and this obliges the servants to thank Him and to worship Him alone, with no partner.
Part of Allah's own freedom from need is that He enriched the creation in this world and the Hereafter.

notes: Al-Ghani and al-Mughni go together in meaning: Allah is free of need Himself, and He is the One who makes others free of need. Whatever wealth a person has comes from His bounty (24:32).
True freedom from need is not only money. The Prophet ﷺ asked Allah for it together with guidance, piety and chastity (Muslim 2721).

lessons.text: Seek sufficiency from Allah, not from people: whoever seeks to be free of need, Allah makes him free of need.
Do not let fear of poverty stop you from obeying Allah; He promised to enrich the believers from His bounty.
Thank Allah for every provision, because every blessing you have is from Him.

dua.text: O Allah, I ask You for guidance, piety, chastity and freedom from need.

names.summary: Allah gives and withholds by His perfect wisdom. No one can hold back what He gives, no one can give what He withholds, and His withholding is never stinginess.
names.established_note: "Al-Mani'" is not found as a Name in the Quran or an authentic hadith; the authentic du'a "none can withhold what You give" (Bukhari 844) affirms the action. Ibn al-Qayyim taught that it is only said together with its opposite, al-Mu'ti (the Giver), which is itself an authentic Name (Bukhari 3116), and IslamQA (531203) notes that some scholars counted the pair.

quran.note: No one can hold back the mercy Allah sends, or release what He holds back (the meaning of withholding).
quran.arabic: مَّا يَفْتَحِ اللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ مِن رَّحْمَةٍ فَلَا مُمْسِكَ لَهَا ۖ وَمَا يُمْسِكْ فَلَا مُرْسِلَ لَهُ مِن بَعْدِهِ ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ
quran.translation: Whatever Allāh grants to people of mercy - none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds - none can release it thereafter. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

quran.note: Allah sends provision in measure, because unlimited provision would lead people to transgress.
quran.arabic: وَلَوْ بَسَطَ اللَّهُ الرِّزْقَ لِعِبَادِهِ لَبَغَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَٰكِن يُنَزِّلُ بِقَدَرٍ مَّا يَشَاءُ ۚ إِنَّهُ بِعِبَادِهِ خَبِيرٌ بَصِيرٌ
quran.translation: And if Allāh had extended [excessively] provision for His servants, they would have committed tyranny throughout the earth. But He sends [it] down in an amount which He wills. Indeed He is, of His servants, Aware and Seeing.

quran.note: Allah's giving in this world reaches both groups of people; it is not restricted.
quran.arabic: كُلًّا نُّمِدُّ هَٰؤُلَاءِ وَهَٰؤُلَاءِ مِنْ عَطَاءِ رَبِّكَ ۚ وَمَا كَانَ عَطَاءُ رَبِّكَ مَحْظُورًا
quran.translation: To each [category] We extend - to these and to those - from the gift of your Lord. And never has the gift of your Lord been restricted.

hadith.text: After every obligatory prayer the Prophet ﷺ used to say: "None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things. O Allah, none can withhold what You give, none can give what You withhold, and a man's wealth and fortune cannot benefit him against You."
The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah is the Giver (al-Mu'ti), and I am only the one who distributes."

scholars.text: Allah tells us that whatever He wills happens and whatever He does not will does not happen, and that none can withhold what He gives and none can give what He withholds.
Some of Allah's Names are not said on their own, but only together with their opposite, such as al-Mani', ad-Darr and al-Muntaqim.

If Allah spread out provision without limit, people would become heedless of obeying Him and give themselves over to the pleasures of this world; so He sends it down in the measure that His kindness and wisdom require.

notes: Allah's withholding is not stinginess or lack: His Hand is full and spending never decreases it (Bukhari 7411). He withholds out of wisdom, knowing what is best for His servants (42:27).
Because al-Mani' is only mentioned with al-Mu'ti, it shows Allah's complete control: giving and withholding are both in His Hand alone.

lessons.text: Say after every prayer: "O Allah, none can withhold what You give, and none can give what You withhold", and let it free your heart from hoping in people.
When something you want is held back, trust Allah: you may dislike a thing while it is good for you.
Ask Allah alone, since all opening and holding back of mercy is in His Hand.

dua.text: O Allah, none can withhold what You give, none can give what You withhold, and a man's wealth and fortune cannot benefit him against You.

names.meaning: The One Who Decrees Harm (by His wisdom)
names.summary: Ad-Darr is only ever mentioned together with an-Nafi': Allah alone decrees both harm and benefit. Nothing harms or benefits anyone except by His decree, and all He decrees is full of wisdom and justice.
names.established_note: IslamQA (84270) states that it is not established by authentic evidence that ad-Darr is a Name of Allah; it comes only in the weak list of at-Tirmidhi. Ibn al-Qayyim and Ibn Taymiyyah mention it only paired with an-Nafi', to show that Allah alone controls harm and benefit.

quran.note: Only Allah can remove a harm that touches you, and He has power to bring good.
quran.arabic: وَإِن يَمْسَسْكَ اللَّهُ بِضُرٍّ فَلَا كَاشِفَ لَهُ إِلَّا هُوَ ۖ وَإِن يَمْسَسْكَ بِخَيْرٍ فَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
quran.translation: And if Allāh should touch you with adversity, there is no remover of it except Him. And if He touches you with good - then He is over all things competent.

quran.note: No one can remove the harm Allah decrees, and no one can turn back His favour.
quran.arabic: وَإِن يَمْسَسْكَ اللَّهُ بِضُرٍّ فَلَا كَاشِفَ لَهُ إِلَّا هُوَ ۖ وَإِن يُرِدْكَ بِخَيْرٍ فَلَا رَادَّ لِفَضْلِهِ ۚ يُصِيبُ بِهِ مَن يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ ۚ وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ
quran.translation: And if Allāh should touch you with adversity, there is no remover of it except Him; and if He intends for you good, then there is no repeller of His bounty. He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.

quran.note: Even magic harms no one except by Allah's permission (a related form of the word).
quran.arabic: وَاتَّبَعُوا مَا تَتْلُو الشَّيَاطِينُ عَلَىٰ مُلْكِ سُلَيْمَانَ ۖ وَمَا كَفَرَ سُلَيْمَانُ وَلَٰكِنَّ الشَّيَاطِينَ كَفَرُوا يُعَلِّمُونَ النَّاسَ السِّحْرَ وَمَا أُنزِلَ عَلَى الْمَلَكَيْنِ بِبَابِلَ هَارُوتَ وَمَارُوتَ ۚ وَمَا يُعَلِّمَانِ مِنْ أَحَدٍ حَتَّىٰ يَقُولَا إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ فِتْنَةٌ فَلَا تَكْفُرْ ۖ فَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مِنْهُمَا مَا يُفَرِّقُونَ بِهِ بَيْنَ الْمَرْءِ وَزَوْجِهِ ۚ وَمَا هُم بِضَارِّينَ بِهِ مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ ۚ وَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مَا يَضُرُّهُمْ وَلَا يَنفَعُهُمْ ۚ وَلَقَدْ عَلِمُوا لَمَنِ اشْتَرَاهُ مَا لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَاقٍ ۚ وَلَبِئْسَ مَا شَرَوْا بِهِ أَنفُسَهُمْ ۚ لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ
quran.translation: And they followed [instead] what the devils had recited during the reign of Solomon. It was not Solomon who disbelieved, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic and that which was revealed to the two angels at Babylon, Hārūt and Mārūt. But they [i.e., the two angels] do not teach anyone unless they say, "We are a trial, so do not disbelieve [by practicing magic]." And [yet] they learn from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife. But they do not harm anyone through it except by permission of Allāh. And they [i.e., people] learn what harms them and does not benefit them. But they [i.e., the Children of Israel] certainly knew that whoever purchased it [i.e., magic] would not have in the Hereafter any share. And wretched is that for which they sold themselves, if they only knew.

quran.note: Misfortune that reaches people is because of what their own hands have earned, and Allah pardons much.
quran.arabic: وَمَا أَصَابَكُم مِّن مُّصِيبَةٍ فَبِمَا كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَيَعْفُو عَن كَثِيرٍ
quran.translation: And whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned; but He pardons much.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said to Ibn Abbas: "Know that if the whole nation gathered together to benefit you with something, they could only benefit you with what Allah has already written for you; and if they gathered together to harm you with something, they could only harm you with what Allah has already written against you. The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried."
In his opening supplication in the night prayer, the Prophet ﷺ said to Allah: "All good is in Your Hands, and evil is not attributed to You."

The Prophet ﷺ said: "How wonderful is the affair of the believer! All of it is good for him, and this is for no one except the believer. If something pleasing happens to him, he is thankful, and that is good for him. If hardship befalls him, he is patient, and that is good for him."

scholars.text: The meaning of ad-Darr is the One who decrees harm and makes it reach whomever He wills of His creation. The scholars explained that it is only mentioned together with stating that He is an-Nafi'.
Perfection lies in joining each of these Names with its opposite: giving and withholding, benefit and harm, pardon and just punishment.
All of Allah's actions are pure good, with no evil in them at all. Evil is attributed to the created thing that is done, not to the Lord's act of creating.
Allah is praiseworthy in His actions, because they are all bounty, kindness, justice, wisdom and mercy.

notes: Ad-Darr must never be said on its own. It is mentioned with an-Nafi' to show that harm and benefit are both in Allah's Hand alone, so no one is feared or hoped in besides Him.

When harm reaches a servant, it comes by Allah's decree and justice, often because of the servant's own sins (42:30), and it carries good for the believer who is patient (Muslim 2999). Evil is never attributed to Allah Himself (Muslim 771).

lessons.text: Do not fear any created being for harm or hope in it for benefit; nothing reaches you except what Allah has already written.
Turn to Allah alone to remove a hardship, because no one else can remove it.
Meet hardship with patience and ease with gratitude, and both become good for you.

dua.text: In the Name of Allah, with whose Name nothing on the earth or in the heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. (Three times in the morning and in the evening.)

names.summary: An-Nafi' is mentioned together with ad-Darr: Allah alone grants every benefit. No one can bring you any good unless He has written it for you, and no one can hold back the good He wills for you.
names.established_note: An-Nafi' is not established as a separate Name in the Quran or the authentic Sunnah; it comes in the weak list of at-Tirmidhi. IslamQA (531203, 84270) explains that Allah is not called by it on its own, but it is mentioned together with its opposite, ad-Darr.

quran.note: A command not to call on anything besides Allah that can neither benefit nor harm (verb forms of the same root).
quran.arabic: وَلَا تَدْعُ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنفَعُكَ وَلَا يَضُرُّكَ ۖ فَإِن فَعَلْتَ فَإِنَّكَ إِذًا مِّنَ الظَّالِمِينَ
quran.translation: And do not invoke besides Allāh that which neither benefits you nor harms you, for if you did, then indeed you would be of the wrongdoers.'"

quran.note: No one can prevent what Allah wills of benefit or harm for you (the noun naf', benefit).
quran.arabic: سَيَقُولُ لَكَ الْمُخَلَّفُونَ مِنَ الْأَعْرَابِ شَغَلَتْنَا أَمْوَالُنَا وَأَهْلُونَا فَاسْتَغْفِرْ لَنَا ۚ يَقُولُونَ بِأَلْسِنَتِهِم مَّا لَيْسَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ ۚ قُلْ فَمَن يَمْلِكُ لَكُم مِّنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا إِنْ أَرَادَ بِكُمْ ضَرًّا أَوْ أَرَادَ بِكُمْ نَفْعًا ۚ بَلْ كَانَ اللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا
quran.translation: Those who remained behind of the bedouins will say to you, "Our properties and our families occupied us, so ask forgiveness for us." They say with their tongues what is not within their hearts. Say, "Then who could prevent Allāh at all if He intended for you harm or intended for you benefit? Rather, ever is Allāh, of what you do, Aware.

quran.note: Even the Prophet ﷺ owns no benefit or harm for himself except what Allah wills.
quran.arabic: قُل لَّا أَمْلِكُ لِنَفْسِي نَفْعًا وَلَا ضَرًّا إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ ۚ وَلَوْ كُنتُ أَعْلَمُ الْغَيْبَ لَاسْتَكْثَرْتُ مِنَ الْخَيْرِ وَمَا مَسَّنِيَ السُّوءُ ۚ إِنْ أَنَا إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ وَبَشِيرٌ لِّقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ
quran.translation: Say, "I hold not for myself [the power of] benefit or harm, except what Allāh has willed. And if I knew the unseen, I could have acquired much wealth, and no harm would have touched me. I am not except a warner and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe."

quran.note: The false gods people take besides Allah own no benefit or harm even for themselves.
quran.arabic: قُلْ مَن رَّبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ قُلِ اللَّهُ ۚ قُلْ أَفَاتَّخَذْتُم مِّن دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَاءَ لَا يَمْلِكُونَ لِأَنفُسِهِمْ نَفْعًا وَلَا ضَرًّا ۚ قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمَىٰ وَالْبَصِيرُ أَمْ هَلْ تَسْتَوِي الظُّلُمَاتُ وَالنُّورُ ۗ أَمْ جَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكَاءَ خَلَقُوا كَخَلْقِهِ فَتَشَابَهَ الْخَلْقُ عَلَيْهِمْ ۚ قُلِ اللَّهُ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُوَ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ
quran.translation: Say, "Who is Lord of the heavens and earth?" Say, "Allāh." Say, "Have you then taken besides Him allies not possessing [even] for themselves any benefit or any harm?" Say, "Is the blind equivalent to the seeing? Or is darkness equivalent to light? Or have they attributed to Allāh partners who created like His creation so that the creation [of each] seemed similar to them?" Say, "Allāh is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Prevailing."

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said to Ibn Abbas: "Know that if the whole nation gathered together to benefit you with something, they could only benefit you with what Allah has already written for you; and if they gathered together to harm you with something, they could only harm you with what Allah has already written against you."

In his remembrance after every obligatory prayer, the Prophet ﷺ said: "O Allah, none can withhold what You give, none can give what You withhold, and a man's wealth and fortune cannot benefit him against You."
After the dawn prayer, as he said the salam, the Prophet ﷺ would say: "O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, good provision and deeds that are accepted."

scholars.text: This shows that, in reality, no one benefits except Allah, and no one besides Him harms.
The Lord, glorified is He, is the Owner who manages all affairs: the Giver and the Withholder, the One who harms and benefits, who lowers and raises, who honours and humbles.
An-Nafi' is not one of the Names in the sense that Allah is not called by it on its own; rather it is mentioned together with its opposite.
Allah owns harm and benefit and disposes of His creation as He wills. No one can overturn His judgement or push back His decree.

notes: An-Nafi' and ad-Darr are mentioned together because Allah alone controls both. Created means only benefit or harm by His permission (2:102), so the heart should rely on Him, not on the means.
Allah's benefit reaches His servants out of His bounty, and whatever harm He decrees is by His justice and wisdom. All good is in His Hands, and evil is not attributed to Him (Muslim 771).

lessons.text: Strive for what benefits you, seek Allah's help and do not give up.
Do not call on anyone besides Allah who can neither benefit nor harm you.
When people or means fail you, remember they never owned benefit in the first place, and turn your hope to Allah.

dua.text: O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, good provision and deeds that are accepted.

names.summary: Allah is an-Nur: He is Light, His veil is light, and by Him the heavens and the earth are lit. He also gives the light of guidance and faith to whom He wills.
names.established_note: It comes as "the Light of the heavens and the earth" (24:35; Bukhari 1120). Ibn al-Qayyim, Ibn Mandah and others counted an-Nur among the Names (Ibn Hajar in the attached form), and IslamQA (537274) concludes it is a Name and an Attribute; the Permanent Committee and Ibn Baz held that it comes only in this attached form and is not established as a stand-alone Name (IslamQA 226255).

quran.note: The Ayah of Light, with its parable of a niche and a lamp.
quran.arabic: اللَّهُ نُورُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۚ مَثَلُ نُورِهِ كَمِشْكَاةٍ فِيهَا مِصْبَاحٌ ۖ الْمِصْبَاحُ فِي زُجَاجَةٍ ۖ الزُّجَاجَةُ كَأَنَّهَا كَوْكَبٌ دُرِّيٌّ يُوقَدُ مِن شَجَرَةٍ مُّبَارَكَةٍ زَيْتُونَةٍ لَّا شَرْقِيَّةٍ وَلَا غَرْبِيَّةٍ يَكَادُ زَيْتُهَا يُضِيءُ وَلَوْ لَمْ تَمْسَسْهُ نَارٌ ۚ نُّورٌ عَلَىٰ نُورٍ ۗ يَهْدِي اللَّهُ لِنُورِهِ مَن يَشَاءُ ۚ وَيَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ الْأَمْثَالَ لِلنَّاسِ ۗ وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ
quran.translation: Allāh is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp; the lamp is within glass, the glass as if it were a pearly [white] star lit from [the oil of] a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if untouched by fire. Light upon light. Allāh guides to His light whom He wills. And Allāh presents examples for the people, and Allāh is Knowing of all things.

quran.note: On the Day of Judgement the earth will shine with the light of its Lord.
quran.arabic: وَأَشْرَقَتِ الْأَرْضُ بِنُورِ رَبِّهَا وَوُضِعَ الْكِتَابُ وَجِيءَ بِالنَّبِيِّينَ وَالشُّهَدَاءِ وَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُم بِالْحَقِّ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ
quran.translation: And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the record [of deeds] will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and it will be judged between them in truth, and they will not be wronged.

quran.note: The disbelievers want to put out Allah's light, but He will complete it.
quran.arabic: يُرِيدُونَ أَن يُطْفِئُوا نُورَ اللَّهِ بِأَفْوَاهِهِمْ وَيَأْبَى اللَّهُ إِلَّا أَن يُتِمَّ نُورَهُ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْكَافِرُونَ
quran.translation: They want to extinguish the light of Allāh with their mouths, but Allāh refuses except to perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it.

quran.note: Whoever Allah does not give light has no light at all.
quran.arabic: أَوْ كَظُلُمَاتٍ فِي بَحْرٍ لُّجِّيٍّ يَغْشَاهُ مَوْجٌ مِّن فَوْقِهِ مَوْجٌ مِّن فَوْقِهِ سَحَابٌ ۚ ظُلُمَاتٌ بَعْضُهَا فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ إِذَا أَخْرَجَ يَدَهُ لَمْ يَكَدْ يَرَاهَا ۗ وَمَن لَّمْ يَجْعَلِ اللَّهُ لَهُ نُورًا فَمَا لَهُ مِن نُّورٍ
quran.translation: Or [they are] like darknesses within an unfathomable sea which is covered by waves, upon which are waves, over which are clouds - darknesses, some of them upon others. When one puts out his hand [therein], he can hardly see it. And he to whom Allāh has not granted light - for him there is no light.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ stood among us and told us five things: "Allah does not sleep, and it is not befitting for Him to sleep. He lowers the scale and raises it. The deeds of the night are taken up to Him before the deeds of the day, and the deeds of the day before the deeds of the night. His veil is light; if He were to remove it, the glory of His Face would burn whatever of His creation His sight reaches."

When the Prophet ﷺ stood for the night prayer he would say: "O Allah, to You belongs all praise. You are the Sustainer of the heavens and the earth and all that is in them. To You belongs all praise; You are the Light of the heavens and the earth and all that is in them."

scholars.text: Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth, of both seen light and the light of meaning. He Himself is Light, and His veil is light; were it not for His kindness, the glory of His Face would burn whatever of His creation His sight reaches.
By Him the Throne, the Kursi, the sun, the moon and light itself are lit, and by Him Paradise is lit.
The texts have come naming the Lord as Light, and stating that He has light attributed to Him.
scholars.book: Mukhtasar as-Sawa'iq al-Mursalah, p. 423, quoted in IslamQA 537274

scholars.text: The text of Allah's Book and the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ has named Allah the Light of the heavens and the earth.

notes: Ahl as-Sunnah affirm light for Allah exactly as Allah and His Messenger ﷺ affirmed it: He is Light, His veil is light, and His Face has glory. All of this is real and befitting His majesty, unlike any created light, and it is not explained away.
Allah also gives light to hearts: He sent down the Quran as a clear light (4:174), and whoever He does not give light has no light (24:40).

lessons.text: Ask Allah for light in your heart, your sight, your hearing and all around you, as the Prophet ﷺ did.
Hold firmly to the Quran, which Allah sent down as a clear light.
Guard your prayer, for the Prophet ﷺ said: "Prayer is light."

dua.text: O Allah, place light in my heart, light in my sight and light in my hearing, light on my right and light on my left, light above me and light below me, light in front of me and light behind me, and make light great for me.

names.summary: Allah is al-Hadi: He guided every creature to what is good for it, He shows people the path of truth, and He alone can open a heart to accept it and walk on it.
names.established_note: It comes in the Quran as a description of Allah: "hadiyan" (25:31) and, in a restricted form, "hadi" (22:54). IslamQA (161275) counts it among the Names established in the Quran, and many scholars listed it, such as al-Khattabi, al-Bayhaqi, Ibn Hajar and al-Sa'di, though Ibn Uthaymeen did not include it in his list (al-Qawa'id al-Muthla).

quran.note: Allah is sufficient as a Guide and a Helper for His Messenger ﷺ.
quran.arabic: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلْنَا لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ عَدُوًّا مِّنَ الْمُجْرِمِينَ ۗ وَكَفَىٰ بِرَبِّكَ هَادِيًا وَنَصِيرًا
quran.translation: And thus have We made for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals. But sufficient is your Lord as a guide and a helper.

quran.note: Allah guides the believers to a straight path.
quran.arabic: وَلِيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكَ فَيُؤْمِنُوا بِهِ فَتُخْبِتَ لَهُ قُلُوبُهُمْ ۗ وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَهَادِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ
quran.translation: And so those who were given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord and [therefore] believe in it, and their hearts humbly submit to it. And indeed is Allāh the Guide of those who have believed to a straight path.

quran.note: Musa tells Pharaoh that his Lord gave everything its form, then guided it.
quran.arabic: قَالَ رَبُّنَا الَّذِي أَعْطَىٰ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلْقَهُ ثُمَّ هَدَىٰ
quran.translation: He said, "Our Lord is He who gave each thing its form and then guided [it]."

quran.note: Allah decreed for each creature its measure and guided it to it.
quran.arabic: وَالَّذِي قَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ
quran.translation: And who destined and [then] guided

quran.note: The Prophet ﷺ cannot give guidance to whoever he loves; Allah guides whom He wills.
quran.arabic: إِنَّكَ لَا تَهْدِي مَنْ أَحْبَبْتَ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَهْدِي مَن يَشَاءُ ۚ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ
quran.translation: Indeed, [O Muḥammad], you do not guide whom you like, but Allāh guides whom He wills. And He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.

hadith.text: In a hadith qudsi, Allah says: "O My servants, all of you are astray except those I guide, so ask Me for guidance and I will guide you."

The Prophet ﷺ would open his night prayer by calling on Allah as Lord of Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil, and asking: "Guide me, by Your permission, to the truth in what people have differed over; indeed You guide whom You will to a straight path."
In his night prayer the Prophet ﷺ asked: "Guide me to the best of manners; no one guides to the best of them except You."

scholars.text: There is no way to attain guidance except from Allah. He is the Guide who directs people to what is good for them in both worlds.

He guides you so that you reach what you seek and what is good for your religion and your worldly life. He helps you against your enemies and repels every harm from you, so let Him be enough for you and rely on Him.
Whoever follows His Messenger ﷺ, believes in His Book, affirms it and follows it, Allah is his Guide and Helper in this world and the Hereafter.

notes: Allah's guidance has several levels: He guided every creature to what suits it (20:50; 87:3), He shows people the way through His messengers and His Book, and He alone places acceptance of the truth in the heart, which even the Prophet ﷺ could not give to those he loved (28:56).
Guidance is the greatest gift a servant can receive, which is why the believer asks for it in every rak'ah (1:6).

lessons.text: Ask Allah for guidance constantly, as you do in every rak'ah of your prayer.
Strive in Allah's way and He will guide you to His paths.
Do not rely on your own understanding; ask Allah to guide you to the truth wherever people differ.

dua.text: O Allah, I ask You for guidance, piety, chastity and freedom from need.

names.summary: Allah is the Originator of the heavens and the earth: He brought them into being without any previous example, in the most beautiful and perfect way.
names.established_note: It comes in the attached form "Badi' as-samawati wal-ard", Originator of the heavens and the earth (2:117; 6:101; Abu Dawud 1495). IslamQA (535598) concludes it is an attached Name by which Allah is called upon, and notes that al-Saqqaf considered counting "al-Badi'" on its own as doubtful.

quran.note: Allah originated the heavens and the earth, and brings a thing into being by His command.
quran.arabic: بَدِيعُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۖ وَإِذَا قَضَىٰ أَمْرًا فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُ كُن فَيَكُونُ
quran.translation: Originator of the heavens and the earth. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.

quran.note: The Originator of the heavens and the earth has no son and no wife; He created everything.
quran.arabic: بَدِيعُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۖ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لَهُ وَلَدٌ وَلَمْ تَكُن لَّهُ صَاحِبَةٌ ۖ وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ ۖ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ
quran.translation: [He is] Originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have a son when He does not have a companion [i.e., wife] and He created all things? And He is, of all things, Knowing.

quran.note: Allah made everything He created excellent.
quran.arabic: الَّذِي أَحْسَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ ۖ وَبَدَأَ خَلْقَ الْإِنسَانِ مِن طِينٍ
quran.translation: Who perfected everything which He created and began the creation of man from clay.

quran.note: The passing of the mountains is described as the work of Allah, who perfected all that He made.
quran.arabic: وَتَرَى الْجِبَالَ تَحْسَبُهَا جَامِدَةً وَهِيَ تَمُرُّ مَرَّ السَّحَابِ ۚ صُنْعَ اللَّهِ الَّذِي أَتْقَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ ۚ إِنَّهُ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا تَفْعَلُونَ
quran.translation: And you see the mountains, thinking them motionless, while they will pass as the passing of clouds. [It is] the work of Allāh, who perfected all things. Indeed, He is Aware of that which you do.

hadith.text: Anas reported that a man prayed: "O Allah, I ask You, for to You belongs all praise; there is no god but You, al-Mannan, Originator of the heavens and the earth. O Owner of majesty and honour, O Ever-Living, O Self-Sustaining." The Prophet ﷺ said that he had called upon Allah by His Greatest Name, by which, when He is called, He answers, and when He is asked, He gives.
The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah existed and nothing else existed besides Him. His Throne was over the water, He wrote everything in the Record, and He created the heavens and the earth."

scholars.text: Badi' of the heavens and the earth means their Creator without any previous example; Mujahid and as-Suddi said this, and it is what the language requires. From this, a newly introduced thing is called a bid'ah.
Badi' of the heavens and the earth means their Creator and Originator, in the utmost beauty and wonderful creation.
scholars.book: Tafsir al-Sa'di (section on the Names), quoted in IslamQA 535598

scholars.text: Some counted al-Badi' among the Names of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and this is open to question.
scholars.book: Sifat Allah al-Waridah fil-Kitab was-Sunnah, p. 80, quoted in IslamQA 535598

notes: Allah's originating is unlike any human making. People only shape what Allah has already created, while Allah existed when nothing else existed (Bukhari 3191), and He brought all things into being without any previous example (2:117).
The same root gives the word bid'ah, a newly introduced thing without a previous example, as Ibn Kathir explained on 2:117.

lessons.text: Reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth; they are signs for people of understanding, who then praise and remember Allah.
Call upon Allah by His beautiful Names when you ask Him, as the man did whom the Prophet ﷺ praised.
Allah perfected everything He made, so recognise His perfection in His creation and glorify Him for it.

dua.text: O Allah, I ask You, for to You belongs all praise; there is no god but You, al-Mannan, Originator of the heavens and the earth. O Owner of majesty and honour, O Ever-Living, O Self-Sustaining.

names.summary: Allah is Everlasting: He remains forever after all of creation passes away. He is the Last, after whom there is nothing, the Ever-Living who never dies.
names.established_note: Al-Baqi is not found as a Name in the Quran or the authentic Sunnah; it comes only in the weak narrations that list the Names (IslamQA 535972). Ibn Baz and al-Barrak said its meaning is correct because Allah is al-Akhir (the Last), which is the established Name with this meaning.

quran.note: Everyone on earth will pass away, and the Face of your Lord remains (the verb form of this meaning).
quran.arabic: كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍ ۝ وَيَبْقَىٰ وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ
quran.translation: Everyone upon it [i.e., the earth] will perish, And there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor.

quran.note: Everything will perish except His Face.
quran.arabic: وَلَا تَدْعُ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا آخَرَ ۘ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۚ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ هَالِكٌ إِلَّا وَجْهَهُ ۚ لَهُ الْحُكْمُ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ
quran.translation: And do not invoke with Allāh another deity. There is no deity except Him. Everything will be destroyed except His Face. His is the judgement, and to Him you will be returned.

quran.note: Among the four Names here is al-Akhir, the Last, which carries the meaning of al-Baqi.
quran.arabic: هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ وَالظَّاهِرُ وَالْبَاطِنُ ۖ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ
quran.translation: He is the First and the Last, the Ascendant and the Intimate, and He is, of all things, Knowing.

quran.note: A command to rely on the Ever-Living who does not die.
quran.arabic: وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى الْحَيِّ الَّذِي لَا يَمُوتُ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِهِ ۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِهِ بِذُنُوبِ عِبَادِهِ خَبِيرًا
quran.translation: And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die, and exalt [Allāh] with His praise. And sufficient is He to be, with the sins of His servants, [fully] Aware -

quran.note: What people have runs out, and what is with Allah remains.
quran.arabic: مَا عِندَكُمْ يَنفَدُ ۖ وَمَا عِندَ اللَّهِ بَاقٍ ۗ وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّ الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا أَجْرَهُم بِأَحْسَنِ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ
quran.translation: Whatever you have will end, but what Allāh has is lasting. And We will surely give those who were patient their reward according to the best of what they used to do.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ taught us to say before sleeping: "O Allah, You are the First, and there is nothing before You; You are the Last, and there is nothing after You; You are az-Zahir, and there is nothing above You; You are al-Batin, and there is nothing beyond You."
The Prophet ﷺ used to say: "I seek refuge in Your might; there is no god but You, the One who does not die, while jinn and humans die."

scholars.text: Allah tells us that all the people of the earth will pass away and die, and no one will remain except His Noble Face. The Lord, Exalted and Holy is He, does not die; rather He is the Ever-Living who never dies.
I do not know a text that mentions the name al-Baqi, but its meaning is correct, for He, Majestic and Exalted, is al-Akhir.
scholars.book: Fatwa on the names Abd ar-Rashid and Abd al-Baqi (binbaz.org.sa 21208)

scholars.text: His Name al-Akhir shows His everlastingness and that He is the Ever-Abiding, glorified and exalted is He. If it is said, "He is al-Baqi", then yes, He truly is the Everlasting.

notes: Ahl as-Sunnah affirm the Face of Allah as a real Attribute befitting His majesty, unlike any created face. 55:27 and 28:88 tell us that His Face remains while everything else perishes.
His being the Last has no end, just as His being the First has no beginning (Muslim 2713). So the meaning of al-Baqi is expressed by the established Name al-Akhir.

lessons.text: Rely on the Ever-Living who never dies, not on people who will pass away.
Prefer what remains with Allah over what runs out with you.
Remember that everything on earth will pass away, and prepare for the meeting with your Lord, whose Face remains.

dua.text: I seek refuge in Your might; there is no god but You, the One who does not die, while jinn and humans die.

names.summary: Allah is al-Warith: He remains after all creation passes away, and everything people own returns to Him. He is the best of inheritors.
names.established_note: It comes in the Quran in the plural of majesty, "al-warithun" and "khayr al-warithin" (15:23; 21:89; 28:58). Ibn Uthaymeen counted al-Warith among the Names drawn from the Quran (al-Qawa'id al-Muthla, as listed in IslamQA 605086).

quran.note: Allah gives life and causes death, and He is the Inheritor.
quran.arabic: وَإِنَّا لَنَحْنُ نُحْيِي وَنُمِيتُ وَنَحْنُ الْوَارِثُونَ
quran.translation: And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the Inheritor.

quran.note: Zakariyya calls on Allah as the best of inheritors when asking Him for a child.
quran.arabic: وَزَكَرِيَّا إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُ رَبِّ لَا تَذَرْنِي فَرْدًا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ الْوَارِثِينَ
quran.translation: And [mention] Zechariah, when he called to his Lord, "My Lord, do not leave me alone [with no heir], while You are the best of inheritors."

quran.note: Allah will inherit the earth and all upon it, and all will return to Him.
quran.arabic: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَرِثُ الْأَرْضَ وَمَنْ عَلَيْهَا وَإِلَيْنَا يُرْجَعُونَ
quran.translation: Indeed, it is We who will inherit the earth and whoever is on it, and to Us they will be returned.

quran.note: Towns destroyed for their ingratitude; their dwellings were left, and Allah is the Inheritor.
quran.arabic: وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَرْيَةٍ بَطِرَتْ مَعِيشَتَهَا ۖ فَتِلْكَ مَسَاكِنُهُمْ لَمْ تُسْكَن مِّن بَعْدِهِمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا ۖ وَكُنَّا نَحْنُ الْوَارِثِينَ
quran.translation: And how many a city have We destroyed that was insolent in its [way of] living, and those are their dwellings which have not been inhabited after them except briefly. And it is We who were the inheritors.

quran.note: The inheritance of the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah, so why not spend in His cause?
quran.arabic: وَمَا لَكُمْ أَلَّا تُنفِقُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلِلَّهِ مِيرَاثُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۚ لَا يَسْتَوِي مِنكُم مَّنْ أَنفَقَ مِن قَبْلِ الْفَتْحِ وَقَاتَلَ ۚ أُولَٰئِكَ أَعْظَمُ دَرَجَةً مِّنَ الَّذِينَ أَنفَقُوا مِن بَعْدُ وَقَاتَلُوا ۚ وَكُلًّا وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الْحُسْنَىٰ ۚ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ
quran.translation: And why do you not spend in the cause of Allāh while to Allāh belongs the heritage of the heavens and the earth? Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest [of Makkah] and fought [and those who did so after it]. Those are greater in degree than they who spent afterwards and fought. But to all Allāh has promised the best [reward]. And Allāh, of what you do, is Aware.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah will grasp the earth and fold up the heavens in His Right Hand, then He will say: I am the King; where are the kings of the earth?"

The Prophet ﷺ asked: "Which of you loves the wealth of his heir more than his own wealth?" They said that each of them loved his own wealth more. He said: "His wealth is what he has sent ahead, and the wealth of his heir is what he has left behind."

scholars.text: Allah tells us that He is the Creator, the Owner and the One who disposes of all things. All creation will perish and He alone will remain, and no one will claim any dominion or control. He is the Inheritor of all His creation, the One who remains after them, the Judge among them.
He gave life to creation from nothing, then causes them to die, then will raise them all for the Day of Gathering; and He inherits the earth and all upon it, and to Him they return.
He alone, with no partner, gives life to the creation from nothing, after they were not anything worth mentioning, and causes them to die at the terms He decreed; and He is the Inheritor.

notes: Everything people own is held only for a while. It returns to Allah, the true Owner, to whom belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth (57:10).
Ahl as-Sunnah affirm the Right Hand of Allah mentioned in Bukhari 4812 as a real Attribute befitting His majesty, unlike the hands of creation.

lessons.text: Spend for Allah's sake now: your real wealth is what you send ahead, and what you leave behind belongs to your heirs.
Do not hold back from spending in Allah's cause, for the inheritance of the heavens and the earth belongs to Him.
Do not be deceived by worldly power; on the Last Day Allah alone will be King, and He will ask where the kings of the earth are.

names.summary: Allah is the One who guides His servants to right conduct. Only those He guides find the right way, and no one can direct the one He leaves astray.
names.established_note: Ar-Rashid is not found as a Name in the Quran or the authentic Sunnah, so IslamQA (5457) states it is not a Name of Allah, and Ibn Baz said he did not recall any text for it (binbaz.org.sa fatwa 21208). What is established is that Allah guides to right conduct (rushd), as in 18:17 and 49:7.

quran.note: Whoever Allah leaves astray will find no protector to direct him rightly (murshid, from the same root).
quran.arabic: وَتَرَى الشَّمْسَ إِذَا طَلَعَت تَّزَاوَرُ عَن كَهْفِهِمْ ذَاتَ الْيَمِينِ وَإِذَا غَرَبَت تَّقْرِضُهُمْ ذَاتَ الشِّمَالِ وَهُمْ فِي فَجْوَةٍ مِّنْهُ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ مِنْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ ۗ مَن يَهْدِ اللَّهُ فَهُوَ الْمُهْتَدِ ۖ وَمَن يُضْلِلْ فَلَن تَجِدَ لَهُ وَلِيًّا مُّرْشِدًا
quran.translation: And [had you been present], you would see the sun when it rose, inclining away from their cave on the right, and when it set, passing away from them on the left, while they were [lying] within an open space thereof. That was from the signs of Allāh. He whom Allāh guides is the [rightly] guided, but he whom He sends astray - never will you find for him a protecting guide.

quran.note: Allah made faith beloved to the believers and sin hateful to them; they are the rightly guided (rashidun, from the same root).
quran.arabic: وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ فِيكُمْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ۚ لَوْ يُطِيعُكُمْ فِي كَثِيرٍ مِّنَ الْأَمْرِ لَعَنِتُّمْ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ حَبَّبَ إِلَيْكُمُ الْإِيمَانَ وَزَيَّنَهُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ وَكَرَّهَ إِلَيْكُمُ الْكُفْرَ وَالْفُسُوقَ وَالْعِصْيَانَ ۚ أُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الرَّاشِدُونَ
quran.translation: And know that among you is the Messenger of Allāh. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in difficulty, but Allāh has endeared to you the faith and has made it pleasing in your hearts and has made hateful to you disbelief, defiance and disobedience. Those are the [rightly] guided.

quran.note: The jinn wondered whether their Lord intended right guidance for the people of the earth.
quran.arabic: وَأَنَّا لَا نَدْرِي أَشَرٌّ أُرِيدَ بِمَن فِي الْأَرْضِ أَمْ أَرَادَ بِهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ رَشَدًا
quran.translation: And we do not know [therefore] whether evil is intended for those on earth or whether their Lord intends for them a right course.

quran.note: The youths of the cave asked Allah for mercy and right guidance in their affair.
quran.arabic: إِذْ أَوَى الْفِتْيَةُ إِلَى الْكَهْفِ فَقَالُوا رَبَّنَا آتِنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحْمَةً وَهَيِّئْ لَنَا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا رَشَدًا
quran.translation: [Mention] when the youths retreated to the cave and said, "Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance."

quran.note: Allah answers the one who calls on Him, so that people may be rightly guided.
quran.arabic: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ ۖ أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ الدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ ۖ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا لِي وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا بِي لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْشُدُونَ
quran.translation: And when My servants ask you, [O Muḥammad], concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me [by obedience] and believe in Me that they may be [rightly] guided.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ told Ali: "Say: O Allah, guide me and keep me on the right course. When you say guidance, think of being guided on the road, and when you say right course, think of the straightness of an arrow."
In a hadith qudsi, Allah says: "O My servants, all of you are astray except those I guide, so ask Me for guidance and I will guide you."

scholars.text: Ar-Rashid is not one of the Names of Allah, because it does not come in the Quran or in the authentic Sunnah.
The Names of Allah are tawqifi: it is not permitted to name Allah except with what He named Himself or what His Messenger ﷺ named Him.

There is no way to attain guidance except from Allah; He is the Guide who directs people to what is good for them in both worlds. As for the one He leaves astray, you will find no one to take charge of him and manage his affairs for his good, nor to direct him to good and success.

notes: Since ar-Rashid is not found as a Name in the Quran or the authentic Sunnah, and Allah's Names are known only from revelation, we do not call Him by it as a Name. But we affirm what the Quran affirms: Allah is the Guide who directs His servants to right conduct, as al-Sa'di explained on 18:17.
Right conduct (rushd) is a favour from Allah. He makes faith beloved to the heart and sin hateful to it (49:7-8).

lessons.text: Ask Allah for right guidance in your affairs, as the youths of the cave did.
Respond to Allah and believe in Him; this is the way to right guidance.
If you love faith and dislike sin, thank Allah, for this is His favour on the rightly guided.

dua.text: O Allah, guide me and keep me on the right course.

names.summary: Allah is the Most Patient: no one is more patient than He is over the hurtful words people say about Him. He does not hasten their punishment, but gives them time and keeps providing for them.
names.established_note: As-Sabur does not come as a Name in the Quran or the authentic Sunnah, only in the weak list of at-Tirmidhi; but Allah's patience is affirmed in the authentic hadith "no one is more patient over hurtful words than Allah" (Bukhari 6099). Al-Khattabi, Ibn Mandah, al-Bayhaqi, Ibn al-Qayyim and others counted it as a Name, others did not, and IslamQA (191329) calls it a matter of scholarly judgement.

quran.note: If Allah took people to account at once for what they earn, no creature would be left; He delays them to an appointed term. (The meaning of patience, without the word itself.)
quran.arabic: وَلَوْ يُؤَاخِذُ اللَّهُ النَّاسَ بِمَا كَسَبُوا مَا تَرَكَ عَلَىٰ ظَهْرِهَا مِن دَابَّةٍ وَلَٰكِن يُؤَخِّرُهُمْ إِلَىٰ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى ۖ فَإِذَا جَاءَ أَجَلُهُمْ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِعِبَادِهِ بَصِيرًا
quran.translation: And if Allāh were to impose blame on the people for what they have earned, He would not leave upon it [i.e., the earth] any creature. But He defers them for a specified term. And when their time comes, then indeed Allāh has ever been, of His servants, Seeing.

quran.note: Allah does not seize people at once for their wrongdoing, but delays them to an appointed term.
quran.arabic: وَلَوْ يُؤَاخِذُ اللَّهُ النَّاسَ بِظُلْمِهِم مَّا تَرَكَ عَلَيْهَا مِن دَابَّةٍ وَلَٰكِن يُؤَخِّرُهُمْ إِلَىٰ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى ۖ فَإِذَا جَاءَ أَجَلُهُمْ لَا يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ سَاعَةً ۖ وَلَا يَسْتَقْدِمُونَ
quran.translation: And if Allāh were to impose blame on the people for their wrongdoing, He would not have left upon it [i.e., the earth] any creature, but He defers them for a specified term. And when their term has come, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede [it].

quran.note: Your Lord is Most Forgiving and merciful; He does not hasten the punishment, though it has an appointed time.
quran.arabic: وَرَبُّكَ الْغَفُورُ ذُو الرَّحْمَةِ ۖ لَوْ يُؤَاخِذُهُم بِمَا كَسَبُوا لَعَجَّلَ لَهُمُ الْعَذَابَ ۚ بَل لَّهُم مَّوْعِدٌ لَّن يَجِدُوا مِن دُونِهِ مَوْئِلًا
quran.translation: And your Lord is the Forgiving, the possessor of mercy. If He were to impose blame upon them for what they earned, He would have hastened for them the punishment. Rather, for them is an appointment from which they will never find an escape.

hadith.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: "No one, or nothing, is more patient over hurtful words he hears than Allah. They claim that He has a son, yet He still gives them well-being and provides for them."
The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer, but when He seizes him, He does not let him escape." Then he recited 11:102.

scholars.text: As-Sabur is the One who does not hasten to punish the disobedient; rather He delays it to an appointed term and gives them respite until a known time.
scholars.book: Sha'n ad-Du'a, p. 98, quoted in IslamQA 191329

scholars.text: He is the Most Patient over the hurt of His enemies: they reviled Him, and even spoke slander about Him.
Rather, whether as-Sabur is counted among the Beautiful Names remains a matter of scholarly reasoning and judgement.

notes: Being "hurt" by words here does not mean that anyone can harm Allah: He says that His servants can never reach the point of harming Him (Muslim 2577). It refers to the offensive things they say about Him.

Allah's patience is unlike the patience of His creation. He is able to take people to account at once, yet He delays them to an appointed term (35:45), and when He seizes the wrongdoer, he cannot escape (Bukhari 4686).

lessons.text: Do not take Allah's respite as a sign that He is pleased; repent before the appointed term comes.
Be patient when people hurt you with words; al-Bukhari placed this hadith in his chapter on patience in the face of harm.
Ask Allah for patience and strive for it: whoever strives to be patient, Allah gives him patience, and no gift is better or more vast than patience.

dua.text: O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I keep Your covenant and Your promise as much as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favour upon me and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for no one forgives sins except You.
